metadata.section: 3. Designated Persons and immediate relatives of designated persons in the organisation
3. Designated Persons and immediate relatives of designated persons in the organisation

__data__.text:
3. Designated Persons and immediate relatives of designated persons in the organisation
shall be governed by an internal code of conduct governing dealings in units of the mutual
fund. 4. (1)Designated persons may deal in the units of the mutual fund subject to compliance
with these regulations. The compliance officer of the asset management company shall
determine the closure period during which a Designated Person or class of Designated
Persons can reasonably be expected to have possession of unpublished price sensitive
information. Such closure period shall be imposed in relation to such schemes to which
such unpublished price sensitive information relates. During such time, any requests to
transact in the units of the mutual funds by the Designated Persons and/or their
immediate relatives shall not be processed by the asset management company. (2) The closure period restrictions mentioned in sub-clause (1) shall not apply in respect
of transactions specified in clauses (i) to (iii) of the proviso to sub-regulation (1) of
regulation 5D and in respect to the pledge of mutual fund units for a bonafide purpose,
subject to pre-clearance by the compliance officer and compliance with the other
requirements, if any, as may be specified by the Board. 5. The timing for re-opening of the closure period shall be determined by the compliance
officer taking into account various factors including the unpublished price sensitive
information in question becoming generally available and being capable of assimilation by
the market. 6. When the closure period is not applicable, trading in the mutual fund units by
Designated Persons and their immediate relatives including at the time of initiation of
systematic transactions shall be subject to pre-clearance by the compliance officer, if the
value of the proposed trades is above such thresholds (separate thresholds for systematic
transactions and lumpsum payments) as the Board of AMCs may stipulate:

Provided that for transactions in units by the Designated Persons pursuant to the mandatory
requirement under ‘Alignment of interest of Key Employees (‘Designated Employees’) of
asset management companies with the unit holders of the mutual fund schemes’ or
otherwise shall be as specified by the Board in this regard:
Provided further that the requirement of pre-clearance of trades by Designated Persons
shall not apply for trading in Overnight Schemes, Index funds and Exchange Traded
Funds. 7. Prior to approving any trades, the compliance officer shall be entitled to seek a
declaration to the effect that the applicant for pre-clearance is not in possession of any
unpublished price sensitive information with due regard to whether any such declaration is
reasonably capable of being rendered inaccurate. 8. The code of conduct formulated by the chief executive officer or managing director of
the asset management company shall specify any reasonable timeframe, which in any event
shall not be more than seven business days, within which trades that have been pre-cleared
have to be executed by the Designated Person, failing which fresh pre-clearance shall be
required for the trades to be executed. 9. The code of conduct shall also specify the period, which in any event shall not be less
than two months, within which a Designated Person who is permitted to trade shall not
execute a contra trade. The compliance officer may be empowered to grant relaxation from
the strict application of such restriction for reasons to be recorded in writing provided that
such relaxation does not violate these regulations or other requirements specified by the
Board. In case a contra trade is executed, inadvertently or otherwise, in violation of such a
restriction, the profits or loss avoided from such trade shall be liable to be disgorged by the
asset management company and credited under intimation to the Board, to the Investor
Protection and Education Fund established by the Board under the Act:
Provided that trading restrictions imposed for contra trade shall not be applicable for
Overnight Schemes.

including wage freeze, suspension, recovery, etc., that may be imposed by the asset
management company for the contravention of the code of conduct. Any amount collected
under this clause shall be disgorged by the asset management company and credited under
intimation to the Board, to the Investor Protection and Education Fund established by the
Board under the Act. 12. The code of conduct shall specify that in case it is observed by the asset management
company that there has been a violation of these regulations, it shall promptly inform to the

time to time. 13. Designated Persons shall be required to disclose names and Permanent Account

by designated persons shall be subject to pre- clearance by the compliance officer(s), if the value

CHAPTER -II
SUBSTANTIAL ACQUISITION OF SHARES, VOTING RIGHTS OR CONTROL
Substantial acquisition of shares or voting rights. 3. (1) No acquirer shall acquire shares or voting rights in a target company which taken
together with shares or voting rights, if any, held by him and by persons acting in
concert with him in such target company, entitle them to exercise twenty-five per
cent or more of the voting rights in such target company unless the acquirer makes
a public announcement of an open offer for acquiring shares of such target
company in accordance with these regulations. (2) No acquirer, who together with persons acting in concert with him, has acquired
and holds in accordance with these regulations shares or voting rights in a target
company entitling them to exercise twenty-five per cent or more of the voting
rights in the target company but less than the maximum permissible non-public
shareholding, shall acquire within any financial year additional shares or voting
rights in such target company entitling them to exercise more than five per cent of
the voting rights, unless the acquirer makes a public announcement of an open
offer for acquiring shares of such target company in accordance with these
regulations:
15[Provided that the acquisition beyond five per cent but upto ten per cent of
the voting rights in the target company shall be permitted for the financial year
2020-21 only in respect of acquisition by a promoter pursuant to preferential issue
of equity shares by the target company.] Provided that such acquirer shall not be entitled to acquire or enter into any
agreement to acquire shares or voting rights exceeding such number of shares as
would take the aggregate shareholding pursuant to the acquisition above the
maximum permissible non-public shareholding. 16[Provided further that, acquisition pursuant to a resolution plan approved under
section 31 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 [No. 31 of 2016] shall
15 Inserted by the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2020,
w.e.f. 16-06-2020.

no acquirer shall acquire, directly or indirectly, control over such target company
unless the acquirer makes a public announcement of an open offer for acquiring
shares of such target company in accordance with these regulations. Indirect acquisition of shares or control. 5. (1) For the purposes of regulation 3 and regulation 4, acquisition of shares or voting

the consolidated sales turnover of the entity or business being acquired; or
(c) the proportionate market capitalisation of the target company as a
percentage of the enterprise value for the entity or business being acquired;

financial statements, such indirect acquisition shall be regarded as a direct
acquisition of the target company for all purposes of these regulations including
without limitation, the obligations relating to timing, pricing and other
compliance requirements for the open offer. Explanation.— For the purposes of computing the percentage referred to in clause

taken into account on the basis of the volume-weighted average market price of
such shares on the stock exchange for a period of sixty trading days preceding the

This document is an Extraordinary publication in THE GAZETTE OF INDIA, Part III - Section 4, published by authority in New Delhi on September 11, 2018. It contains a NOTIFICATION from the SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA (SEBI), issued from Mumbai on the same date, regarding the SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA (ISSUE OF CAPITAL AND DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS) REGULATIONS, 2018.

These regulations, numbered No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2018/31, are made by the Board under the powers conferred by section 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992.

**CHAPTER I - PRELIMINARY** outlines the short title and commencement, and definitions:

1.  **Short title and commencement:**
    *   The regulations are called the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018.
    *   They come into force on the sixtieth day from their publication in the Official Gazette.

2.  **Definitions:** Unless the context requires otherwise, key terms are defined:
    *   **Act:** Refers to the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992.
    *   **Advertisement:** Includes notices, brochures, pamphlets, show cards, catalogues, hoardings, placards, posters, newspaper insertions, pictures, and films in any print or electronic media, radio, or television programs.
    *   **Anchor investor:** A qualified institutional buyer applying for at least ten crore rupees in a main board public issue via book building, or at least two crore rupees for an issue under Chapter IX.
    *   **Application supported by blocked amount (ASBA):** An application for a public or rights issue with authorization to a self-certified syndicate bank to block the application money in a bank account.
    *   **Associate:** A person or entity that is an associate under sub-section (6) of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013, or under applicable accounting standards.
    *   **Board:** The Securities and Exchange Board of India.
    *   **Book building:** A process to elicit demand and assess the price for specified securities or Indian Depository Receipts.
    *   **Composite issue:** An issue of specified securities by a listed issuer on a public-cum-rights basis, with simultaneous allotment in both public and rights issues.
    *   **Control:** Has the same meaning as in the SEBI (Substantial Acquisitions of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.
    *   **Convertible debt instrument:** An instrument creating or acknowledging indebtedness, convertible into equity shares of the issuer later, with or without the holder's option, and whether or not constituting a charge on assets.
    *   **Convertible security:** A security convertible into or exchangeable with equity shares of the issuer later, with or without the holder's option, including convertible debt instruments and convertible preference shares.
    *   **Designated stock exchange:** A recognized stock exchange with nationwide trading terminals chosen by the issuer for listing securities for a particular issue, with the option to choose a different one for subsequent issues.
    *   **Draft letter of offer:** The draft letter of offer filed with the stock exchange(s) for a rights issue.
    *   **Draft offer document:** The draft offer document filed with the Board for a public issue.
    *   **Employee:** A permanent employee (working in or outside India) of the issuer, its promoters, or subsidiary, or a director (whole-time or not) of the issuer. It excludes promoters, promoter group members, or directors holding more than ten percent of outstanding equity shares (directly or indirectly). For stock option schemes, it refers to the definition in the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021.
    *   **Financial year:** Has the same meaning as assigned under sub-section (41) of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013.
    *   **Fugitive economic offender:** An individual declared as such under section 12 of the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018.
    *   **Further public offer:** An offer of specified securities by a listed issuer to the public for subscription, including an offer for sale by existing holders.
    *   **General corporate purposes:** Identified purposes for which no specific amount is allocated, or any specified amount, or any such purpose in the draft offer document, draft letter of offer, offer document, or letter of offer. Issue-related expenses are not considered part of this if no specific amount is allocated.
    *   **Green shoe option:** An option to allot equity shares in excess of those offered in a public issue as a post-listing price stabilizing mechanism.
    *   **Group companies:** Companies (excluding promoters and subsidiaries) with related party transactions during the disclosed financial period, as per applicable accounting standards, and other companies deemed material by the issuer's board.
    *   **Housing finance company:** A deposit-taking housing finance company registered with the National Housing Bank.
    *   **Infrastructure sector:** Includes transportation (roads, rail, ports, aviation, logistics), agriculture (storage, agro-processing, preservation), and water management.

This document outlines various definitions related to capital markets and infrastructure, as per the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, including subsequent amendments.

**I. Infrastructure Sector Activities (A-xi):**
The text lists numerous activities and services considered part of the infrastructure sector:
*   **Water:** Supply, distribution, irrigation, and treatment.
*   **Telecommunication:** Basic or cellular (including radio paging), domestic satellite service (owned/operated by an Indian company for telecommunication), and networks for trunking, broadband, and internet services.
*   **Industrial, Commercial, and Social Development & Maintenance:** Real estate development (including industrial parks or special economic zones), tourism (hotels, convention/entertainment centres), public markets and buildings, trade fair/convention/exhibition/cultural centres, sports and recreation infrastructure, public gardens and parks, construction of educational institutions and hospitals, and other urban development (solid waste management, sanitation, sewerage systems).
*   **Power:** Generation (thermal, hydro, nuclear, fossil fuel, wind, and other renewable sources), and transmission, distribution, or trading of power by laying new lines.
*   **Petroleum and Natural Gas:** Exploration and production, import terminals, liquefaction and re-gasification, storage terminals, and transmission/distribution networks (including city gas infrastructure).
*   **Housing:** Urban and rural housing (public/mass housing, slum rehabilitation), and allied activities like drainage, lighting, road laying, and sanitation facilities.
*   **Services:** Provided by recognised stock exchanges and registered depositories, in relation to securities.
*   **Other Miscellaneous Facilities or Services:** Mining and related activities, technology-related infrastructure, manufacturing of components/materials/utilities for the infrastructure sector (e.g., energy saving/metering devices), environment-related infrastructure, disaster management services, preservation of monuments and icons, and emergency services (medical, police, fire, rescue).
*   **Board Discretion:** Any other facility or service deemed infrastructure sector by the board.

**II. Key Definitions (w-pp):**
*   **(w) Initial Public Offer (IPO):** An offer of specified securities by an unlisted issuer to the public for subscription, including an offer for sale of specified securities by existing holders in an unlisted issuer.
*   **(x) Innovators Growth Platform:** A trading platform for listing and trading specified securities of issuers that meet eligibility criteria in regulation 283.
*   **(y) Institutional Investor:** Either a qualified institutional buyer (QIB) or a family trust/intermediary registered with the Board having a net worth exceeding five hundred crore rupees (as per last audited financial statements), for listing/trading on the innovators growth platform.
*   **(z) Issue Size:** Includes the offer through the offer document and promoters' contribution brought in as part of the issue.
*   **(aa) Issuer:** A company or body corporate authorized to issue specified securities under relevant laws, whose securities are being issued or offered for sale according to these regulations.
*   **(bb) Key Managerial Personnel (KMP):** Defined as per sub-section (51) of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013.
*   **(cc) Lead Manager:** A merchant banker registered with the Board, appointed by the issuer to manage the issue. For book-built issues, they act as book running lead manager(s).
*   **(dd) Listed Issuer:** An issuer whose equity shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange with nationwide trading terminals.
*   **(ee) Main Board:** A recognised stock exchange with nationwide trading terminals, excluding an SME exchange.
*   **(ff) Net Offer:** An offer of specified securities to the public, excluding reservations and promoters' contribution.
*   **(gg) Net Tangible Assets:** The sum of all net assets of the issuer, excluding intangible assets as defined in Accounting Standard 26 (AS 26) or Indian Accounting Standard (Ind AS) 38.
*   **(hh) Net Worth:** The aggregate value of paid-up share capital, reserves (from profits, securities premium), and profit and loss account balance (debit or credit), after deducting accumulated losses, deferred expenditure, and miscellaneous expenditure not written off, as per the audited balance sheet. It excludes reserves from revaluation of assets, write-back of depreciation, and amalgamation.
*   **(ii) Nominated Investor:** A qualified institutional buyer or a private equity fund (registered with a regulatory authority or established by a person registered with a regulatory authority) who agrees with the lead manager(s) to subscribe to an issue (Chapter IX) in case of under-subscription, or to receive/deliver specified securities in the market-making process for such an issue.
*   **(jj) Non-Institutional Investor:** An investor other than a retail individual investor and a qualified institutional buyer.
*   **(kk) Offer Document:** For a public issue, it means a red herring prospectus, prospectus, or shelf prospectus as per the Companies Act, 2013; for a rights issue, it means a letter of offer.
*   **(ll) Offer Through Offer Document:** Comprises the net offer and reservations.
*   **(mm) Persons Acting in Concert:** Has the same meaning as assigned under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.
*   **(nn) Preferential Issue:** An issue of specified securities by a listed issuer to a select person or group of persons on a private placement basis (Chapter V). It excludes offers made through employee stock option schemes, employee stock purchase schemes, issues of sweat equity shares, or depository receipts/foreign securities issued outside India.
*   **(oo) Promoter:** Includes a person:
    *   Named as such in a draft offer document or offer document, or identified in the annual return (section 92 of Companies Act, 2013).
    *   Who has direct or indirect control over the issuer's affairs (as a shareholder, director, or otherwise).
    *   In accordance with whose advice, directions, or instructions the issuer's board of directors is accustomed to act (excluding those acting in a professional capacity).
    *   *Proviso:* Certain entities (financial institutions, scheduled commercial banks, foreign portfolio investors other than individuals/corporate bodies/family offices, mutual funds, venture capital funds, alternative investment funds, foreign venture capital investors, insurance companies, or other Board-specified categories) are not deemed promoters merely by holding 20% or more of the issuer's equity share capital, unless they satisfy other regulatory requirements.
*   **(pp) Promoter Group:** Includes:
    *   The promoter.
    *   An immediate relative of the promoter (spouse, parent, brother, sister, or child of the person or spouse).
    *   If the promoter is a body corporate: its subsidiary or holding company; any body corporate where the promoter holds 20% or more of the equity share capital; and/or any body corporate which holds 20% or more of the equity share capital of the promoter.
    *   If the promoter is an individual: any body corporate where 20% or more of the equity share capital is held by the promoter, an immediate relative, or a firm/Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) in which the promoter or any relative is a member; any body corporate in which such a body corporate (as described above) holds 20% or more of the equity share capital; and any HUF or firm where the aggregate share of the promoter and their relatives is 20% or more of the total capital.
    *   All persons whose shareholding is aggregated under the "shareholding of the promoter group" heading.
    *   *Proviso:* Similar to the promoter definition, certain entities (financial institutions, scheduled banks, foreign portfolio investors other than individuals/corporate bodies/family offices, mutual funds, venture capital funds, alternative investment funds, foreign venture capital investors, insurance companies, or other Board-specified categories) are not deemed part of the promoter group merely by holding 20% or more of the equity share capital of the promoter or entity, unless they satisfy other regulatory requirements.

This document provides definitions for various terms and outlines the applicability of regulations.

**Prior Omission:**
A clause defining "C) any body corporate" was omitted. This clause described a body corporate where a group of individuals, companies, or combinations thereof, acting in concert, held twenty percent or more of the equity share capital in that body corporate, and the same group also held twenty percent or more of the equity share capital of the issuer and were acting in concert.

**Definitions:**

*   **Promoter Group:** Includes mutual funds, venture capital funds, alternative investment funds, foreign venture capital investors, and insurance companies (registered with IRDAI), or other Board-specified categories. These are treated as promoter groups for subsidiaries or companies promoted by them, or for mutual funds sponsored by them.
*   **Public Financial Institution:** Defined as per the Companies Act, 2013.
*   **Public Issue:** Means an initial public offer or a further public offer.
*   **Qualified Institutional Buyer (QIB):** Includes:
    *   Mutual funds, venture capital funds, alternative investment funds, and foreign venture capital investors registered with the Board.
    *   Foreign portfolio investors (FPI) *other than* individuals, corporate bodies, and family offices (substituted w.e.f. 23.09.2019; previously "foreign portfolio investor other than Category III foreign portfolio investor, registered with the Board").
    *   Public financial institutions.
    *   Scheduled commercial banks.
    *   Multilateral and bilateral development financial institutions.
    *   State industrial development corporations.
    *   Insurance companies registered with IRDAI.
    *   Provident funds with a minimum corpus of twenty-five crore rupees.
    *   Pension funds with a minimum corpus of twenty-five crore rupees, registered with the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (inserted w.e.f. 23.5.2023).
    *   National Investment Fund (set up by GoI resolution dated November 23, 2005).
    *   Insurance funds set up and managed by the army, navy, or air force of the Union of India.
    *   Insurance funds set up and managed by the Department of Posts, India.
    *   Systemically important non-banking financial companies.
*   **Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP):** An issue of eligible securities by a listed issuer to QIBs on a private placement basis, including an offer for sale of specified securities by promoters and/or promoter group on a private placement basis.
*   **Relative:** Defined as per the Companies Act, 2013.
*   **Retail Individual Investor (RII):** An individual investor applying or bidding for specified securities for a value of not more than two lakhs rupees.
*   **Retail Individual Shareholder (RIS):** A shareholder applying or bidding for specified securities for a value of not more than two lakhs rupees.
*   **Rights Issue:** An offer of specified securities by a listed issuer to its shareholders as on the record date.
*   **Schedule:** Refers to a schedule annexed to these regulations.
*   **Scheduled Commercial Bank:** Banks included in the second schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
*   **Self-Certified Syndicate Bank (SCSB):** A banker to an issue registered with the Board, offering the ASBA facility.
*   **Selling Shareholder(s):** Any shareholder of the issuer offering specified securities for sale in a public issue.
*   **Senior Management:** (Inserted w.e.f. 31.01.2023) Officers and personnel of the issuer's core management team, excluding the Board of Directors. It comprises all management members one level below the Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, Whole Time Director, or Manager (including CEO and Manager if not on the Board), and specifically includes functional heads, the Company Secretary, and the Chief Financial Officer.
*   **Securities Laws:** Includes the Act, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, the Depositories Act, 1996, and rules/regulations/orders/guidelines/circulars thereunder, as well as provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 (or previous company law) and subordinate legislation administered by the Board.
*   **SME Exchange:** A trading platform of a recognised stock exchange with nationwide trading terminals permitted by the Board to list specified securities (under Chapter IX), including stock exchanges granted recognition for this purpose, but *excluding* the Main Board.
*   **Specified Securities:** Equity shares and convertible securities.
*   **SR Equity Shares:** (Inserted w.e.f. 29.07.2019) Equity shares of an issuer having superior voting rights compared to all other equity shares issued by that issuer.
*   **Stabilising Agent:** A merchant banker responsible for stabilising the price of equity shares under a green shoe option.
*   **Stock Exchange:** Any recognised stock exchange with nationwide trading terminals chosen by the issuer for a particular issue, *other than an SME exchange*.
*   **Syndicate Member:** An intermediary registered with the Board, permitted to accept bids, applications, place orders, and carry on underwriting activity.
*   **Systemically Important Non-Banking Financial Companies:** Non-banking financial companies registered with and recognised as systemically important by the Reserve Bank of India.
*   **Unlisted Issuer:** An issuer which is not a listed issuer.
*   **Valuer:** A person registered under section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013 and relevant rules, or as specified by the Board.
*   **Wilful Defaulter or a Fraudulent Borrower:** (Substituted w.e.f. 14.1.2022; previously "wilful defaulter") A person or issuer categorized as such by any bank or financial institution (or consortium thereof) in accordance with RBI guidelines.
*   **Working Day:**
    *   Generally: All days on which commercial banks in the specified city are open for business.
    *   For announcement of price band and bid/issue period: All days, *excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays*, on which commercial banks in the notified city are open for business.
    *   For the time period between bid/issue closing date and listing: All *trading days of the stock exchanges, excluding Sundays and bank holidays*, as per Board circulars.

**Undefined Words and Expressions:**
Any words or expressions used but not defined in these regulations, but defined in the Act, Companies Act, 2013, Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, or Depositories Act, 1996, or rules/regulations thereunder, shall have the same meaning as assigned to them in those statutes or rules/regulations.

**Applicability of the Regulations:**
Unless otherwise provided, these regulations apply to:
*   An initial public offer by an unlisted issuer.
*   A rights issue by a listed issuer (the clause "where the aggregate value of the issue is fifty crore rupees or more;" was omitted w.e.f. 08.04.2025).
*   A further public offer by a listed issuer.
*   A preferential issue by a listed issuer.
*   A qualified institutions placement by a listed issuer.
*   An initial public offer of Indian depository receipts.
*   A rights issue of Indian depository receipts.
*   An initial public offer by a small and medium enterprise.
*   A listing on the *innovators growth platform* (substituted w.e.f. 05.04.2019; previously "institutional trading platform") through an issue or without an issue.
*   A bonus issue by a listed issuer.

The provided text outlines regulations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, pertaining to Initial Public Offers (IPOs) on the Main Board. These regulations generally do not apply to certain issues of securities under clauses (b), (d), and (e) of sub-regulation (1) of regulation 9 of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.

For an IPO, an issuer must satisfy the specified conditions as on the date of "filing" (substituted for "registering" w.e.f. 01.01.2020) the draft offer document with the Board and the offer document with the Registrar of Companies.

**Entities Not Eligible to Make an Initial Public Offer (Regulation 5):**
An issuer is ineligible if:
*   The issuer, its promoters, promoter group, directors, or selling shareholders are debarred from accessing the capital market by the Board. This restriction does not apply if the debarment period is already over.
*   Any of its promoters or directors is a promoter or director of another company debarred by the Board. This restriction also does not apply if the debarment period is over.
*   The issuer or any of its promoters or directors is a "wilful defaulter or a fraudulent borrower" (substituted w.e.f. 14.01.2022 from "wilful defaulter").
*   Any of its promoters or directors is a fugitive economic offender.
*   There are any outstanding convertible securities or other rights entitling a person to receive equity shares, with specific exceptions:
    *   Outstanding employee stock options compliant with the Companies Act, 2013.
    *   Outstanding stock appreciation rights granted to employees, fully exercised for equity shares prior to the filing of the red herring prospectus or prospectus, with disclosures made (inserted w.e.f. 08.03.2025).
    *   Fully paid-up outstanding convertible securities required to be converted on or before the filing date of the red herring prospectus or prospectus.

**Eligibility Requirements for an Initial Public Offer (Regulation 6):**
An issuer is eligible if it meets the following criteria, calculated on a restated and consolidated basis:
*   **Net Tangible Assets:** At least three crore rupees in each of the preceding three full years, with not more than fifty per cent held in monetary assets. This fifty per cent limit on monetary assets is not applicable if the IPO is made entirely through an offer for sale, or if the issuer has utilized or made firm commitments to utilize such excess monetary assets in its business or project.
*   **Average Operating Profit:** At least fifteen crore rupees during the preceding three years, with operating profit in each of these three years.
*   **Net Worth:** At least one crore rupees in each of the preceding three full years.
*   **Name Change:** If the name was changed within the last one year, at least fifty per cent of the revenue for the preceding full year must have been earned from the activity indicated by its new name.

If an issuer does not satisfy the above conditions, it may still be eligible if the issue is made through the book-building process, and the issuer undertakes to allot at least seventy-five per cent of the net offer to qualified institutional buyers, refunding the full subscription money if it fails to do so.

**Special Conditions for Issuers with SR Equity Shares (Regulation 6(3)):**
An issuer that has issued SR (Superior Rights) equity shares to its promoters/founders is allowed to do an IPO of only ordinary shares for listing on the Main Board, provided:
*   The issuer is intensive in the use of technology, information technology, intellectual property, data analytics, bio-technology, or nano-technology to provide products, services, or business platforms with substantial value addition.
*   The net worth of the SR shareholder, as determined by a Registered Valuer, is not more than rupees one thousand crore (substituted w.e.f. 26.10.2021; previously, the collective net worth of the promoter group was not to exceed rupees 500 crores). The current explanation clarifies that while determining individual net worth, investment/shareholding in other listed companies is considered, but not in the issuer company.
*   The SR shares were issued only to promoters/founders holding an executive position in the issuer company.
*   The issue of SR equity shares was authorized by a special resolution passed at a general meeting, with the notice specifically detailing the size of the issue and the ratio of voting rights of SR equity shares vis-à-vis ordinary shares.

**Other Noted Amendments:**
*   Regulation 23 was substituted w.e.f. 05.04.2019, changing its prior reading of "institutional trading platform".
*   Regulation 24, including a proviso regarding rights issues of size less than fifty crores rupees, was omitted w.e.f. 08.04.2025.

This document outlines regulations concerning superior voting rights (SR) equity shares, general conditions for initial public offers (IPOs), additional conditions for offers for sale, and requirements for convertible debt instruments.

**SR Equity Shares:**
SR equity shares must specify rights regarding differential dividends, sunset provisions for their validity, and matters where they have the same voting rights as ordinary shares. They must be issued prior to the filing of the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) and held for at least three months before the red herring prospectus (RHP) filing (this was updated from a prior requirement of six months). These shares must have voting rights in a ratio of a minimum of 2:1 up to a maximum of 10:1 compared to ordinary shares, in whole numbers. They must have the same face value as ordinary shares, and an issuer can only have one class of SR equity shares. Except for superior voting rights, SR equity shares are equivalent to ordinary equity shares in all other respects.

**General Conditions for Initial Public Offers (Regulation 7):**
An issuer making an IPO must:
*   Apply for in-principle listing approval to one or more stock exchanges and designate one.
*   Enter into an agreement with a depository for dematerialization of existing and proposed securities.
*   Ensure all promoter-held specified securities are in dematerialized form before filing the offer document.
*   Have all existing partly paid-up equity shares either fully paid-up or forfeited.
*   Make firm arrangements for 75% of the stated means of finance for a specific project, excluding the amount from the public issue or existing internal accruals.
The amount for general corporate purposes, as stated in the offer documents, initially could not exceed 25% of the amount raised. This was later amended: the combined amount for general corporate purposes and objects where the issuer has not identified an acquisition or investment target shall not exceed 35% of the amount raised, with the latter specifically not exceeding 25%. These limits do not apply if the proposed acquisition or strategic investment target is identified and specific disclosures are made.
*   **Explanations for Regulations 6 and 7:** A "project" is the object for which monies are raised. The track record of operating profit for a partnership firm or limited liability partnership (LLP) is considered if its financial statements conform to the Companies Act, 2013 format, include adequate disclosures (Schedule III), and are certified by a statutory auditor confirming compliance with Schedule III, applicable accounting standards, and a true and fair view. Similar conditions apply to the track record of distributable profits for a division spun-off from an existing company.

**Additional Conditions for an Offer for Sale (Regulation 8):**
Only fully paid-up equity shares held by sellers for at least one year prior to the DRHP filing can be offered for sale. If shares are received from the conversion or exchange of fully paid-up compulsorily convertible securities (including depository receipts), the combined holding period of both the convertible securities and the resultant equity shares is considered. This one-year holding period must be met at the time of DRHP filing. The conversion or exchange of such securities must be completed before the offer document filing (RHP or prospectus), with full disclosures in the DRHP.
*   **Exceptions to the one-year holding period:**
    *   Offer for sale by a government company, statutory authority, corporation, or special purpose vehicle (SPV) in the infrastructure sector.
    *   Equity shares acquired pursuant to a scheme approved by a High Court, tribunal, or the Central Government (under sections 230-234 of the Companies Act, 2013) in lieu of business and invested capital existing for over one year prior to scheme approval.
    *   Equity shares issued under a bonus issue on securities held for at least one year prior to DRHP filing, provided they are issued from free reserves and share premium (not revaluation reserves or unrealized profits).

**Additional Conditions for an Offer for Sale for Issues under Regulation 6(2) (Regulation 8A):**
For issues where the DRHP is filed under sub-regulation (2) of regulation 6:
*   Shareholders holding, individually or with persons acting in concert, more than 20% of the pre-issue shareholding (fully diluted) can offer for sale a maximum of 50% of their pre-issue shareholding.
*   Shareholders holding less than 20% of the pre-issue shareholding (fully diluted) can offer for sale a maximum of 10% of the pre-issue shareholding.
*   For shareholders holding more than 20% of the pre-issue shareholding, lock-in provisions under regulation 17 apply, and the relaxation from lock-in under clause (c) of regulation 17 does not apply.
These limits are calculated based on the shareholding as of the DRHP filing date and apply cumulatively to the total shares offered for sale and any prior secondary sale transactions.

**Eligibility and Additional Requirements for Convertible Debt Instruments (Regulations 9 & 10):**
An issuer is eligible to make an IPO of convertible debt instruments without a prior public issue of its equity shares and listing, provided it is not in default of payment of interest or principal amount on any public debt instruments for more than six months.
*   **Additional requirements:** The issuer must obtain a credit rating from at least one agency, appoint at least one debenture trustee, and create a debenture redemption reserve.
*   **For secured convertible debt instruments:** Assets must be sufficient to discharge the principal, be free from encumbrance, and if security already exists or is on leasehold land, consent for a second or pari passu charge must be obtained and submitted to the debenture trustee before the issue opens. The security or asset cover is calculated after reducing liabilities with a first or prior charge. The issuer must redeem the instruments as per the offer document.

**Conversion of Optionally Convertible Debt Instruments into Equity Shares (Regulation 11):**
The issuer cannot convert optionally convertible debt instruments into equity shares without the positive consent of the holders; non-receipt of a reply is not considered consent. If the value of the convertible portion of listed optionally convertible debt instruments exceeds ₹10 crore and the conversion price was not determined at the time of issue, holders must be given the option not to convert. This option is not necessary if an upper limit on the price and its justification were determined and disclosed at the time of issue. If holders do not exercise the option to convert, the issuer must redeem that part of the instruments within one month at a price not less than its face value, unless such redemption is already disclosed in the offer document.

**Issue of Convertible Debt Instruments for Financing (Regulation 12):**
An issuer cannot issue convertible debt instruments for financing, providing loans to, or acquiring shares of any person who is part of the promoter group or group companies. However, fully convertible debt instruments can be issued for these purposes if their conversion period is less than eighteen months from the date of issue.

This document outlines regulations for issuing warrants and promoters' contributions in an initial public offer (IPO).

**Issue of Warrants (Section 13):**
An issuer can issue warrants in an IPO if:
*   Their tenure does not exceed eighteen months from allotment.
*   A specified security can have one or more warrants attached.
*   The exercise price or its formula must be determined upfront and disclosed in the offer document.
*   At least twenty-five percent of the consideration, based on the exercise price (or cap price if a formula is used), must be received upfront.
*   If a warrant holder fails to exercise the option for equity shares within three months of consideration payment, the consideration for those warrants will be forfeited by the issuer.

**Minimum Promoters’ Contribution (Section 14):**
*   **Requirement:** Promoters must hold at least twenty percent of the post-issue capital.
*   **Shortfall Contribution:** If promoters' post-issue shareholding is less than twenty percent, alternative investment funds, foreign venture capital investors, scheduled commercial banks, public financial institutions, insurance companies, non-individual public shareholders holding at least five percent of post-issue capital, or promoter group entities (other than promoters) may contribute up to ten percent of the post-issue capital to meet the shortfall, without being identified as promoters.
*   **Exemption:** This requirement does not apply if an issuer has no identifiable promoter.
*   **Form of Contribution:** Promoters' contribution can be in equity shares (including SR equity shares) or convertible securities.
    *   If the conversion price of convertible securities is not predetermined and disclosed, promoters must contribute only via subscription to public issue convertible securities and undertake to subscribe to equity shares upon conversion.
    *   For convertible securities with varying conversion dates, if contribution is via equity shares (with predetermined conversion price), the price must not be lower than the weighted average price of equity shares arising from conversion.
    *   For an IPO of convertible debt instruments without a prior equity IPO, promoters must contribute at least twenty percent of the project cost in equity shares, and at least twenty percent of the issue size from their own funds in equity shares.
*   **Timing:** Promoters must satisfy these requirements at least one day prior to the issue opening date.
*   **Escrow:** The amount for promoters' contribution must be kept in an escrow account with a scheduled commercial bank, released with issue proceeds. If funds are already utilized, a cash flow statement must be disclosed.
*   **Large Contribution:** If the minimum promoters' contribution exceeds ₹100 crore and the IPO is for partly paid shares, at least ₹100 crore must be brought in before the issue opening, with the remainder on a pro-rata basis before public calls.
*   **Computation:** Promoters' contribution is computed based on post-issue expanded capital, assuming full conversion of convertible securities and exercise of all vested employee stock options/stock appreciation rights. Weighted average price considers the number of equity shares from conversion at various stages and their respective conversion prices.

**Securities Ineligible for Minimum Promoters’ Contribution (Section 15):**
The following specified securities are generally ineligible for computing minimum promoters' contribution:
*   Acquired in the preceding three years for non-cash consideration involving revaluation of assets or capitalization of intangible assets.
*   Resulting from a bonus issue utilizing revaluation reserves or unrealized profits, or from a bonus issue against already ineligible equity shares.
*   Acquired by promoters or specified entities (AIFs, FVCI, banks, PFI, insurance, non-individual public shareholder >5%, promoter group entity) in the preceding one year at a price lower than the IPO price.
    *   **Exceptions to this rule:**
        *   If the difference between the IPO price and acquisition price is paid to the issuer.
        *   If acquired under sections 230-234 of the Companies Act, 2013, as approved by a High Court/tribunal/Central Government, in lieu of business and invested capital existing for over one year prior to approval.
        *   For IPOs by government companies, statutory authorities, corporations, or special purpose vehicles in the infrastructure sector.
        *   Equity shares from conversion/exchange of fully paid-up compulsorily convertible securities held by promoters/specified entities for at least one year prior to draft offer document filing, converted before offer document filing, with full disclosures.
    *   The price per share for determining ineligibility is adjusted for corporate actions like share splits or bonus issues.
*   Allotted to promoters or specified entities in the preceding one year at a price less than the issue price, against funds brought in, for issuers formed by converting partnership firms or LLPs (unless the capital existed in such firms for over one year continuously).
*   Specified securities pledged with any creditor.
*   However, securities from the first and third points (acquired for non-cash consideration or from partnership/LLP conversion) can be eligible if acquired pursuant to a scheme approved by a High Court, tribunal, or the Central Government under sections 230 to 234 of the Companies Act, 2013.

This document outlines the lock-in periods and restrictions on transferability for specified securities under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, incorporating various amendments up to March 8, 2025.

**Regulation 16: Lock-in of specified securities held by the promoters**

*   **Minimum Promoters' Contribution:**
    *   Specified securities held by promoters, including contributions from alternative investment funds, foreign venture capital investors, scheduled commercial banks, public financial institutions, IRDAI-registered insurance companies, any non-individual public shareholder holding at least five percent of the post-issue capital, or any entity (individual or non-individual) forming part of the promoter group (other than the promoter(s)), are locked-in for **eighteen months** from the date of allotment in the initial public offer.
    *   **Exception:** If the majority of the issue proceeds (excluding the offer for sale portion) are proposed to be utilized for capital expenditure, the lock-in period is **three years** from the date of allotment.
    *   **Capital Expenditure Definition:** Includes civil work, miscellaneous fixed assets, purchase of land, building, plant and machinery, and repayment of existing loan(s) taken for such capital expenditure.
*   **Promoters' Holding in Excess of Minimum Contribution:**
    *   This portion is locked-in for **six months** from the date of allotment in the initial public offer.
    *   **Exception:** If the majority of the issue proceeds (excluding the offer for sale portion) are proposed to be utilized for capital expenditure, the lock-in period is **one year** from the date of allotment.
*   **SR Equity Shares (Sub-regulation 16(2)):**
    *   SR equity shares are locked-in until their conversion into equity shares with ordinary voting rights or for the period specified in sub-regulation (1), whichever is later.

**Regulation 17: Lock-in of specified securities held by persons other than the promoters**

*   The entire pre-issue capital held by persons other than the promoters is locked-in for **six months** from the date of allotment in the initial public offer.
*   **Exemptions:**
    *   **a) Employee Shares:** Equity shares allotted to employees (current or not) under an employee stock option, employee stock purchase, or stock appreciation right scheme of the issuer prior to the initial public offer, provided full disclosures were made.
    *   **b) Employee Stock Option Trust Shares:** Equity shares held by an employee stock option trust or transferred to employees by such a trust pursuant to the exercise of options under an employee stock option plan, employee stock purchase scheme, or stock appreciation rights scheme. These shares are subject to the lock-in provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021.
    *   **c) Venture Capital/AIF/FVCI Shares:** Equity shares held by a venture capital fund, alternative investment fund of Category I or Category II, or a foreign venture capital investor. These shares are locked-in for at least **six months** from the date of purchase by the respective fund or investor.
*   **Explanations for clause (c):**
    *   (i) For equity shares resulting from the conversion of fully paid-up compulsorily convertible securities, the holding period of both the convertible securities and the resultant equity shares is combined for the six-month calculation. Convertible securities are considered fully paid-up if the entire consideration is paid and no further consideration is due at conversion.
    *   (ii) For equity shares resulting from a bonus issue, the holding period of the original equity shares and the bonus shares is combined for the six-month calculation, provided the bonus shares are issued from free reserves and share premium existing at the end of the financial year preceding the draft offer document filing, and not from revaluation reserves or unrealized profits.
*   **Explanation for clauses (a) and (b):**
    *   (iii) Equity shares include any bonus shares allotted against equity shares allotted under an employee stock option, employee stock purchase scheme, or a stock appreciation right scheme.

**Regulation 18: Lock-in of specified securities lent to stabilising agent under the green shoe option**

*   The lock-in provisions do not apply to specified securities lent to a stabilising agent for the purpose of the green shoe option, during the period starting from the date of lending.

The provided text outlines regulations concerning specified securities, including lock-in provisions, the appointment of intermediaries, and the disclosure and filing of offer documents.

**Lock-in of Specified Securities:**
*   **Partly Paid-up Securities (Regulation 19):** If locked-in specified securities are partly paid-up and the amount called-up is less than that on public securities, the lock-in period ends three years after these securities become pari passu with those issued to the public.
*   **Non-Transferability Inscription (Regulation 20):** Certificates for locked-in specified securities must bear the inscription "non-transferable" and specify the lock-in period. For dematerialized securities, the issuer must ensure the lock-in is recorded by the depository.
*   **Pledge of Locked-in Securities (Regulation 21):** Promoters' locked-in specified securities (excluding SR equity shares) can be pledged as collateral for loans from scheduled commercial banks, public financial institutions, systemically important non-banking finance companies, or housing finance companies.
    *   If locked-in under regulation 16(a), the loan must be granted to the issuer company or its subsidiary(ies) for financing the issue's objects, and the pledge must be a term of the loan sanction.
    *   If locked-in under regulation 16(b), the pledge must be a term of the loan sanction.
    *   Upon invocation of the pledge, the lock-in continues for the transferee, who cannot transfer the securities until the stipulated lock-in period expires.
*   **Transferability of Locked-in Securities (Regulation 22):**
    *   Promoters' locked-in specified securities (excluding SR equity shares) under regulation 16 may be transferred to another promoter, a person of the promoter group, or a new promoter.
    *   Specified securities locked-in under regulation 17 (for persons other than promoters) may be transferred to any other person holding locked-in specified securities.
    *   In all such transfers, the lock-in continues for the remaining period with the transferee, who is not eligible to transfer them until the lock-in period expires.

**Appointment of Lead Managers, Other Intermediaries, and Compliance Officer (Regulation 23):**
*   The issuer must appoint one or more SEBI-registered merchant bankers as lead manager(s).
*   If multiple lead managers are appointed, their rights, obligations, and responsibilities (e.g., disclosures, allotment, refund, underwriting) must be predetermined and disclosed in the draft and final offer documents.
*   At least one lead manager must not be an associate of the issuer; if an associate, its role is limited to marketing the issue, and its associate status must be disclosed.
*   The issuer, in consultation with the lead manager(s), appoints other SEBI-registered intermediaries after the lead manager(s) assess their capability.
*   The issuer enters into agreements with lead manager(s) (as per Schedule II) and other intermediaries (as per their respective regulations). These agreements can include additional clauses, provided they do not diminish liabilities. For the ASBA process, the issuer acknowledges a deemed agreement with self-certified syndicate banks.
*   The issuer appoints syndicate member(s) for book-building issues or bankers to issue for other issues.
*   A SEBI-registered registrar to the issue with connectivity to all depositories must be appointed. The issuer cannot appoint itself as registrar, nor can a lead manager act as registrar if also handling post-issue responsibilities.
*   A compliance officer, qualified as a company secretary, must be appointed to monitor securities law compliance and redress investor grievances.

**Disclosures in and Filing of Offer Documents (Regulations 24-25):**
*   **Disclosures (Regulation 24):**
    *   Draft and final offer documents must contain all material disclosures that are true and adequate for applicants to make informed investment decisions.
    *   Red-herring prospectuses and prospectuses must include disclosures specified in the Companies Act, 2013, and Part A of Schedule VI.
    *   Lead manager(s) must exercise due diligence on all aspects of the issue, including the veracity and adequacy of disclosures.
    *   Lead manager(s) must ensure the issuer, its promoters, directors, and selling shareholders (for an offer for sale) fulfill their disclosed obligations.
    *   Information in the draft offer document, offer document, and restated audited financial statements must not be more than six months old from the issue opening date.
*   **Filing (Regulation 25):**
    *   Before an initial public offer, the issuer files three copies of the draft offer document with the Board (SEBI) through the lead manager(s), along with fees (Schedule III) and as per Schedule IV.
    *   The lead manager(s) must submit a certificate confirming the agreement with the issuer and a due diligence certificate (Form A, Schedule V). For convertible debt instruments, a debenture trustee's due diligence certificate (Form B, Schedule V) is also required.
    *   The issuer also files the draft offer document with the stock exchange(s) where the securities are proposed to be listed, providing promoter details (PAN, bank account, passport for individuals; PAN, bank account, company registration number, and Registrar of Companies address for body corporates).
    *   The Board may specify changes or issue observations on the draft offer document within thirty days (from receipt of the draft, satisfactory reply to clarifications, information from other regulators, or in-principle approval from stock exchange).
    *   The issuer and lead manager(s) must implement the Board's changes, submit an updated draft highlighting these changes, before filing the offer documents with the Registrar of Companies.
    *   If there are changes related to matters specified in Schedule XVI, an updated or fresh draft offer document must be filed with the Board along with fees.
    *   Copies of the offer documents must be filed with the Board and the stock exchange(s) through the lead manager(s) promptly after filing with the Registrar of Companies.
    *   Both the draft and final offer documents must also be furnished to the Board in a soft copy.

The Board requires the draft offer document and the final offer document to be furnished in a soft copy.

After the Board issues observations or the stipulated period expires without observations, the lead manager(s) must submit several documents:
*   A statement certifying that all Board-made changes, suggestions, and observations have been incorporated into the offer document.
*   A due diligence certificate (Form C of Schedule V) at the time of filing the offer document.
*   A copy of the issuer's board of directors' resolution for allotting specified securities to promoter(s) against their contribution, to be submitted before the issue opens.
*   A certificate from a statutory auditor, before the issue opens, confirming that promoters' contribution was received per regulations, including names, addresses, and amounts paid/credited by each promoter to the issuer's bank account.
*   A due diligence certificate (Form D of Schedule V) if the issuer has disclosed any material development via public notice under Schedule IX, para 4.

**Public Availability of Offer Documents (Regulation 26):**
The draft offer document filed with the Board must be made public for comments for at least twenty-one days from the date of publication of the public announcement. It must be hosted on the websites of the issuer, the Board, stock exchanges where securities are to be listed, and the lead manager(s). Within two working days of filing the draft offer document, the issuer must make a public announcement in one English national daily, one Hindi national daily, and one regional language newspaper (at the registered office location), disclosing the filing and inviting public comments to the Board, issuer, or lead manager(s). After the comment period, the lead manager(s) must file details of received public comments and any consequential changes with the Board. The issuer and lead manager(s) must ensure that hosted offer documents match the versions filed with the Registrar of Companies, Board, and stock exchanges. Lead manager(s) and stock exchanges must provide copies of the offer document to the public upon request for a reasonable sum.

**Pricing (Part VII):**
**Face Value of Equity Shares (Regulation 27):** Disclosure of the face value of equity shares, along with the price band or issue price, must be made in identical font size in the draft offer document, offer document, advertisements, and application forms.

**Pricing (Regulation 28):** The issuer may determine the price of equity shares, and for convertible securities, the coupon rate and conversion price, in consultation with lead manager(s) or through the book building process (as specified in Schedule XIII).

**Price and Price Band (Regulation 29):**
The issuer may state a price or price band in the offer document (for fixed price issues) or a floor price or price band in the red herring prospectus (for book built issues), determining the final price later before filing the prospectus with the Registrar of Companies. The prospectus filed with the Registrar of Companies must contain only one price or specific coupon rate. The cap on the price band and coupon rate (for convertible debt instruments) must be less than or equal to one hundred and twenty percent of the floor price, and at least one hundred and five percent of the floor price. The floor price or final price must not be less than the face value of the specified securities. The issuer must announce the floor price or price band at least two working days before the issue opening in a pre-issue and price band advertisement, published in the same newspapers as the public announcement under Regulation 26(2). This announcement must include relevant financial ratios for both the upper and lower ends of the price band and draw investors' attention to the "basis of issue price" section of the offer document. The announcement and financial ratios must also be disclosed on stock exchange websites and pre-filled in application forms available on those websites.

**Differential Pricing (Regulation 30):**
The issuer may offer specified securities at different prices:
*   Retail individual investors, retail individual shareholders, or employees (entitled to reservation under Regulation 33) may be offered securities at a price not more than ten percent lower than the price offered to other categories of applicants (excluding anchor investors) in the net offer.
*   In a book built issue, the price for anchor investors must not be lower than the price offered to other applicants.
*   If the issuer uses the alternate book building method (Part D of Schedule XIII), employees may be offered securities at a price not more than ten percent lower than the floor price.
Any discount must be expressed in rupee terms in the offer document.

**Issuance Conditions and Procedure (Part VIII):**
**Minimum Offer to Public (Regulation 31):** The minimum offer to the public is subject to the provisions of clause (b) of sub-rule (2) of rule 19 of the Securities Contracts (Regulations) Rules, 1957.

**Allocation in the Net Offer (Regulation 32):** In a book building issue under Regulation 6(1), not less than thirty-five percent of the allocation in the net offer category must be made to retail individual investors.

The document outlines regulations for capital issue allocations and related processes.

For issues made through the book building process, the allocation in the net offer category is specified. In one scenario, not less than fifteen percent is allocated to non-institutional investors, and not more than fifty percent to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), with five percent of the QIB portion allocated to mutual funds. Mutual funds are also eligible for allocation under the balance available for QIBs. Unsubscribed portions in either the non-institutional or the QIB categories may be allocated to applicants in any other category.

In an issue made through the book building process under sub-regulation (2) of regulation 6, the allocation in the net offer category is: not more than ten percent to retail individual investors, not more than fifteen percent to non-institutional investors, and not less than seventy-five percent to QIBs, with five percent of this allocated to mutual funds. Mutual funds are also eligible for allocation under the balance available for QIBs. Unsubscribed portions in either the retail individual or non-institutional categories may be allocated to applicants in the other category.

In a book building process, the issuer may allocate up to sixty percent of the portion available for QIBs to anchor investors, subject to conditions in Schedule XIII.

For non-institutional investors in a book building process, effective from April 1, 2022 (or July 1, 2022, for public issues of ₹10,000 crore or more opening on or after April 1, 2022), one-third of their portion is reserved for applicants with application sizes between more than two lakh rupees and up to ten lakh rupees, and two-thirds for applicants with application sizes of more than ten lakh rupees. Unsubscribed portions in either of these sub-categories may be allocated to applicants in the other sub-category.

For issues made other than through the book building process, the net offer allocation is a minimum of fifty percent to retail individual investors (or a higher percentage if entitled proportionately). The remaining portion is allocated to individual applicants other than retail individual investors, and other investors including corporate bodies or institutions. Unsubscribed portions in these remaining categories may be allocated to applicants in the other category.

Issuers may make reservations on a competitive basis out of the issue size (excluding promoters’ contribution) for employees and shareholders (other than promoters and promoter group) of listed subsidiaries or listed promoter companies. However, no reservation is allowed for lead manager(s), registrar, syndicate member(s), their promoters, directors, employees, or their group or associate companies. Employee reservations cannot exceed five percent of the post-issue capital, with individual allotments not exceeding two lakh rupees, though under-subscription allows proportionate allotment up to five lakh rupees per employee. Shareholder reservations cannot exceed ten percent of the issue size. Applicants in reserved categories (except employees and retail individual shareholders) cannot make further applications in the net offer. Unsubscribed portions in any reserved category may be added to another reserved category, and any remaining unsubscribed portion is added to the net offer. If the net offer category is under-subscribed, spill-over from the reserved category is permitted. An applicant in any reserved category may apply for any number of specified securities, not exceeding the reserved portion for that category.

Other regulations include:
*   The abridged prospectus must contain disclosures specified in Part E of Schedule VI and accompany every application form.
*   Issuers must accept bids using only the ASBA facility.
*   Lead manager(s) must ensure the availability of the offer document and other issue material to various entities before the issue opens.
*   No person connected with the issue shall offer any direct or indirect incentive for making an application, except for fees or commission for services rendered.
*   Regulation 38, concerning security deposits, was omitted effective May 18, 2024.
*   Issuers may obtain grading for their initial public offer from one or more credit rating agencies registered with the Board.

Underwriting provisions vary based on the issue process. For issues made other than through the book building process, if underwriting is desired, the issuer must enter an underwriting agreement with merchant bankers or stock brokers before filing the prospectus, indicating the maximum number of specified securities they shall subscribe to at a predetermined price (not less than the issue price), and disclose this in the prospectus.

For issues made through the book building process, the issue shall be underwritten by lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s). However, at least seventy-five percent of the net offer compulsorily allotted to QIBs for eligibility cannot be underwritten. The issuer must enter an underwriting agreement before filing the prospectus, detailing the number of specified securities to be subscribed in the event of under-subscription. Lead manager(s) shall fulfill underwriting obligations if syndicate member(s) fail. Lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s) shall not subscribe to the issue except for fulfilling their underwriting obligations. Lead manager(s) must undertake minimum underwriting obligations as specified in the SEBI (Merchant Bankers) Regulations, 1992, and underwriting obligations should cover at least the minimum subscription.

This document outlines regulations for initial public offers (IPOs), covering underwriting, monitoring of issue proceeds, advertisements, issue opening, minimum subscription, subscription period, and application details.

**Underwriting:**
*   **For IPOs not using the book building process:** The issuer must enter an underwriting agreement with SEBI-registered merchant bankers or stock brokers before filing the prospectus. This agreement specifies the number of securities they will subscribe to for rejected applications (either directly or by procuring subscriptions) at a price not less than the issue price. This agreement must be disclosed in the prospectus.
*   **For IPOs using the book building process:**
    *   The issue must be underwritten by lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s), but at least 75% of the net offer compulsorily allotted to qualified institutional buyers (for eligibility) shall not be underwritten.
    *   Before filing the prospectus, the issuer must enter an underwriting agreement with lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s), detailing the number of securities they will subscribe to for rejected bids (directly or by procuring subscriptions) at a price not less than the issue price. This must be disclosed in the prospectus.
    *   If the issuer desires underwriting to cover under-subscription, an agreement must be made with lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s) before filing the red herring prospectus, indicating the maximum number of securities they will subscribe to (directly or by procuring subscriptions) at a price not less than the issue price. This must be disclosed in the red herring prospectus.
    *   If syndicate members fail their obligations, lead manager(s) must fulfill them.
    *   Lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s) can only subscribe to the issue to fulfill their underwriting obligations.
    *   Lead manager(s) must undertake minimum underwriting obligations as per SEBI (Merchant Bankers) Regulations, 1992.
    *   Where underwriting is required, obligations must be at least to the extent of minimum subscription.

**Monitoring Agency (Regulation 41):**
*   If the issue size (excluding offer for sale) exceeds 100 crore rupees, the issuer must arrange for a SEBI-registered credit rating agency to monitor the use of issue proceeds. This does not apply to issues by banks, public financial institutions, or insurance companies.
*   The monitoring agency submits quarterly reports (in Schedule XI format) to the issuer until 100% of the proceeds have been utilized.
*   The issuer's board and management must provide comments on these findings (as per Schedule XI).
*   The issuer must publicly disseminate the report on its website and submit it to stock exchange(s) within 45 days from the end of each quarter.

**Public Communications, Publicity Materials, Advertisements and Research Reports (Regulation 42):**
*   All such materials must comply with Schedule IX.

**Issue-related Advertisements (Regulation 43):**
*   After filing the red herring prospectus (book built issue) or prospectus (fixed price issue) with the Registrar of Companies, the issuer must make a pre-issue and price band advertisement in the same newspapers where the public announcement under Regulation 26(2) was published.
*   This advertisement must follow the format and disclosures specified in Part A of Schedule X.
*   The issuer may release advertisements for issue opening and closing, using formats in Parts B and C of Schedule X.
*   During the subscription period, no advertisements implying full or oversubscription or indicating investor response are permitted.

**Opening of the Issue (Regulation 44):**
*   A public issue may open within twelve months from the date of the Board's observations under Regulation 25.
*   An issue must open at least three working days after filing the red herring prospectus (book built) or prospectus (fixed price) with the Registrar of Companies.

**Minimum Subscription (Regulation 45):**
*   The minimum subscription for an issue must be at least 90% of the offer through the offer document, except for an offer for sale. This is also subject to minimum specified securities allotment as per Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957.
*   If the minimum subscription is not received, all application monies must be refunded to applicants forthwith, but no later than four days from the issue closure.

**Period of Subscription (Regulation 46):**
*   An initial public offer must be open for at least three working days and not more than ten working days.
*   If the price band is revised, the bidding (issue) period must be extended for a minimum of three working days.
*   In cases of force majeure, banking strike, or similar unforeseen circumstances, the issuer may extend the bidding (issue) period for a minimum of one working day, with recorded reasons.

**Application and Minimum Application Value (Regulation 47):**
*   A person cannot apply for more specified securities in the net offer category than the total number offered to the public.
*   The maximum application by non-institutional investors cannot exceed the total specified securities offered in the issue minus those offered to qualified institutional buyers.
*   The issuer must stipulate a minimum application size (number of securities) corresponding to a minimum application value between ten thousand rupees and fifteen thousand rupees.
*   Applications must be invited in multiples of this minimum application value.
*   The minimum sum payable on application per specified security must be at least 25% of the issue price, except for an offer for sale, where the full issue price is payable at the time of application.
*   The "minimum application value" refers to the issue price of the securities, not the amount payable on application.

The provided text outlines regulations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (Amendment) Regulations, 2024, and 2022, pertaining to capital issues.

**Manner of Calls (Regulation 48):** If an issuer proposes to receive subscription monies in calls, the outstanding amount must be called within twelve months from the date of allotment. Failure to pay within this period results in the forfeiture of the equity shares and already paid subscription money, unless a monitoring agency (as per regulation 41) has been appointed.

**Allotment Procedure and Basis of Allotment (Regulation 49):**
*   An allotment cannot be made if the number of prospective allottees is less than one thousand.
*   Allotment cannot exceed the specified securities offered, except for rounding off in cases of oversubscription (up to one per cent of the net offer to public for minimum lots), in consultation with the designated stock exchange.
*   Allotment to investors other than retail individual investors, non-institutional investors (inserted w.e.f. 1.4.2022/1.7.2022), and anchor investors is on a proportionate basis within their respective categories, rounded to the nearest integer, subject to a minimum application size.
*   The value of specified securities allotted to any person (except employees) under specific reservations (Regulation 33(1)(a) or 33(2)(a)) is capped at two lakh rupees for retail investors or five lakh rupees for eligible employees.
*   Retail individual investors receive not less than the minimum bid lot, with any remaining shares allotted proportionately.
*   Non-institutional investors (inserted w.e.f. 1.4.2022/1.7.2022) receive not less than the minimum application size, with any remaining shares allotted proportionately as per Schedule XIII.
*   The basis of allotment is finalized fairly by authorized employees of the designated stock exchange, lead manager(s), and registrars, following the procedure in Part A of Schedule XIV.

**Allotment, Refund, and Payment of Interest (Regulation 50):**
*   The issuer and lead manager(s) must ensure allotment and/or refund/unblocking of application monies within the period specified by the Board.
*   Lead manager(s) are responsible for ensuring electronic allotment, credit of dematerialized securities, and refund/unblocking.
*   If allotment and/or refund/unblocking are not completed within the stipulated period, the issuer must pay interest at fifteen per cent per annum to investors, as disclosed in the offer document, with lead manager(s) ensuring this.

**Post-Issue Advertisements (Regulation 51):**
*   Lead manager(s) must release an advertisement within ten days of the completion of various activities, detailing subscription, basis of allotment, application statistics (including ASBA), refund despatch, credit of securities, and listing application date.
*   This advertisement must be published in at least one English national daily, one Hindi national daily, and one regional language daily with wide circulation at the issuer's registered office location.
*   These details must also be placed on the stock exchange(s) websites.

**Post-Issue Responsibilities of the Lead Manager(s) (Regulation 52):**
*   Lead manager(s) remain responsible until the issue process is complete and for any subsequent issue-related matters.
*   They must regularly monitor the redressal of investor grievances. Their responsibility continues until applicants receive securities/credit/refund, the listing agreement is entered, and listing/trading permission is obtained.
*   They coordinate with registrars and intermediaries to monitor application flow, processing, basis of allotment finalization, demat credit, ASBA unblocking/refund despatch, and listing.
*   Any acts of omission or commission by intermediaries must be reported to the Board.
*   In case of underwriter devolvement, a notice must be issued within ten days from the date of issue closure.
*   For undersubscribed underwritten issues, information on underwriters who failed to meet their devolvement must be furnished to the Board (Schedule XVIII).

**Release of Subscription Money (Regulation 53):**
*   Lead manager(s) confirm to bankers (with copies of listing and trading approvals) that all issue formalities are complete, allowing the release of money to the issuer or for refund if the issue fails.
*   If the issuer fails to obtain listing/trading permission, it must refund all monies received within four days (substituted w.e.f. 14.1.2022) of receiving intimation from stock exchanges rejecting the listing application.
*   If the money is not repaid within these four days, the issuer and every defaulting director are jointly and severally liable to repay with fifteen per cent per annum interest from the expiry of the fourth day (substituted w.e.f. 14.1.2022).
*   Lead manager(s) ensure money release complies with Section 40(3) of the Companies Act, 2013.

**Reporting of Transactions of Promoters and Promoter Group and Other Pre-IPO Transactions (Regulation 54):**
