The provided text outlines various regulations concerning bonus issues, the Social Stock Exchange, and the Board's powers regarding enforcement, contravention, and relaxation of rules.

**Social Stock Exchange (SSE):**
The Social Stock Exchange is required to specify additional norms for issue procedures, covering aspects like agreements with depositories and banks, ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) related matters, duration for public issuance, allocation methodology, and other ancillary matters.

**Conditions for Bonus Issues:**
An issuer can make a bonus issue of equity shares only if:
*   Its articles of association authorize bonus shares or capitalization of reserves; if not, a general body resolution must be passed to make such provisions.
*   It has received approval from stock exchanges for listing and trading of all securities issued prior to the bonus issue (excluding employee stock options and convertible securities).
*   It has not defaulted on interest or principal payments for fixed deposits or debt securities.
*   It has not defaulted on statutory dues for employees (e.g., provident fund, gratuity, bonus).
*   Any outstanding partly paid shares are made fully paid-up.
*   None of its promoters or directors are fugitive economic offenders.

**Restrictions on Bonus Issues (Regulation 294):**
*   An issuer must reserve equity shares of the same class for holders of outstanding compulsorily convertible debt instruments, proportionate to their convertible part. These reserved shares are to be issued at the time of conversion on the same terms and proportion as the bonus shares.
*   Bonus issues must be made only from free reserves, the securities premium account, or the capital redemption reserve account, provided they are built from genuine profits or securities premium collected in cash. Reserves created by revaluation of fixed assets cannot be capitalized for this purpose.
*   Bonus shares cannot be issued in lieu of dividends.
*   If an issuer has issued SR (Special Rights) equity shares to promoters or founders, any bonus issue on these SR shares must carry the same ratio of voting rights as ordinary shares, and the bonus SR shares will convert to equity shares with voting rights equivalent to ordinary equity shares, along with existing SR equity shares.
*   The allotment of shares in a bonus issue must be made only in dematerialized form.

**Completion of Bonus Issues (Regulation 295):**
*   If a bonus issue only requires board approval, it must be implemented within fifteen days from the date of board approval.
*   If shareholders' approval for capitalization of profits or reserves is required, the bonus issue must be implemented within two months from the date of the board meeting where the decision was taken, subject to shareholders' approval.
*   For the purpose of implementation, the date of commencement of trading is considered.
*   Once announced, a bonus issue cannot be withdrawn.

**Power to Relax Strict Enforcement (Regulatory Sandbox - Chapter XI-A, Regulation 295A):**
The Board may exempt any person or class of persons from the operation of all or any provisions of these regulations for up to twelve months. This is for furthering innovation related to testing new products, processes, services, or business models in a live environment of a "regulatory sandbox" in the securities markets. Such exemptions are subject to specified conditions. A regulatory sandbox is defined as a live testing environment where new products, processes, services, or business models can be deployed on a limited set of eligible customers for a specified period to foster innovation.

**Directions by the Board (Regulation 296):**
The Board can issue directions or orders, either on its own initiative or based on information/investigation, in the interest of investors or the securities market. These directions may include prohibiting persons from accessing the securities market for a specified period, directing the sale or divestment of securities, or any other appropriate direction. A reasonable opportunity of being heard must be given to the concerned person, either before or after issuing such a direction or order (for interim orders).

**Liability for Contravention (Regulation 297):**
A listed issuer or any other person contravening these regulations is liable for actions by the respective stock exchange(s), which may include imposition of fines, suspension of trading, freezing of promoter/promoter group holdings of designated securities, and other actions specified by the Board. The Board also specifies the manner of revoking suspension and freezing actions.

**Failure to Pay Fine (Regulation 298):**
If a listed issuer fails to pay a fine imposed by a recognized stock exchange within the specified period, the stock exchange may initiate other actions in accordance with its bye-laws after giving written notice.

**Power to Remove Difficulty (Regulation 299):**
The Board may issue clarifications through guidance notes or circulars, with recorded reasons, to address any difficulties in the application or interpretation of these regulations.

**Power to Relax Strict Enforcement (General - Regulation 300):**
The Board may relax the strict enforcement of any requirement of these regulations in the interest of investors or for the development of the securities market if it is satisfied that:
*   The requirement is procedural in nature.
*   A disclosure requirement is not relevant for a particular class of industry or issuer.
*   The non-compliance was caused by factors beyond the issuer's control.
An application for such relaxation, detailing the grounds, must be filed with the Board and accompanied by a non-refundable fee of rupees one lakh.

**Repeal and Savings (Regulation 301):**
Upon the commencement of these regulations, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2009, are rescinded.

This document outlines the disclosure requirements for draft offer documents, draft letters of offer, offer documents, and letters of offer pertaining to public issues and rights issues of specified securities.

**General Disclosure Instructions:**
All information must be relevant, updated, and substantiated with disclosed sources. Terms like "market leader" require proper substantiation. Blank spaces in the draft offer document must be filled before filing. Simple English should be used, clarifying any technical terms. Cross-references to other parts of the document must include paragraph headings and page numbers. Unsubstantiated forward-looking statements are prohibited. Consistency in disclosure style (e.g., using first person throughout) and the use of a single standard financial unit are mandatory.

**Applicability and Exceptions:**
Issuers undertaking a public issue or a rights issue of specified securities must adhere to these disclosures.
*   A fast track public issue may omit disclosures specified in Part D (which was Part B prior to a 2022 amendment).
*   A further public offer may omit Part C disclosures if specific conditions are met.
*   A rights issue may only make Part B disclosures if specific conditions are met.
*   For public issues by issuers listed or to be listed on an SME exchange, "retail individual investors" refers to "individual investors who apply for minimum application size" (as per a 2025 amendment).

**Offer Document Structure and Content:**

**1. Cover Pages:**
*   **Physical Specifications:** Cover pages must be of at least 100 GSM quality, white, and without patterns.
*   **Front Outside Cover Page:** Must contain issue and issuer details, selling shareholder details (in tabular format, including average cost of acquisition and offer for sale details), and other Board-specified information (content updated in 2022).
*   **Front Inside Cover Page:** (Previously blank, content updated in 2022) Must include:
    *   The type of offer document (e.g., "Draft Red Herring Prospectus").
    *   Date of the document.
    *   Type of issuance (book built or fixed price).
    *   For public issues, a prominent clause: "Please read Section 32 of the Companies Act, 2013".
    *   Issuer details: name, logo, incorporation date/place, Corporate Identity Number (CIN), registered/corporate office addresses, telephone, contact person, website, and email (with reference to any changes in address/name).
    *   Names of the promoter(s).
    *   Nature, number, and price of specified securities offered, and issue size (including any offer for sale).
    *   Aggregate amount to be raised through all stages of offers via a shelf prospectus.
    *   For a first issue, a 'Risks in relation to the First Issue' clause in a box format, stating no formal market, issue price not indicative of market price, and no assurance of active/sustained trading.
    *   A 'General Risk' clause in a box format, advising investors of investment risks, reliance on their own examination, and that SEBI does not recommend or guarantee the document's accuracy, with a cross-reference to 'Risk factors'.
    *   An 'Issuer’s Absolute Responsibility' clause in a box format, confirming the issuer's responsibility for the document's material accuracy, completeness, and non-misleading nature, with selling shareholders accepting responsibility for their specific statements.
    *   Names, logos, and addresses of all lead manager(s) (who signed the due diligence certificate and filed the document), including contact details and disclosure if an associate of the issuer.
    *   Name, logo, and address of the registrar to the issue, with contact details.
    *   Issue schedule: Anchor bid period (if any), opening/closing dates, and earliest closing date (if any).
    *   Credit rating (if applicable) and IPO grading (if any).
    *   Names of stock exchanges where securities are proposed to be listed and details of their in-principle approval.
*   **Back Cover Pages:** Both the back inside and back outside cover pages must be blank.

**2. Table of Contents:** Must appear immediately after the front inside cover page.

**3. Definitions and Abbreviations:** This section should cover conventional/general terms, issue-related terms, issuer/industry-related terms, and abbreviations.

**4. Offer Document Summary:** This section must summarize the following:
*   Primary business of the Issuer and the industry in which it operates (each in not more than 100 words).
*   Names of the promoters.
*   Size of the issue, separately disclosing fresh issue and offer for sale.
*   Objects of the issue in a tabular format.
*   Aggregate pre-issue shareholding of the promoter, promoter group, and selling shareholder(s) as a percentage of the paid-up share capital.
*   Pre-issue and post-issue shareholding (as at allotment) for the promoter(s), promoter group, and additional top 10 shareholders, presented in a specific tabular format (added in 2025), including notes on promoter group members, exercised options, and transfers until the prospectus date.
*   Details from restated consolidated financial statements for the past 3 years and stub period in tabular format: Share capital, Net Worth, Revenue, Profit after tax, Earnings per share, Net Asset Value per equity share, and Total borrowings.
*   Auditor qualifications not given effect in the restated financial statements.
*   A summary table of outstanding litigations with a cross-reference.
*   A cross-reference to the 'Risk Factors' section.
*   A summary table of contingent liabilities with a cross-reference.
*   A summary of related party transactions for the last 3 years with a cross-reference.
*   Details of all financing arrangements by promoters, promoter group members, directors of a promoter company, issuer's directors, and their relatives for purchasing issuer securities (outside normal business) in the six months preceding the document date.
*   Weighted average price at which specified securities were acquired by each promoter and selling shareholder in the last one year.
*   Average cost of acquisition of shares for promoters and selling shareholders.
*   Size of the pre-IPO placement and allottees upon completion.
*   Any issuances of equity shares for consideration other than cash in the last one year.
*   Any split or consolidation of equity shares in the last one year.

This document outlines disclosure requirements, primarily focusing on risk factors, for an issuer.

**Key Disclosure Requirements:**

1.  **Exemption from Securities Laws:** Any exemption granted by SEBI from complying with securities laws must be disclosed.

2.  **Risk Factors:**
    *   **Presentation:** Must be printed in a clear, readable font (preferably minimum 10 point size).
    *   **Classification:** Risks are classified as specific to the project/internal to the issuer, or external/beyond the issuer's control.
    *   **Materiality:** Determined by considering risks collectively, their qualitative impact, and potential future material impact, even if not individually or presently material.
    *   **Format:** Each risk factor must state the risk as envisaged by the issuer and any proposals to address it.
    *   **Proposals:** Proposals to address risks must not contain speculative statements about positive outcomes or relate to sub-judice matters.
    *   **Order & Implications:** Disclosed in descending order of materiality. Risks with material impact require disclosure of likely/potential implications (including financial, if quantifiable); if not quantifiable, a distinct statement to that effect is required.
    *   **Mandatory Disclosures (where applicable):** Include, but are not limited to:
        *   Material statutory clearances/approvals yet to be received.
        *   Seasonality of business.
        *   Recent issues of specified securities at a lower price (excluding bonus issues).
        *   Details of interim use of funds and probable acquisition completion date if issue object is to finance unidentified acquisitions.
        *   Risk of unplaced orders for plant and machinery related to issue objects (with percentage/value).
        *   Lack of significant experience of the issuer or promoters in the industry segment.
        *   Losses in the last three financial years.
        *   Dependence on a single or few customers.
        *   Refusal of listing for issuer's or subsidiaries' securities in the last ten years.
        *   Failure to meet listing requirements by the issuer or subsidiaries, and any penalties.
        *   Limited or sporadic trading of issuer's specified securities.
        *   Defaults in outstanding debt instruments (e.g., covenants, interest, redemption, reserve, asset/interest/debt-service cover).
        *   Unsecured loans of the issuer and subsidiaries that can be recalled anytime.
        *   Default in repayment of deposits or interest by the issuer and subsidiaries.
        *   Potential conflict of interest of promoters/directors involved in similar ventures.
        *   Quantified shortfalls in performance versus stated objects of previous issues by the listed issuer/subsidiaries (last 10 years) or listed subsidiaries/promoters (last 5 years).
        *   Interests of promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, or senior management beyond normal remuneration/reimbursement.
        *   Portion of issue proceeds proposed to be paid to promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, or senior management.
        *   Relationship of promoter/directors with entities from whom land was acquired/proposed in the last 5 years.
        *   Excessive dependence on key managerial personnel or senior management for the project.
        *   Material unsecured investments in debt instruments by the issuer.
        *   Non-provision for decline in investment value.
        *   Summary of outstanding litigations (tabular, with amount involved), highlighting material adverse criminal/regulatory/taxation matters.
        *   Delay in project implementation schedule for which funds are raised.
        *   Statement that deployment of issue proceeds is at the issuer's discretion if no monitoring agency is required.
        *   Negative cash flow from operating activities in the last three financial years.
        *   If land to be acquired from issue proceeds is not registered in the issuer's name.
        *   Restrictive covenants on equity shareholders' interests in various agreements.
        *   Existence of a large number of pending investor grievances against the issuer and listed subsidiaries.
        *   Risks associated with second/residual charge or subordinated obligation on asset cover for secured convertible debt instruments.
        *   If proforma/restated consolidated financial statements are provided by a peer-reviewed Chartered Accountant who is not the statutory auditor, this must be a Top 10 Risk Factor.

3.  **Introduction:**
    *   Includes brief issue details and a summary of consolidated financial information.

4.  **General Information:**
    *   Covers name and address of registered/corporate offices, issuer's registration number, RoC address, names/designations/addresses/DINs of board members, and contact details (names, addresses, phone, email, website) for the Company Secretary, legal advisor, bankers to the issuer, compliance officer, lead manager(s), registrars to the issue, and bankers/brokers to the issue.

This document outlines disclosure requirements for public offers, including initial public offers (IPOs), further public offers (FPOs), and rights issues, covering several key areas:

**1. Promoters' Contribution and Lock-in:**
Disclosures must include the number, face value, issue price, percentage of promoters’ contribution to total issued capital, and the lock-in date for specified securities. For an IPO, details of all individual allotments from the issuer's incorporation date are required. For an FPO by a listed issuer, these details are needed for the preceding five years. In FPOs or rights issues, shares acquired by promoters through public issues, rights issues, preferential issues, bonus issues, conversion of depository receipts, or employee stock schemes must be shown separately from shares acquired in the secondary market, along with the aggregate cost of secondary market shares if available. Compliance with promoters’ contribution and lock-in requirements must be detailed, and if exempt, the relevant provisions cited. A statement is required from the promoter undertaking full conversion if their contribution is in the same optionally convertible debt instrument offered to the public.

**2. General Statements and Lead Manager Details:**
A statement confirming that the issuer, its directors, or lead manager(s) have not entered into any buy-back arrangements for the specified securities is required. All securities offered must be stated to be fully paid-up (if applicable) or subject to forfeiture for non-payment of calls within twelve months of allotment. Details of shareholding of the lead manager(s) and their associates in the issuer must also be provided.

**3. Employee Stock Option/Purchase Schemes (ESOP/ESPS):**
Details of options granted or equity shares issued under any ESOP or ESPS in the preceding three years (separately for each year) and cumulatively prior to the offer document date are required. For IPOs with outstanding options, specific disclosures include options granted, vested, exercised, exercise price, total shares arising from exercise, lapsed options, variation of terms, money realized, and total options in force. Employee-wise details are required for key managerial personnel (KMP) and senior management; employees receiving 5% or more of options granted in a year; and identified employees granted options equal to or exceeding 1% of issued capital at the time of grant. Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) pursuant to option exercise must be calculated. If the intrinsic value method was used for employee compensation cost, the difference between this and the fair value method, and its impact on profits and EPS, must be disclosed. The pricing formula, method, and significant assumptions (e.g., risk-free rate, expected life, volatility, dividends, underlying share price) used for fair value estimation are required. The impact on profits and EPS for the last three years, had SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 been followed, must be shown. Intentions of KMP, senior management, and whole-time directors holding shares from ESOP/ESPS to sell within three months of listing (aggregate number) must be disclosed, regardless of when options were exercised. Specific disclosures are required for directors, KMP, senior management, and employees holding over 1% of issued capital from ESOP/ESPS who intend to sell within three months, including their name, designation, quantum issued, and quantum intended to sell. For ESPS, details include the number of shares issued, price, and employee-wise details for KMP and senior management; employees issued 5% or more shares in a year; and identified employees issued shares equal to or exceeding 1% of issued capital at issuance. Diluted EPS from ESPS shares and consideration received are also required.

**4. Further Public Offer Compliance:**
For FPOs by a listed issuer that previously made a preferential allotment, bonus issue, or qualified institutions placement (QIP) in the ten years preceding the draft offer document/offer document date, a confirmation of compliance with relevant regulations is necessary.

**5. Particulars of the Issue - Objects of the Issue:**
The general objects of the issue must be stated. If loan repayment is an object, details of the loan (lender, terms, outstanding amount) and a statutory auditor's certificate (or a Chartered Accountant's certificate from a Peer Review Board-certified CA for specific cases) for loan utilization are required. If investment in a joint venture, subsidiary, or acquisition is an object, details of the investment form (equity, debt, etc.), or a statement if undecided, are needed. For debt investments, interest rate, security, repayment terms, and subordination details are required, along with the nature of expected benefit to the issuer. If granting a loan to an entity other than a subsidiary, details of loan agreements (interest rate, secured/unsecured, duration, security, repayment terms, subordination) and expected benefits are required, including details if to group companies. If long-term working capital is an object, additional disclosures on a standalone basis (based on audited standalone financial statements, restated if consolidated statements impact them) include the basis of estimation, reasons for raising additional capital, projected working capital requirements (with detailed breakdowns of current assets, liabilities, and financing sources), total envisaged working capital, and existing working capital details. Reasons must be provided if no working capital is shown as part of the project. For land acquisition, names of entities from whom land is acquired/proposed, cost, and relationship are required.

This document outlines various disclosure requirements for an issuer, particularly when raising capital through an issue, as per the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations.

Key details to be disclosed include:

1.  **Objects of the Issue:**
    *   **Land Acquisition:** If issue proceeds are used for land acquisition, details must be provided regarding transactions with promoters/directors, whether the land is free from encumbrances, has a clear title, is registered, and if all necessary approvals have been applied for/received (or an affirmative statement if none are required). Figures must be consistent with the "Cost of the Project" section.
    *   **Project Funding:** If funding a project, details are required on the project's location, plant and machinery (including cost, suppliers, order/supply dates, quotations for unplaced orders, and details of second-hand machinery), technology, process, technical and financial collaborations (including collaborator's registration, incorporation year, paid-up capital, turnover, and general relevant information), and infrastructure facilities for raw materials and utilities.
    *   **Property Purchase:** If purchasing property, details include vendors' information (names, addresses, occupations), amounts paid/payable (cash, shares, debentures, goodwill), nature of title/interest, and particulars of any related transactions within the preceding two years involving vendors, promoters, or directors. This applies to property paid for wholly or partly by issue proceeds or not yet acquired.
    *   **Plant/Equipment/Technology/Process Purchase:** If purchasing these items, details similar to project funding are required, including equipment specifics, cost, suppliers, order/supply dates, quotations for unplaced orders, and details of second-hand equipment.

2.  **Specific Instrument Disclosures:**
    *   **Secured Convertible Debt Instruments:** Description of assets for security/asset cover, basis for security cover computation, valuation methods, periodicity of valuation, and ranking of charges.
    *   **Warrants:** The objects for which funds from warrant conversions are proposed to be used.

3.  **Requirement of Funds:**
    *   Total project cost, broken down activity-wise or project-wise, especially if multiple activities or phased implementation.
    *   Details of all material existing or anticipated transactions related to issue proceeds or project cost with promoters, promoter group, directors, key managerial personnel, senior management, and group companies.

4.  **Funding Plan (Means of Finance):**
    *   An undertaking confirming firm arrangements for 75% of the stated means of finance for the project (excluding the proposed issue amount and existing internal accruals).
    *   Details of the balance portion of finance for which no firm arrangement has been made.
    *   Details of funds tied up and avenues for deployment of any excess proceeds.

5.  **Appraisal:**
    *   Scope, purpose, and date of any project appraisal.
    *   Project cost and means of finance must align with the appraisal report, with explanations for any revisions.
    *   Weaknesses and threats identified in the appraisal report must be presented as risk factors, along with applicable disclaimer clauses.

6.  **Schedule of Implementation:**
    *   A tabular schedule of project implementation, including progress made (land acquisition, civil works, plant/machinery installation, trial/commercial production), and reasons for any delays.

7.  **Deployment of Funds:**
    *   Details of sources and deployment of funds on the project up to two months prior to the offer document filing date, certified by a statutory auditor.
    *   A cash flow statement from the statutory auditor for promoter's contribution utilized before the public issue.
    *   Means and sources of financing for funds already deployed, including bridge loans repayable from issue proceeds.
    *   Year-wise break-up of proposed project expenditure.
    *   Net issue proceeds pending utilization must be deposited only in scheduled commercial banks.

8.  **Expenses of the Issue:**
    *   A break-up of issue expenses (amount, percentage of total issue expenses, and percentage of total issue size) for items such as lead manager(s) fees (including underwriting commission), brokerage, registrars, legal advisors, advertising, regulators, printing, and others.

9.  **Basis for Issue Price:**
    *   Disclosures on a consolidated basis, adjusted for any bonus or split shares, including:
        *   Earnings Per Share (EPS) and Diluted EPS (pre-issue, last three years).
        *   Price to Earnings (P/E) ratio (pre-issue) and comparison with industry P/E (highest, lowest, average).
        *   Average Return on Net Worth (last three years).
        *   Net Asset Value (NAV) per share (based on last balance sheet, after issue, and comparison with issue price).
    *   An illustrative format for these disclosures is provided, with specific example figures.
    *   The formula or basis for calculating these financial ratios must be disclosed.
    *   Lead manager(s) must exercise due diligence for illustrative entries.
    *   Comparison of issuer's accounting ratios with industry average and peer group (comparable size, same industry), ensuring consistency (e.g., consolidated vs. consolidated) and using regulatory filings for peer group data.
    *   Disclosure of dilution of financial ratios due to bonus shares and justification of the issue price.
    *   Specific statements are required for book-built issues (price determined in consultation with lead manager(s) based on book-building) and fixed-price issues (price determined and justified in consultation with lead manager(s) based on provided information).
    *   Accounting ratios must account for compulsory conversions and assumed exercise of options.
    *   For fully convertible debt instruments bearing interest less than the bank rate, the price that would work out to the investor, considering notional interest loss, must be disclosed.
    *   **Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):** KPIs and their terms must be defined consistently and precisely in simple English in the "Definitions and Abbreviations" section, with technical terms further clarified. KPIs must be approved by the Audit Committee.

The document also notes amendments made by the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (Amendment) Regulations in 2025, 2022, and 2023.

This document outlines disclosure requirements for Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and issue price details in offer documents, as per the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2022, effective 21.11.2022, and applicable for Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) filed on or after this date.

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):**
*   Technical terms used in explaining KPIs must be clarified in simple terms.
*   KPIs disclosed in the offer document require approval from the Audit Committee of the Issuer Company.
*   They must be certified by statutory auditor(s), Chartered Accountants (holding a valid certificate from the Peer Review Board of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India), or Cost Accountants (holding a valid certificate from the Peer Review Board of the Institute of Cost Accountants of India).
*   The certificate issued for KPIs must be included in the list of material documents for inspection.
*   KPI details must be provided for a period co-terminus with the restated financial information disclosed in the offer document.
*   KPIs should be comprehensive, with explanations on how management historically used them to analyze, track, or monitor operational and/or financial performance.
*   Comparison of KPIs over time must explain additions or dispositions to the business, such as material acquisitions or dispositions of assets/business.

**Disclosures in the ‘Basis for Issue Price’ section:**
*   All KPIs pertaining to the Issuer Company that have been disclosed to its investors at any point during the three years preceding the date of filing of the DRHP/RHP must be disclosed.
*   The Audit Committee of the Issuer Company must confirm that verified and audited details for these previously disclosed KPIs are included.
*   The Issuer Company, in consultation with the lead merchant banker, may disclose any other relevant and material KPIs that have a bearing on the basis for issue price.
*   Cross-references of KPIs disclosed in other sections of the offer document must be provided in this section.
*   KPIs disclosed here must be compared with Indian and/or global listed peer companies of comparable size, industry, and business model, with appropriate notes to explain differences if a one-to-one comparison is not possible.

**Ongoing KPI Disclosure:**
*   The Issuer Company must continue to disclose the KPIs from the ‘Basis for Issue Price’ section periodically (at least once a year or for any lesser period determined by the Issuer) for at least one year after the listing date or until the utilization of issue proceeds.
*   Any changes in these KPIs during this period must be explained by the Issuer Company.
*   Ongoing KPIs must continue to be certified by a member of an expert body.

**Issue Price, Floor Price, or Price Band:**
The Issuer Company and lead merchant banker (LMs) must disclose details regarding:
*   **Primary/New Issue Price:** Price per share for primary/new issues (equity/convertible securities, excluding ESOP/ESOS and bonus shares) during the 18 months preceding the DRHP/RHP filing, if such issuance is 5% or more of the fully diluted paid-up share capital (pre-issue, excluding unvested ESOPs) in a single or rolling 30-day transaction.
*   **Secondary Sale/Acquisition Price:** Price per share for secondary sales/acquisitions (equity/convertible securities) involving promoter/promoter group entities, shareholders selling through an offer for sale in IPO, or shareholders with director nomination rights (excluding gifts) during the 18 months preceding the DRHP/RHP filing, if the acquisition or sale is 5% or more of the fully diluted paid-up share capital (pre-issue, excluding unvested ESOPs) in a single or rolling 30-day transaction.
*   **Fallback:** If no such transactions exist, information on the last 5 primary or secondary transactions (secondary transactions involving specific parties) not older than 3 years prior to the DRHP/RHP filing, irrespective of transaction size, must be disclosed.
*   All disclosed prices per share must be adjusted for corporate actions (e.g., split, bonus).
*   **Weighted Average Cost of Acquisition (WACA):** The floor price and cap price, expressed as "[●] times" the WACA based on primary/secondary transactions, must be disclosed in a table format.
*   **Explanation for Offer Price/Cap Price:** A detailed explanation for the offer price/cap price being "[●] times" WACA, including a comparison of the Issuer Company’s KPIs and financial ratios for the last three full financial years and any stub period.
*   **External Factors:** An explanation for the offer price/cap price being "[●] times" WACA in view of external factors that may have influenced the pricing.
*   **Price Band Advertisement:** The WACA table and a recommendation from a Committee of Independent Directors (stating that the price band is justified based on quantitative factors/KPIs versus WACA) must be included in the ‘Risks to Investors’ section of the Price Band Advertisement.

**Tax Benefits:**
*   Any special tax benefits (under direct and indirect tax laws) for the issuer, its shareholders, and its material subsidiaries (identified in accordance with SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015) must be disclosed.

**About the Issuer:**
*   **Industry Overview:** If an extract of any industry report is disclosed, the complete industry report must be provided as part of the material documents. (This section was substituted by SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2023, w.e.f. 23.5.2023).
*   **Business Overview:** Includes details on the primary business, plant/machinery/technology/process, subsisting collaborations, infrastructure facilities, products/services (nature, end users, marketing approach), business strategy (without financial forecasts), existing installed capacities and capacity utilization for the previous three years, intellectual property rights (legal holding, registration details, agreements for use if registered with promoter-interested entities), and material properties.
*   **Key Industry-Regulations (if applicable).**
*   **History and Corporate Structure:** Includes details such as the date of incorporation, business commencement, conversions, name changes (with reasons), registered office changes (with reasons), major historical events (e.g., significant partnerships, project time/cost overruns, capacity creation, product/service launches, market entry/exit, awards, defaults/restructuring of borrowings), and material acquisitions/divestments, mergers, amalgamations, or asset revaluations in the last ten years.

This document outlines various disclosure requirements related to an issuer's structure, agreements, and management.

**Key details include:**

1.  **Main Objects and Amendments:** Disclosure of the issuer's main objects as per its Memorandum of Association, along with dates and details of any amendments made in the last ten years.
2.  **Group Entities:** Information on holding companies, subsidiaries, and joint ventures, if applicable. This includes their name, nature of business, capital structure, the issuer's shareholding, and any accumulated profits or losses of subsidiaries not accounted for by the issuer.
3.  **Shareholders' and Other Agreements:**
    *   Key terms of all existing shareholders’ agreements, even if the issuer is not a party but is aware of them.
    *   Agreements entered into by key managerial personnel (KMP) (or senior management, inserted w.e.f. 31.01.2023), directors, promoters, or other employees concerning compensation or profit sharing related to dealings in the issuer's securities.
    *   Details of guarantees given to third parties by a promoter offering shares in a proposed offer for sale, including reasons, amount, issuer obligations, guarantee period, financial implications of default, security, and consideration.
    *   Key terms, dates, parties, and general nature of other existing material agreements (e.g., with strategic, joint venture, or financial partners) not in the ordinary course of business.
    *   Details of agreements required under Clause 5A of paragraph A of part A of Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (inserted w.e.f. 08.03.2025).
    *   All such shareholders' and other agreements must be included in the list of material contracts as required under sub-item (1) of Item (18) (substituted w.e.f. 14.1.2022).
4.  **Management:**
    *   **Board of Directors:**
        *   Personal details (name, DIN, DOB, age, qualifications, experience, address, occupation, term expiration, directorship period, other directorships) for managers, managing directors, and other directors (including nominee and whole-time directors).
        *   Details of current and past directorships in listed companies whose shares were suspended from trading (name, stock exchange, suspension date, reasons/period if >3 months, revocation date, director's term) for the preceding five years.
        *   Details of current and past directorships in listed companies that were delisted (name, stock exchange, delisting date, compulsory/voluntary, reasons, relisting date, director's term).
        *   Nature of any family relationship between directors or between directors and KMP (or senior management, inserted w.e.f. 31.01.2023).
        *   Any arrangements or understandings with major shareholders, customers, suppliers, or others leading to a director's or senior management's selection.
        *   Details of service contracts with directors providing termination benefits, or a negative statement if none exist.
        *   Details of borrowing powers.
    *   **Compensation of Managing Directors and/or Whole-time Directors:**
        *   Dates, parties, and general nature of contracts appointing or fixing remuneration in the preceding two years.
        *   Amount of compensation paid and benefits in kind granted individually by the issuer for all services, and remuneration paid/payable by subsidiary or associate companies in the last financial year, including contingent or deferred compensation.
        *   A brief description of any bonus or profit-sharing plan and the basis of director participation.
        *   All such contracts must be included in the list of material contracts under sub-item (1) of Item (18) (substituted w.e.f. 14.1.2022).
    *   **Shareholding of Directors:** Including qualification shares, if applicable.
    *   **Interest of Directors:** Nature and extent of interest in the issuer, including property acquired/proposed, or in its promotion/formation. If the interest is through a firm/company, details of that firm/company's interest and any sums paid to the director/firm/company for becoming/qualifying as a director or for services in promotion/formation.
    *   **Changes in Directors:** Any changes and reasons during the last three years.
    *   **Management Organisation Structure.**
    *   **Corporate Governance:** A statement of compliance with SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, regarding board composition and committees (audit, nomination and remuneration, stakeholders relationship). Details of these committees (and risk management committee, if applicable), including members and terms of reference.
    *   **Key Managerial Personnel (KMP) and Senior Management (inserted w.e.f. 31.01.2023):**
        *   Details including name, joining date, qualification, term of office/expiration, service contracts (including termination/retirement benefits), and previous employment.
        *   Past business experience, functions, and areas of experience in the issuer.
        *   Nature of any family relationship between KMP (and senior management, inserted w.e.f. 31.01.2023).
        *   Any arrangements or understandings with major shareholders, customers, suppliers, or others leading to a KMP's (or senior management's, inserted w.e.f. 31.01.2023) selection.
        *   Amount of compensation paid and benefits in kind granted individually by the issuer in the last financial year, including contingent or deferred compensation.
        *   A brief description of any bonus or profit-sharing plan and the basis of KMP (and senior management, inserted w.e.f. 31.01.2023) participation.
        *   Status as a permanent employee or otherwise.
        *   Shareholding in the issuer.
        *   Any changes (other than normal retirement) in KMP (or senior management, inserted w.e.f. 31.01.2023) in the preceding three years.

The document outlines disclosure requirements for various aspects of an issuer's operations and personnel.

**Regarding Employees:**
*   If attrition of key managerial personnel and senior management is high compared to the industry, reasons must be disclosed.
*   Disclosures concerning employee stock option schemes or employee stock purchase schemes, if any, must refer to the relevant page.
*   Any non-salary related amount or benefit paid or intended to be paid to key managerial personnel and senior management within the two preceding years, along with the consideration for such payment, must be disclosed.

**Regarding Promoters/Principal Shareholders:**
*   **For individual promoters:** A complete profile including name, date of birth, age, personal addresses, educational qualifications, business experience, past positions, directorships, other ventures, special achievements, business and financial activities, photograph, and Permanent Account Number (PAN) is required. A declaration confirming submission of PAN, Bank Account Number(s), Passport Number, Aadhaar card number, and driving license number to stock exchanges at the time of filing the draft offer document is also needed.
*   **For company promoters:** A brief history (incorporation date, activity changes, present activities), history of the companies and their promoters (including names of natural persons controlling 15% or more voting rights or on the board if promoters are companies/bodies corporate), details of change in control in the preceding three years, and a declaration confirming submission of PANs, Bank Account Numbers, Company Registration Numbers, and Registrar of Companies addresses to stock exchanges are required.
*   **For Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) or Foreign Venture Capital Investors (FVCIs) as promoters:** Details of the Fund Manager, generic fund details, investor distribution (total, category-wise, percentage stake), details of funded companies (total, country-wise, holding period-wise, sector-wise, number under Fund control), and specific details for companies where shares were offered for lock-in (name, listing date, Fund's shareholding at listing and DRHP filing), average holding period, and sector focus are required.
*   If present promoters are not original and control was acquired in the preceding five years, details of acquisition (date, terms, consideration, compliance with SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, and SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015) must be provided.
*   If there is no identifiable promoter, details of shareholders controlling 15% or more voting rights or having director appointment rights must be disclosed.
*   If promoters lack experience in the proposed business, this fact and how activities will be managed must be disclosed.
*   Brief details of any other interests promoters have in the issuer, beyond their role as promoters, are required.
*   Full particulars of the nature and extent of interest of promoters, directors, or group companies in the issuer's promotion, any property acquired/proposed in the preceding three years, or transactions involving land acquisition, building construction, and machinery supply must be disclosed. This includes details if the interest is through a firm or company, with sums paid or agreed to be paid.
*   Any non-salary related amount or benefit paid or intended to be paid to any promoter or promoter group in the preceding two years, along with the consideration, must be disclosed.
*   Brief details of material guarantees given to third parties by promoters regarding the issuer's specified securities are required.
*   A list of all individuals and entities forming part of the promoter group must be provided.
*   If promoters disassociated from any companies or firms in the preceding three years, reasons, circumstances, and terms of disassociation must be disclosed.

**Regarding Dividend Policy:**
*   The dividend policy, mode of payment, details of dividends paid in the last three financial years and any stub period, and the period between the last audited period and the filing date of the draft offer document/offer document must be disclosed.

**Regarding Financial Statements (Indian Accounting Standards - Ind AS):**
*   The financial information section of the offer document must be divided into restated financial information and other financial information, both complete.
*   **Restated Financial Information:**
    *   Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) prepared in accordance with Ind AS for three years and any applicable stub period must be audited and certified by statutory auditor(s) or Chartered Accountants holding a valid certificate from the Peer Review Board of ICAI.
    *   A stub period CFS is required if the latest full financial year Ind AS CFS is older than six months from the filing date, and the stub period should not end earlier than six months from the filing date.
    *   CFS must be restated for consistency in presentation, disclosures, and accounting policies across all periods, aligning with the latest financial year/stub period. Significant errors, non-provisions, regrouping, and other adjustments must be reflected. Changes in accounting policies and error corrections must be disclosed per Ind AS 8.
    *   Quantifiable audit modifications must be adjusted in the restated financial information; unquantifiable ones require appropriate disclosures in notes.
    *   A reconciliation explaining differences between audited CFS equity and profit (loss) and the restated CFS must be presented in a columnar format.

This document outlines various requirements for financial reporting and disclosures, particularly concerning restated financial information, auditor responsibilities, and specific conditions for consolidated and acquired entities.

**Auditor Requirements:**
An auditor or Chartered Accountant must issue an examination report on restated and audited financial information, adhering to the Guidance Note issued by the ICAI. The auditor must possess a valid peer review certificate from the ICAI's Peer Review Board as of the date of signing the restated financial information. If a new auditor with a valid certificate is appointed for a stub period and the predecessor lacked one for the last annual financial statement, the last annual financial statement must be re-audited by the new auditor, potentially excluding CARO, internal financial control, and other pure regulatory matters. An earlier peer review certificate remains valid if renewal was initiated and not expressly refused by the board, even if not valid at the signing date of restated information.

**Financial Statement Presentation and Disclosure:**
If an issuer has no subsidiary, associate, or joint venture in a financial year, it must present separate financial statements for that year, following restated CFS requirements. The restated financial information must disclose a list of related parties and all related party transactions of consolidated entities (whether eliminated or not), as required by Ind AS 24 and/or Section 188(2) of the Companies Act, 2013. All funding arrangements, including inter-se guarantees among consolidated entities (excluding equity share capital contributions), along with their important terms, conditions, and fund transfer restrictions, must also be disclosed in the restated financial information. For companies not subject to Ind AS, principles from SEBI Circular No SEBI/HO/CFD/DIL/CIR/P/2016/47 of March 31, 2016, or other relevant Board circulars apply.

**Availability of Financial Statements:**
Separate audited financial statements for the past three full financial years immediately preceding the offer document filing date for the issuer and all its material subsidiaries must be available on the issuer's website, or relevant links provided. The link to the issuer's separate financial statement must be specified in the offer document. Subsidiaries are identified per the Companies Act, 2013, and these requirements apply for the duration of the parent-subsidiary relationship.

**Foreign Entities and Materiality:**
For consolidated entities whose financial statements are not in English, a certified English translated copy must be available on the company's website. Financial statements in non-Indian Rupee currency must be translated into Indian Rupee according to Ind AS 21. Foreign consolidated entities' financial statements must be audited unless they are not material to the CFS and local regulations do not mandate an audit. An entity is 'material' if it contributes 10% or more to turnover, net-worth, or profits before tax in the annual CFS. Total unaudited information in the CFS cannot exceed 20% of turnover, net-worth, or profits before tax. Foreign entities' financial statements may be audited as per local regulations, or by Indian auditing standards if local law doesn't mandate an audit. Foreign subsidiaries' financial statements may be acceptable in a GAAP other than Ind AS if local laws require it.

**Other Financial Information and Acquisitions/Divestments:**
Other financial information, including Earnings per share (Basic and Diluted), Return on net worth, Net Asset Value per share, and EBITDA, must be computed as per ICAI Guidance Note and disclosed.

If issue proceeds are used for acquiring material businesses or entities (contributing 20% or more to turnover, net worth, or profit before tax in the latest annual CFS), audited balance sheets, profit and loss, and cash flow statements for the latest three financial years and stub period (if available) must be included in the offer document, prepared as per the applicable framework. Issuers may voluntarily provide these statements for acquisitions below the materiality threshold or provide proforma financial statements to show acquisition impact, prepared per ICAI guidance/standards/guidelines and certified by a statutory auditor or a chartered accountant with a valid Peer Review Board certificate. If general purpose financial statements are unavailable for acquired/divested businesses, combined/carved-out financial statements must be prepared according to ICAI guidance/standards/guidelines and audited by the seller's auditor.

Proforma financial statements, certified by a statutory auditor or a chartered accountant with a valid Peer Review Board certificate, are required for material subsidiaries or businesses (contributing 20% or more to turnover, net worth, or profit before tax in the latest annual CFS) acquired or divested after the latest disclosed financial information but before the offer document filing date. These proforma statements, prepared for at least the last completed financial year and stub period (if any) according to ICAI guidance/standards/guidelines, can also be voluntarily provided for acquisitions/divestments below the materiality threshold or completed prior to the latest disclosed financial information.

This document outlines requirements for financial disclosures, particularly concerning acquisitions, divestments, and the presentation of financial statements in an offer document.

**I. Acquisitions and Divestments:**
*   For one or more acquisitions or divestments, a single combined set of Proforma financial statements must be presented.
*   If the acquired/divested businesses are not separate entities, combined/carved-out financial statements must be prepared according to ICAI Guidance Notes, Standards on Assurance Engagements, or guidelines.
*   Disclosures for non-material acquisitions/divestments (fact, consideration, financing mode) must be certified by the issuer company's statutory auditor or a Chartered Accountant (CA) holding a valid certificate from the ICAI Peer Review Board, appointed by the issuer.
*   The issuer may voluntarily include certified financial statements of the acquired/divested business or subsidiary, certified by its auditor or an ICAI Peer Review Board certified CA.

**II. Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A):**
*   MD&A of Financial Position and Results of Operations, based on restated Ind AS Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS), must be provided.
*   It must include:
    *   A statement by directors on significant developments since the last financial year/stub period, addressing any circumstances materially and adversely affecting or likely to affect within 12 months: the issuer's trading/profitability, asset value, or ability to pay liabilities.
    *   Factors that may affect results of operations.
    *   Discussion on results of operations, including:
        *   Summary of past financial results (after adjustments) for the last three full financial years and stub period, detailing significant income/expenditure.
        *   Summary of major income/expenditure for the last three years and most recent audit period.
        *   Income and sales by major product/main activities.
        *   Break-up and nature (recurring/non-recurring) of other income if it exceeds 10% of total income.
        *   Disclosure of dependence on single/few customers/suppliers (including foreign ones) and impact of exchange rate fluctuations.
        *   Analysis and disclosure of impact if the issuer deviated from applicable accounting standards for sales/revenues.
        *   Nature of miscellaneous income/expenditure for interim and preceding years.
    *   Comparison of the last three years and stub period on major Profit & Loss statement heads, with analysis of reasons for changes in significant items, covering: unusual events/transactions, significant economic changes, known trends/uncertainties, expected future cost/revenue changes, reasons for sales/revenue increases (volume, new products, prices), turnover by major industry segment, status of new products/business segments, seasonality, dependence on suppliers/customers, and competitive conditions.
*   MD&A must be based on restated financial information for the last three years and the stub period.

**III. Capitalisation Statement:**
*   A Capitalisation Statement showing total borrowings, total equity, and borrowing/equity ratios before and after the issue must be incorporated.
*   It is prepared based on the restated CFS for the latest financial year or stub period.
*   Any change in share capital since the financial information disclosure date requires an explanatory note.
*   Terms like "Current borrowings," "Non-current borrowings," "Equity share capital," and "Other equity" carry meanings as per Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013.

**IV. Requirements for Indian GAAP in Restated Financial Information:**
*   The financial information section of the offer document is divided into restated and other financial information, both complete.
*   **Restated Financial Information:**
    *   Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) prepared in accordance with Indian GAAP for three years and a stub period (if applicable) must be audited and certified by statutory auditor(s) or CAs holding a valid ICAI Peer Review Board certificate.
    *   A stub period CFS is required if the latest full financial year Indian GAAP CFS is older than six months from the draft offer document/offer document filing date, and the stub period must not end earlier than six months of the offer document filing date.
    *   CFS must be prepared as per the Companies Act, 2013.
    *   CFS (including stub period) must be restated for consistency in presentation, disclosures, and accounting policies across all periods, aligning with the latest financial year/stub period. Significant errors, non-provisions, regrouping, and other adjustments must be reflected. Changes in estimates are not restated. Disclosures for error correction, accounting policy changes, and estimate changes must follow AS 5.
    *   Quantifiable or estimable audit modifications (qualified, adverse, or disclaimer opinions per SA 705) must be adjusted in the restated financial information. Non-quantifiable qualifications require appropriate disclosures in notes.
    *   A columnar reconciliation explaining differences between audited CFS equity/profit (loss) and restated CFS equity/profit (loss) must be presented.
    *   The auditor or CA must issue an examination report on the restated and audited financial information in accordance with ICAI Guidance Notes.
    *   The auditor must hold a valid ICAI Peer Review Board certificate on the date of signing the restated financial information. If a new auditor (with a valid certificate) is appointed for the stub period and the predecessor auditor lacked a valid certificate for the last annual financial statement, the last annual financial statement must be re-audited by the new auditor (excluding CARO, Internal Financial Control, and other pure regulatory matters). If an auditor previously held a valid certificate but not at the restated signing date, the earlier certificate is considered valid if there's no express refusal by the board and the renewal process was initiated.
    *   If an issuer has no subsidiary, associate, or joint venture in any financial year, it must present separate financial statements for that year following applicable restated CFS requirements.

This document outlines various financial disclosure requirements for restated financial information, offer documents, and other financial reporting.

**Restated Financial Information Disclosures:**
*   Must include a list of all related parties and their transactions for consolidated entities (whether eliminated or not), as required by AS 18 and/or Section 188(2) of the Companies Act, 2013, and as disclosed in separate financial statements.
*   All funding arrangements, including inter-se guarantees among consolidated entities (excluding equity share capital contributions), must be disclosed, along with their important terms, conditions, and any fund transfer restrictions.
*   Disclosures as per AS 13 and AS 14 are required, based on amounts recognized and measured under Indian GAAP and ICAI Guidance Notes.

**Separate Audited Financial Statements:**
*   The issuer company and its material subsidiaries must make their separate audited financial statements for the three full financial years immediately preceding the offer document filing date available on the issuer’s website. Subsidiaries are identified by the Companies Act, 2013 definitions, and this applies for the duration of the parent-subsidiary relationship.
*   A certified English translation of financial statements must be available on the company’s website for any consolidated entity whose statements are not in English.
*   Financial statements reported in currencies other than Indian Rupee must be translated into Indian Rupee according to Ind AS 21.
*   Financial statements of all foreign consolidated entities must be audited, unless they are not material to the Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) and local regulations do not mandate an audit. A consolidated entity is considered 'material' if it contributes 10% or more to turnover, net-worth, or profits before tax in the annual CFS. The total unaudited CFS cannot exceed 20% of the turnover, net-worth, or profits before tax of the CFS.
*   Audits for foreign entities may follow local regulations; if local law does not mandate an audit, Indian auditing standards apply. Foreign GAAP may be acceptable if required by local laws.

**Other Financial Information:**
*   The following must be computed as per ICAI Guidance Notes and disclosed: Earnings per share (Basic and Diluted), Return on net worth, Net Asset Value per share, and EBITDA.

**Acquisitions and Divestments:**
*   If issue proceeds are used for material acquisitions (contributing 20% or more to turnover, net worth, or profit before tax in the latest annual CFS), audited balance sheets, profit and loss, and cash flow statements for the latest three financial years and stub period of the acquired business/entity must be included. Voluntary disclosure for non-material acquisitions is permitted.
*   Proforma financial statements may be voluntarily provided to disclose the impact of such acquisitions, prepared as per ICAI guidance/standards and certified by a statutory auditor or an ICAI Peer Review Board certified Chartered Accountant (CA).
*   For material acquisitions or divestments (contributing 20% or more to turnover, net worth, or profit before tax in the latest annual CFS) occurring after the latest disclosed financial information but before the offer document filing, proforma financial statements are mandatory. These must cover at least the last completed financial year and stub period, be prepared as per ICAI guidance/standards, and certified by a statutory auditor or an ICAI Peer Review Board certified CA. Voluntary proforma statements are allowed for non-material or earlier transactions.
*   If general purpose financial statements are unavailable for acquired/divested businesses, combined/carved-out financial statements must be prepared as per ICAI guidance/standards and audited by the seller's auditor (for acquisitions using proceeds) or certified by the issuer's auditor/ICAI Peer Review Board certified CA (for proforma statements).
*   For non-material acquisitions/divestments, disclosures regarding the fact, consideration paid/received, and mode of financing must be certified by the issuer's statutory auditor or an ICAI Peer Review Board certified CA.

**Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A):**
*   MD&A of Financial Position and Results of Operations, based on restated Indian GAAP CFS, must be provided.
*   This includes a statement from directors on any significant adverse developments since the last financial statements that could affect trading/profitability, asset value, or ability to pay liabilities within 12 months.
*   Discussion on factors affecting operations and results of operations, including a summary of past financial results (three years and stub period) with significant income/expenditure, major income/expenditure items, income/sales by major product/activity, break-up of other income if over 10% of total income, dependence on major customers/suppliers (including foreign ones and exchange rate impact), analysis of deviations from statutory sales/revenue recording, and nature of miscellaneous income/expenditure.
*   A comparison of the last three years and stub period on major P&L heads, analyzing reasons for changes in significant items, including unusual events, accounting policy changes, and significant economic changes.
