Convertible debt instruments cannot finance, provide loans to, or acquire shares of promoter group or group companies, unless fully convertible with a conversion period less than eighteen months.

**Issue of Warrants (Regulation 13):** Warrants can be issued with a tenure not exceeding eighteen months, requiring upfront payment of at least 25% of the exercise price, with forfeiture for non-exercise.

**Minimum Promoters’ Contribution (Regulation 14):** Promoters must hold at least 20% of the post-issue capital. Shortfalls can be met by specific entities (AIFs, FVCIs, banks, PFIs, insurance companies, non-individual public shareholders >5%, promoter group entities other than promoters) up to 10% of post-issue capital. This contribution can be in equity shares or convertible securities, with specific pricing and timing requirements. The amount for promoters' contribution must be kept in an escrow account.

**Securities Ineligible for Minimum Promoters’ Contribution (Regulation 15):** Generally, securities acquired for non-cash consideration involving revaluation, bonus issues from revaluation reserves, or those acquired by promoters/specified entities in the preceding one year at a price lower than the IPO price are ineligible (with exceptions for price difference payment, court-approved schemes, government companies, and conversion of fully paid-up compulsorily convertible securities). Securities from partnership/LLP conversions (unless capital existed for over one year) and pledged securities are also ineligible.

**Lock-in of Specified Securities (Regulations 16-22):**
*   **Promoters' Minimum Contribution:** Locked-in for eighteen months (or three years if majority issue proceeds are for capital expenditure).
*   **Promoters' Excess Holding:** Locked-in for six months (or one year for capital expenditure).
*   **SR Equity Shares:** Locked-in until conversion or the specified period, whichever is later.
*   **Pre-issue Capital (Non-Promoters):** Locked-in for six months, with exemptions for employee shares and shares held by venture capital funds/AIFs/FVCIs (which have a six-month lock-in from purchase date).
*   Locked-in securities are non-transferable (certificates bear "non-transferable" inscription, depositories record lock-in) but promoters' locked-in securities (excluding SR equity shares) can be pledged as collateral for specific loans, with the lock-in continuing for the transferee upon invocation. Locked-in securities can be transferred to other promoters/promoter group members or other persons holding locked-in securities, but the lock-in continues for the transferee.

**Appointment of Intermediaries and Compliance Officer (Regulation 23):** The issuer must appoint one or more SEBI-registered merchant bankers as lead manager(s) (at least one non-associate), other SEBI-registered intermediaries, a SEBI-registered registrar to the issue, and a qualified company secretary as compliance officer.

**Disclosures in and Filing of Offer Documents (Regulations 24-26):** Draft and final offer documents must contain true, adequate, and not more than six-month-old material disclosures. Lead manager(s) must exercise due diligence. Three copies of the draft offer document are filed with SEBI through lead manager(s), along with fees and due diligence certificates. SEBI may issue observations within thirty days. The draft offer document must be made public for comments for at least twenty-one days on websites and through public announcements in newspapers.

**Pricing (Regulations 27-30):** The face value, price band, or issue price must be disclosed prominently. The issuer determines the price in consultation with lead manager(s) or via book building. For book-built issues, the cap on the price band must be 105-120% of the floor price, and the floor/final price not less than face value. The floor price or price band must be announced at least two working days before issue opening. Differential pricing allows up to a 10% discount for retail individual investors, retail individual shareholders, or employees (excluding anchor investors).

**Issuance Conditions and Procedure (Regulations 31-39):** The minimum offer to the public is subject to the Securities Contracts (Regulations) Rules, 1957.
*   **Book Building (Regulation 6(1)):** Not less than 35% of the net offer to retail individual investors, not less than 15% to non-institutional investors, and not more than 50% to QIBs (with 5% for mutual funds). Up to 60% of the QIB portion can go to anchor investors. Non-institutional investor portion is split into one-third for applications between ₹2-10 lakh and two-thirds for over ₹10 lakh (effective 01.04.2022/01.07.2022 for large issues).
*   **Book Building (Regulation 6(2)):** Not more than 10% to retail individual investors, not more than 15% to non-institutional investors, and not less than 75% to QIBs (with 5% for mutual funds).
*   **Non-Book Building:** Minimum 50% to retail individual investors.
Reservations are permitted for employees (up to 5% of post-issue capital, individual allotment up to two lakh rupees, or five lakh rupees for under-subscription) and shareholders (up to 10% of issue size). Abridged prospectuses must accompany application forms. Bids must use the ASBA facility. Grading from credit rating agencies is optional.
**Underwriting:** For non-book built issues, underwriting agreements must be in place before filing the prospectus. For book-built issues, lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s) underwrite the issue, but at least 75% of the net offer compulsorily allotted to QIBs for eligibility cannot be underwritten. Underwriting obligations must cover at least the minimum subscription. Regulation 38, concerning security deposits, was omitted w.e.f. May 18, 2024.

This document outlines regulations for Initial Public Offers (IPOs) and Rights Issues, including various amendments.

**I. Initial Public Offers (IPOs)**

*   **Underwriting:**
    *   **Non-Book Building:** Issuer must have an underwriting agreement with SEBI-registered merchant bankers or stock brokers before filing the prospectus, specifying subscription for rejected applications at not less than the issue price. This must be disclosed.
    *   **Book Building:** Underwritten by lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s), but at least 75% of the net offer to Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) is not underwritten. An agreement detailing subscription for rejected bids (at not less than issue price) must be made before prospectus filing and disclosed. If underwriting for under-subscription is desired, an agreement must be made before Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) filing and disclosed. Lead manager(s) must fulfill syndicate members' obligations if they fail. Lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s) can only subscribe to fulfill underwriting obligations. Lead manager(s) have minimum underwriting obligations, and overall obligations must cover minimum subscription.
*   **Monitoring Agency (Regulation 41):** Required if issue size (excluding offer for sale) exceeds ₹100 crore (not for banks, public financial institutions, or insurance companies). A SEBI-registered credit rating agency monitors the use of proceeds, submitting quarterly reports until 100% of proceeds are utilized. The issuer's board and management must comment on findings, and the report must be publicly disseminated on the issuer's website and submitted to stock exchange(s) within 45 days from the end of each quarter.
*   **Public Communications, Advertisements, and Research Reports (Regulation 42, 43):** Must comply with Schedule IX. A pre-issue and price band advertisement is required after RHP/prospectus filing, in specified newspapers, following Schedule X. No advertisements implying full/oversubscription or indicating investor response are permitted during the subscription period.
*   **Issue Opening (Regulation 44):** A public issue may open within twelve months from the Board's observations and at least three working days after filing the RHP/prospectus with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
*   **Minimum Subscription (Regulation 45):** Must be at least 90% of the offer (excluding offer for sale). If not met, all application monies must be refunded forthwith, no later than four days from issue closure.
*   **Subscription Period (Regulation 46):** At least three working days and not more than ten working days. If the price band is revised, the bidding period must be extended for a minimum of three working days. Extensions for force majeure are possible for a minimum of one working day.
*   **Application and Minimum Application Value (Regulation 47):** A person cannot apply for more than the total securities offered to the public in the net offer category. Non-institutional investors' maximum application is capped. The minimum application value must be between ₹10,000 and ₹15,000, with applications in multiples. The minimum sum payable on application is 25% of the issue price (full price for offer for sale).
*   **Manner of Calls (Regulation 48):** Outstanding subscription money must be called within twelve months of allotment. Failure to pay results in forfeiture of shares/money, unless a monitoring agency is appointed.
*   **Allotment Procedure (Regulation 49):** Allotment cannot be made if prospective allottees are less than one thousand, and cannot exceed offered securities (except for 1% rounding off). Allotment to non-retail, non-institutional, and anchor investors is proportionate. Value of specified securities allotted under specific reservations is capped (₹2 lakh for retail, ₹5 lakh for eligible employees). Retail investors receive at least the minimum bid lot, then proportionately. Non-institutional investors (w.e.f. 1.4.2022/1.7.2022) receive at least the minimum application size, then proportionately. The basis of allotment is finalized fairly by authorized employees of the designated stock exchange, lead manager(s), and registrars.
*   **Allotment, Refund, and Interest (Regulation 50):** Issuer and lead manager(s) must ensure allotment/refund/unblocking within the Board-specified period. If not completed, the issuer must pay 15% per annum interest.
*   **Post-Issue Advertisements (Regulation 51):** Lead manager(s) must release an advertisement within ten days of completion of activities, detailing subscription, allotment basis, application statistics, refunds, credit of securities, and listing application date. This must be published in specified national and regional newspapers and on stock exchange websites.
*   **Post-Issue Responsibilities of Lead Manager(s) (Regulation 52):** Lead manager(s) remain responsible until the issue process is complete, investor grievances are redressed, applicants receive securities/credit/refund, and listing/trading permission is obtained. They coordinate with intermediaries and report omissions/commissions to the Board.
*   **Release of Subscription Money (Regulation 53):** Lead manager(s) confirm to bankers for money release or refund. If listing/trading permission is not obtained, the issuer must refund all monies within four days (w.e.f. 14.1.2022) of rejection intimation. Failure to repay within this period incurs 15% per annum interest from the fifth day (w.e.f. 14.1.2022), with the issuer and defaulting directors jointly and severally liable.
*   **Reporting of Transactions (Regulation 54):** The issuer must ensure all security transactions by promoters and the promoter group between the filing of the draft offer document/offer document and issue closure are reported to stock exchange(s) within twenty-four hours. (This regulation was substituted w.e.f. 08.03.2025, with prior text provided).
*   **Post-Issue Reports (Regulation 55):** Lead manager(s) must submit a final post-issue report and a due diligence certificate within seven days of allotment basis finalization or refund if the issue fails.

**II. General Regulations & Amendments**

*   **Restrictions on Further Issue (Regulation 56):** An issuer cannot make further issues between draft offer document filing and listing/refund, except for employee stock option schemes or stock appreciation right schemes (w.e.f. 08.03.2025) with full disclosures.
*   **Price Stabilisation (Regulation 57):** Issuers may use a green shoe option (max 15% over-allotment) for price stabilization for up to thirty days post-listing. Requires shareholder authorization, a lead manager as stabilising agent, and agreements for borrowing securities from promoters/pre-issue shareholders. Specific disclosures, special accounts, and reporting to SEBI are mandated.
*   **Alteration of Rights (Regulation 58):** Terms of specified securities cannot be altered adversely without 3/4 written consent or a special resolution of holders.
*   **Exit Opportunity (Regulation 59):** Promoters/controlling shareholders must provide an exit offer to dissenting shareholders (as per Companies Act, 2013) for changes in objects or contract terms related to objects in the offer document, unless there are no identifiable promoters/controlling shareholders.
*   **Chapter IIA: IPO through Pre-filing (w.e.f. 21.11.2022):** Provides an alternative IPO process.
    *   **Pre-filing:** Issuer files a confidential draft offer document with the Board and stock exchanges.
    *   **Public Announcement:** Within two working days, a public announcement is made about the filing (without issue details).
    *   **Board Observations:** The Board may issue observations within thirty days.
    *   **Updated DRHP-I:** Issuer incorporates Board changes into an "updated draft red herring prospectus-I," which is made public for comments for at least twenty-one days.
    *   **Updated DRHP-II:** After public comments, an "updated draft red herring prospectus-II" is submitted before filing the final offer document with the RoC.
    *   **QIB Interaction (Reg 59D):** Limited marketing to QIBs is permitted from pre-filing until Board observations.
    *   **General Conditions (Reg 59E):** Outstanding convertible securities/rights must be converted and intimated to the Board before observations, with some exceptions (e.g., ESOPs, SARs).
    *   A public issue can open within eighteen months from the Board's observations if an updated DRHP-I is filed within sixteen months.

**III. Rights Issue**

*   **Eligibility (Regulation 60, 61, 62):**
    *   Conditions must be met at the time of filing the draft letter of offer (DLOO) with stock exchange(s) and the letter of offer (LOO) with the Board/stock exchange(s) (w.e.f. 08.04.2025).
    *   Ineligible if the issuer, promoters, promoter group, or directors are debarred by SEBI, or if equity shares are suspended from trading as a disciplinary measure (w.e.f. 08.04.2025).
    *   Must have in-principle listing approval, all partly paid-up shares fully paid or forfeited, and firm finance for 75% of project capital expenditures.
    *   General corporate purposes cannot exceed 25% of the amount raised. Combined general corporate purposes and unidentified acquisition/investment targets cannot exceed 35% (unidentified target max 25%) (w.e.f. 14.01.2022).
    *   If the issuer/promoter/director is a wilful defaulter/fraudulent borrower, promoters/promoter group cannot renounce rights (except within the group or to specific disclosed investors). SR shareholders cannot renounce rights, and SR shares remain locked-in until conversion.
*   **Convertible Debt Instruments (Regulation 63, 64, 65, 66):**
    *   Require a credit rating, appointment of a debenture trustee, and creation of a debenture redemption reserve.
    *   Secured instruments require sufficient, unencumbered assets.
    *   Roll-over of non-convertible portions (if >₹10 crore) requires 75% holder approval and redemption for non-consenting holders.
    *   Conversion of Optionally Convertible Debt Instruments (OCDIs) requires positive consent; holders must have an option not to convert if the conversion price wasn't determined at issue.
    *   Cannot be issued to finance/loan/acquire shares of promoter group/group companies, unless fully convertible and conversion period is less than eighteen months.
*   **Warrants (Regulation 67):** Tenure cannot exceed eighteen months. Exercise price/formula must be determined upfront and disclosed, with at least 25% of consideration received upfront. Consideration is forfeited if the option is not exercised within three months.
*   **Record Date (Regulation 68):** Issuer announces a record date. Withdrawal of a rights issue after announcing the record date makes the issuer ineligible for listing any specified securities for twelve months.
*   **Intermediaries (Regulation 69):** Issuer must appoint Board-registered intermediaries (e.g., bankers, registrars) and ensure agreements do not limit liabilities. Issuer cannot appoint itself as registrar.
*   **Disclosures and Filing (Regulation 70, 71, 72):** DLOO and LOO must contain material, true, and adequate disclosures (Part B of Schedule VI), with information not more than six months old. Disclose if the issuer/promoter/director is a "wilful defaulter or a fraudulent borrower." The issuer files DLOO with stock exchange(s) and LOO with stock exchanges/designated stock exchange and the Board (w.e.f. 08.04.2025). DLOO and LOO must be hosted on websites and match filed versions.
*   **Pricing (Regulation 73):** Issuer decides the issue price before the record date, in consultation with the designated stock exchange. The issue price cannot be less than the face value.
*   **Reservations (Regulation 74):** Equity shares must be reserved for holders of outstanding compulsorily convertible debt instruments, proportionate to their convertible part, issued on the same terms as the rights issue.
*   **ASBA (Regulation 76):** Applicants must apply through the ASBA facility.
*   **Availability and Despatch (Regulation 77):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) ensures LOO and issue materials are available with various entities. LOO and application forms must be despatched to existing shareholders at least three days before issue opening.
*   **Credit of Rights Entitlements (Regulation 77A):** Rights entitlements must be credited to demat accounts before issue opening, and allotment must be in dematerialized form.
*   **Allotment to Specific Investors (Regulation 77B, w.e.f. 08.04.2025):** Applications by specific investors must be made on the first day of issue opening before 11 A.M., with status disclosed by 11:30 A.M. No withdrawal is permitted for these applications.
*   **Plain Paper Applications (Regulation 78):** Shareholders not receiving forms can apply on plain paper, provided all required details are specified. Dual applications (form and plain paper) may be rejected.
*   **Underwriting (Regulation 81):** If desired, the issuer appoints SEBI-registered merchant bankers/stock brokers. Underwriting is limited to the entitlement of non-promoter shareholders. (Lead manager(s) minimum underwriting obligations omitted w.e.f. 08.04.2025).
*   **Monitoring Agency (Regulation 82):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) must arrange for a SEBI-registered credit rating agency to monitor the use of issue proceeds, submitting quarterly reports until 100% of proceeds *actually raised* (w.e.f. 28.09.2020) are utilized.
*   **Advertisement Requirements (Regulation 84):** An advertisement must be published at least two days (w.e.f. 2019) before issue opening in specified newspapers, disclosing despatch dates, centres for duplicate forms, plain paper application details, and specific investor details (w.e.f. 2025). No ads implying full/oversubscription during the subscription period. Issue closure announcement requires 90% subscription and registrar certificate.
*   **Issue Opening (Regulation 85):** A rights issue may be opened within such period as specified by the Board (substituted w.e.f. 2025).
*   **Minimum Subscription (Regulation 86):** At least 90% of the offer. Not applicable (w.e.f. 2020) if the issue's object is not financing capital expenditure and promoters/promoter group subscribe fully without renouncing (except within group or to specific investors (w.e.f. 2025)). If not met, refund within four days (w.e.f. 2022).
*   **Subscription Period (Regulation 87):** Open for a period specified by the Board (substituted w.e.f. 2025). No withdrawal after issue closing date (w.e.f. 2019).
*   **Payment Options (Regulation 88):** Part payment (at least 25% of issue price) with balance in calls, or full payment.
*   **Allotment Procedure (Regulation 90):** Allotment is made first to eligible shareholders and renouncees, then to shareholders applying for additional shares, then to renouncees applying for additional shares, and finally to specific investors (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) if an under-subscribed portion remains. The basis is finalized by designated stock exchange employees and registrars (lead manager(s) omitted w.e.f. 08.04.2025).
*   **Allotment, Refund, and Interest (Regulation 91):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) ensures allotment/refund/unblocking electronically within the Board-specified period. If not completed, the issuer pays 15% per annum interest.
*   **Post-Issue Advertisements (Regulation 92):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) releases an advertisement within ten days of completion, detailing subscription, allotment basis, refunds, credit of securities, and listing application date, published in specified newspapers and on stock exchange websites.
*   **Post-Issue Responsibilities (Regulation 93):** The designated stock exchange (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) monitors investor grievance redressal. The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) is responsible for post-issue activities until applicants receive demat credit/refund and listing/trading permission is obtained.
*   **Release of Subscription Money (Regulation 94):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) confirms to bankers for money release or refund. If listing/trading permission fails, the issuer must refund all monies within four days (w.e.f. 2022) of rejection intimation, or pay 15% interest from the fifth day (w.e.f. 2022).
*   **Reporting of Transactions (Regulation 95):** The issuer must report all security transactions by promoters and the promoter group between the filing of the draft letter of offer/letter of offer and issue closure to stock exchange(s) within twenty-four hours (prior to 2025 substitution).

This document outlines regulations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (ICDR) Regulations, 2018, incorporating amendments up to 2025, concerning capital issues, disclosure, and compliance.

**1. Reporting Requirements:**
*   **Promoters and Promoter Group Transactions:** The issuer must report all transactions in securities by promoters and the promoter group to stock exchange(s) within twenty-four hours, from the date of filing the draft letter of offer (or letter of offer) until the issue closure date.
*   **Pre-issue Placement:** Any proposed pre-issue placement disclosed in the draft letter of offer must be reported to stock exchange(s) within twenty-four hours of such transactions (in part or entirety).
*   **Post-issue Reports:** The issuer (substituted from "lead manager(s)" w.e.f. 08.04.2025) must submit an initial post-issue report (Part B of Schedule XVII) within three working days of issue closure, and a final post-issue report (Part C of Schedule XVII) within fifteen days of allotment finalization or refund if the issue fails.

**2. Restriction on Further Capital Issues:**
*   An issuer is prohibited from making any further issue of specified securities (public, rights, preferential, QIP, bonus shares) between the date of filing the draft letter of offer with the stock exchange(s) (substituted from "Board" w.e.f. 08.04.2025) and the listing of offered securities or refund of application monies.
*   **Exceptions:** This restriction does not apply to issues made pursuant to an employee stock option scheme or a stock appreciation right scheme (inserted w.e.f. 08.04.2025).
*   The restriction is also waived if full disclosures regarding the total number of specified securities or the amount to be raised are made in the draft letter of offer or letter of offer.

**3. Alteration of Rights of Holders of Specified Securities:**
*   An issuer cannot alter the terms of specified securities if it adversely affects holders' interests.
*   **Exceptions:** Alterations are permitted with written consent from holders of not less than three-fourths of that class of securities, or with a special resolution passed at a meeting of those holders.

**4. Fast Track Rights Issue:**
*   The entire Part IX, including Regulation 99 (Eligibility conditions) and Regulation 100 (Issue conditions) for fast track rights issues, was omitted by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, effective 08.04.2025.

**5. Further Public Offer (FPO) - Chapter IV:**
*   **Reference Date (Reg 101):** Conditions must be met as of the date of filing the draft offer document with the Board and filing the offer document with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
*   **Ineligibility (Reg 102):** An issuer is ineligible if the issuer, its promoters, promoter group, directors, or selling shareholders are debarred by the Board (unless debarment period concluded), or if any promoter/director is a promoter/director of another debarred company, or if the issuer/promoter/director is a wilful defaulter/fraudulent borrower, or a fugitive economic offender.
*   **Eligibility (Reg 103):** An issuer is eligible if it has not changed its name in the last one year immediately preceding the filing date, OR if it has, at least 50% of its revenue for the preceding full year must be from the new name's activity. If this isn't met, an FPO is still possible via book-building, with an undertaking to allot at least 75% of the net offer to Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs), refunding if this fails.
*   **General Conditions (Reg 104):**
    *   Application for in-principle listing approval on one or more stock exchanges.
    *   Agreement with a depository for dematerialization.
    *   All existing partly paid-up equity shares are fully paid-up or forfeited.
    *   Firm finance arrangements (verifiable) for 75% of stated means of finance for the specific project (capital expenditures only), excluding public issue proceeds or existing internal accruals.
    *   **Fund Utilization Limits:** Amount for general corporate purposes and objects without an identified acquisition/investment target shall not exceed 35% of the amount raised. Within this, the amount for objects without an identified acquisition/investment target shall not exceed 25% of the amount raised. These limits do not apply if the acquisition/investment target is identified and disclosed.
*   **Offer for Sale (Reg 105):** Only fully paid-up equity shares held by selling shareholder(s) for at least one year prior to filing the draft offer document may be offered. Combined holding period for convertible securities and resultant equity shares counts.
    *   **Exemptions to one-year holding:** Offer for sale by government companies/SPVs in infrastructure, equity shares from court/tribunal/Central Government approved schemes (business/invested capital > 1 year), bonus shares from free reserves/share premium (not revaluation/unrealized profits) on securities held for at least one year.
*   **FPO of Convertible Debt Instruments (Reg 106 & 107):**
    *   **Eligibility:** Issuer's equity shares must be listed, and no default in interest/principal payment for public debt instruments for over six months.
    *   **Requirements:** Credit rating, debenture trustee, debenture redemption reserve. If secured: sufficient, unencumbered assets; consent for second/pari passu charge; security cover calculated after reducing prior charges. Redemption as per offer document.
*   **Roll Over of Non-Convertible Portion (Reg 108):** Non-convertible portion of partly convertible debt instruments (> ₹10 crore) may be rolled over if 75% of holders (by value) approve via postal ballot, and an auditor's certificate on cash flow/liquidity is sent. A credit rating is required within one month before redemption due date.
*   **Conversion of Optionally Convertible Debt Instruments (Reg 109):** Cannot convert without positive consent. If convertible portion > ₹10 crore and conversion price not determined, holders must be given an option not to convert (unless upper limit/formula disclosed). If option not exercised, issuer must redeem within one month at not less than face value (unless offer document states otherwise).
*   **Issue of Convertible Debt Instruments for Financing (Reg 110):** Prohibited for financing/loaning to/acquiring shares of promoter group/group companies, unless fully convertible debt with conversion period < eighteen months.
*   **Issue of Warrants (Reg 111):** Warrants in FPO must have tenure <= eighteen months. Exercise price/formula set upfront, >= 25% consideration upfront. Consideration forfeited if option not exercised within three months.

**6. Promoters’ Contribution:**
*   **Minimum Promoters’ Contribution Not Applicable (Reg 112):** If no identifiable promoter, OR if equity shares frequently traded for >= 3 years, >= 95% investor complaints redressed, and compliant with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 for >= 3 years (board composition non-compliance acceptable if compliant at filing and disclosed). Excess subscription price determined by Regulation 164 or issue price, whichever is higher.
*   **Minimum Promoters’ Contribution (Reg 113):**
    *   **Public/Composite Issue:** 20% of proposed issue size or 20% of post-issue capital (excluding rights component for composite issues).
    *   **Convertible Securities Issue:** 20% via equity shares or subscription to convertible securities. If conversion price not predetermined, must be via convertible securities with an undertaking to subscribe to equity shares. If predetermined, price cannot be lower than weighted average.
    *   **Timing and Escrow:** Contribution satisfied at least one day before issue opening, held in escrow, released with issue proceeds. For FPO of partly paid shares > ₹100 crore, at least ₹100 crore before opening, remainder pro-rata.
    *   SR Equity Shares are eligible. Computation on post-issue expanded capital (assuming full conversion/exercise).
*   **Securities Ineligible (Reg 114):** Securities acquired in preceding three years for non-cash consideration involving revaluation/capitalization of intangibles, bonus issues from revaluation reserves/unrealized profits or against already ineligible shares, or pledged (unless for issuer/subsidiary borrowings). Exception: Securities from court/tribunal/Central Government approved schemes are eligible.

**7. Lock-in Periods for Promoters' Securities (Reg 115):**
*   **Minimum Promoters' Contribution:** 18 months from FPO allotment (reduced from 3 years). Exception: 3 years if majority of issue proceeds (excluding OFS) are for capital expenditure (includes civil work, fixed assets, land, building, plant/machinery, and repayment of existing loans for such capital expenditure w.e.f. 08.03.2025).
*   **Promoters' Holding in Excess of Minimum Contribution:** 6 months (reduced from 1 year). Exception: 1 year if majority proceeds for capital expenditure.
*   **SR Equity Shares:** Locked-in until conversion to equity shares with equivalent voting rights.
*   **Exceptions/Conditions:** Lock-in does not apply to securities lent for green shoe option (Reg 116), resumes after return. For partly-paid securities, lock-in ends 18 months after they become pari passu with public securities (Reg 117). Certificates inscribed "non-transferable" (Reg 118). Locked-in securities (excluding SR equity shares) can be pledged as collateral for loans from specific financial institutions for the issuer/subsidiary (Reg 119). Transferable to another promoter/group member/new promoter/controlling person, but lock-in continues for transferee (Reg 120).

**8. Appointment of Lead Managers, Other Intermediaries, and Compliance Officer (Reg 121):**
*   Issuer appoints one or more SEBI-registered merchant bankers as lead manager(s); at least one must not be an associate. Other SEBI-registered intermediaries appointed in consultation with lead manager(s). Agreements must be entered.
*   A SEBI-registered registrar with depository connectivity must be appointed.
*   A qualified company secretary must be appointed as compliance officer.

**9. Disclosures in and Filing of Offer Documents (Reg 122, 123, 124, 125):**
*   Draft and final offer documents must contain material, true, and adequate disclosures.
*   Lead manager(s) must exercise due diligence, ensuring veracity and adequacy of disclosures, and that financial statements are not more than six months old.
*   Issuer files three copies of the draft offer document with the Board through lead manager(s) (with fees and certificates), and with stock exchanges.
*   The Board may specify changes or issue observations within thirty days. Issuer/lead manager(s) incorporate changes and submit an updated draft before filing with RoC. Final offer documents filed simultaneously with Board, stock exchanges, and RoC.
*   Draft offer document must be made public for comments for at least twenty-one days (websites of issuer, Board, stock exchanges, lead manager(s)). Public announcement in newspapers within two working days.

**10. Pricing (Reg 126, 127, 128):**
*   Disclosures about face value and price band/issue price must be in identical font size.
*   Issuer determines price in consultation with lead manager(s) or via book-building.
*   For fixed-price issues, price/price band in offer document. For book-built, floor price/price band in red herring prospectus (RHP), final price before RoC prospectus.
*   Cap on price band <= 120% of floor price and >= 105% of floor price. Floor price/final price cannot be less than face value.
*   Floor price/price band announced at least two working days before bid opening.
*   **Differential Pricing:** Allowed. Retail individual investors, retail individual shareholders, or employees may be offered securities at a price not lower than by more than ten percent of the net offer price to other categories (excluding anchor investors). Anchor investor price not lower than others. Discount must be in rupee terms.

**11. Issuance Conditions and Procedure (Reg 129-136):**
*   **Allocation in Net Offer (Reg 129):**
    *   **Book Building (Reg 103(1)):** Not less than 35% to RII, not less than 15% to NII, not more than 50% to QIB (5% of QIB to MFs).
    *   **Book Building (Reg 103(2)):** Not more than 10% to RII, not more than 15% to NII, not less than 75% to QIB (5% of QIB to MFs).
    *   **Anchor Investors:** Up to 60% of QIB portion.
    *   **NII Sub-categories (w.e.f. 2022):** 1/3 of NII for applications > ₹2 lakh to ₹10 lakh; 2/3 for applications > ₹10 lakh.
    *   Unsubscribed portions may be allocated to other categories.
*   **Reservation on Competitive Basis (Reg 130):** May reserve for employees (<= 5% of post-issue capital, allotment <= ₹2 lakh, up to ₹5 lakh if undersubscribed) and shareholders (<= 10% of issue size). Prohibited for lead managers, registrar, syndicate, their promoters/directors/employees/group/associates.
*   **Abridged Prospectus (Reg 131):** Must accompany every application form.
*   **ASBA (Reg 132):** Bids must be accepted only using ASBA facility.
*   **Prohibition on Payment of Incentives (Reg 134):** No direct/indirect incentives for applications, except fees/commission.
*   **Underwriting (Reg 136):** For non-book building FPOs, if desired, agreement before filing prospectus. For book-built public issues, issue must be underwritten by lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s) (except for >= 75% net offer to QIBs). Agreement before filing prospectus/RHP. Underwriting obligations must cover minimum subscription.

**12. Monitoring Agency (Reg 137):**
*   If issue size (excluding OFS) exceeds ₹100 crore, issuer must appoint a SEBI-registered credit rating agency to monitor use of proceeds (not for banks, PFIs, insurance companies).
*   Agency submits quarterly reports to issuer, which are then publicly disseminated by the issuer within forty-five days.

**13. Public Communications and Advertisements (Reg 138, 139):**
*   All public communication must comply with Schedule IX.
*   Pre-issue and price band advertisements must be made after filing RHP/prospectus with RoC, in specified newspapers. No advertisements implying full or oversubscription during the subscription period.

**14. Opening of the Issue (Reg 140):**
*   A public issue may open within twelve months from Board observations. Must open at least three working days after filing RHP/prospectus with RoC.

**15. Minimum Subscription (Reg 141):**
*   Must be at least ninety percent of the offer (excluding OFS). If not met, all application monies refunded forthwith, no later than four days from issue closure.

**16. Period of Subscription (Reg 142):**
*   FPO must be open for at least three working days and not more than ten working days. Price band revision requires extending bidding by a minimum of three working days.

**17. Application and Minimum Application Value (Reg 143):**
*   Maximum application cannot exceed total offered to public in net offer.
*   Minimum application size (number of securities) corresponding to a value between ₹10,000 and ₹15,000. Applications in multiples of this value.
*   Minimum sum payable on application per specified security is at least twenty-five percent of the issue price (full price for OFS).

**18. Allotment and Post-Issue (Reg 144-151):**
*   **Manner of Calls (Reg 144):** Outstanding amount called within twelve months of allotment (not required if monitoring agency appointed). Failure to pay results in forfeiture.
*   **Allotment Procedure (Reg 145):** No allotment if less than one thousand prospective allottees. Allotment cannot exceed securities offered (except rounding off). Allotment (except RII, NII, anchor) on a proportionate basis. RII receive at least minimum bid lot, then proportionately. NII receive at least minimum application size, then proportionately. Basis finalized fairly by stock exchange, lead manager(s), and registrars.
*   **Allotment, Refund, Interest (Reg 146):** Allotment/refund/unblock within Board-specified period. If not, issuer pays 15% p.a. interest.
*   **Post-issue Advertisements (Reg 147):** Lead manager(s) release advertisements detailing subscription, allotment basis, statistics, refund/credit dates, and listing application within ten days of activity completion.
*   **Post-issue Responsibilities of Lead Manager(s) (Reg 148):** Remain responsible until issue process is complete, including investor grievance redressal and listing.
*   **Release of Subscription Money (Reg 149):** Lead manager(s) confirm formalities to bankers. If listing/trading permission denied, issuer must refund all monies within four days (substituted from "seven days" w.e.f. 14.01.2022) of intimation. Failure to repay makes issuer/directors jointly/severally liable for 15% p.a. interest from the expiry of the fourth day.
*   **Reporting of Transactions by Promoters and Promoter Group and other Pre-offer Transactions (Reg 150):** (Substituted w.e.f. 08.03.2025) Issuer ensures all transactions by promoters/promoter group (between filing draft/offer doc and issue closure) are reported to stock exchange(s) within twenty-four hours. Proposed pre-offer placement also reported within twenty-four hours.
*   **Post-issue Reports (Reg 151):** Lead manager(s) submit final post-issue report and due diligence certificate within seven days of allotment finalization or refund.

**19. Price Stabilisation through Green Shoe Option (Reg 153):**
*   Issuer may implement a green shoe option to stabilize post-listing price.
*   Requires shareholder authorization, lead manager as stabilising agent, agreement on terms before draft offer document, and agreement with promoters/pre-issue shareholders to borrow securities for over-allotment (<= 15% of issue size) before filing offer document.
*   Stabilisation period <= thirty days from trading permission. Special bank and DP accounts required.
*   Market-bought securities returned to lenders immediately (<= two working days after stabilisation). If shortfall, issuer allots at issue price to DP account within five days. Remaining monies in special bank account transferred to Investor Protection and Education Fund.
*   Stabilising agent submits daily reports to stock exchange and final report to Board (Schedule XV).

**20. Eligibility Conditions for Fast Track Further Public Offer (Reg 155):**
*   Certain sub-regulations of Reg 123 do not apply if the issuer meets conditions including: equity shares listed for >= 3 years, entire promoter group shareholding dematerialised, average market capitalization of public shareholding >= ₹1000 crore, high trading turnover, compliance with listing regulations for >= 3 years, >= 95% investor complaints redressed, no pending show-cause notices (excluding penalty proceedings) from the Board, disclosure of compliance with SEBI settlement orders, no trading suspension as disciplinary measure in last 3 years, no conflict of interest with lead manager(s), and restated financials for audit qualifications or appropriate disclosure.

**21. Post-listing Exit Opportunity for Dissenting Shareholders (Reg 157):**
*   In FPOs (including fast track), promoters or controlling shareholders must provide an exit offer to dissenting shareholders if there's a change in objects or variation in contract terms related to objects in the offer document, as per Companies Act, 2013. Not applicable if no identifiable promoters or controlling shareholders.

**22. Preferential Issue (Chapter V) (Reg 158, 159):**
*   **General Exemptions (Reg 158):** Chapter V provisions generally do not apply to preferential issues made pursuant to conversion of loans/options (Companies Act, 2013), court/tribunal/Central Government approved schemes (though pricing provisions may apply), Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP), rehabilitation schemes (BIFR), resolution plans (IBC Section 31) (except lock-in), equity shares allotted to certain financial institutions (except pricing/lock-in), or debt conversion as part of RBI debt restructuring (subject to specific conditions including RBI price guidelines, independent valuers, and a one-year lock-in).
*   **Issuers Ineligible (Reg 159):**
    *   **Share Sales:** Cannot make a preferential issue to any person who sold issuer's equity shares in the last 90 trading days (previously six months) preceding the relevant date (unless Board relaxation). Promoters/promoter group are ineligible if they sold/transferred shares in the last 90 trading days (unless inter-se transfer or pledge invocation by specific entities).
    *   **Failed Warrants:** Promoters/promoter group who previously subscribed to warrants but failed to exercise them are ineligible for one year from expiry/cancellation.
    *   **Legal Status:** Ineligible if any promoter/director is a fugitive economic offender.
    *   **Outstanding Dues:** Ineligible if the issuer has any outstanding dues to the Board, stock exchanges, or depositories (inserted w.e.f. 14.01.2022), unless these dues are subject to a pending appeal or proceeding.

This document, part of the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) 2018, details regulations for preferential issues, Qualified Institutions Placements (QIPs), Initial Public Offers (IPOs) of Indian Depository Receipts (IDRs), Rights Issues of IDRs, and IPOs by Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), incorporating amendments from 2022, 2023, and 2024.

**Part II: Conditions for Preferential Issue**

*   **Conditions (Reg 160):** A listed issuer must ensure allotted equity shares are fully paid, a special resolution is passed, proposed allottees hold dematerialised shares and have PANs (unless exempt) before applying for in-principle approval, and the issuer complies with continuous listing conditions. The in-principle approval application must be made on the same day the general meeting notice is sent.
*   **Relevant Date (Reg 161):** For equity shares, it's 30 days prior to the shareholder meeting (except for stressed assets under RBI/NCLT, where it's the approval date). For convertible securities, it's either the equity share date or 30 days prior to entitlement to apply for equity shares. If the date falls on a weekend/holiday, the preceding day is used.
*   **Tenure of Convertible Securities (Reg 162):** Cannot exceed 18 months from allotment. Equity shares upon conversion must be allotted within 15 days of exercise.
*   **Monitoring Agency (Reg 162A):** For issues exceeding ₹100 crore (excluding banks, public financial institutions, insurance companies), a SEBI-registered credit rating agency monitors proceeds. Quarterly reports are submitted to the issuer, uploaded on its website, and submitted to stock exchanges within 45 days from quarter-end, with board/management comments.

**Part III: Disclosures to Shareholders (Reg 163)**

Disclosures in the explanatory statement for the special resolution include: objects of issue, maximum securities, promoter/director/KMP/senior management intent to subscribe, shareholding pattern (before/after), issue timeframe, identity of ultimate beneficial owners (with exceptions for listed entities/MFs/banks/insurance companies), percentage of post-issue capital for allottees, change in control, and undertakings for price re-computation and lock-in if not paid. Disclosures for wilful defaulters/fraudulent borrowers (Schedule VI) are also required.

**Key Amendments (2022 & 2023)**

*   **2023 (w.e.f. 31.01.2023):** Amended disclosure requirements for intent to subscribe to include "senior management."
*   **2022 (w.e.f. 14.01.2022):**
    *   Omitted requirements for disclosing specific post-issue capital percentage and change in control, instead mandating disclosure of allottee status (promoter/non-promoter).
    *   Required a certificate from a "practicing company secretary" (replacing "statutory auditors") for compliance, to be placed before the general meeting and hosted on the issuer's website.
    *   Stipulated non-cash consideration for preferential issues must be a swap of shares based on an independent registered valuer's report.
    *   Required the special resolution to specify the relevant date for pricing equity shares from convertible securities.

**Pricing of Preferential Issues**

*   **Frequently Traded Shares (Reg 164):**
    *   **Listed ≥ 90 trading days:** Price not less than the higher of 90-day VWAP or 10-day VWAP preceding the relevant date.
    *   **Listed < 90 trading days:** Price not less than the higher of IPO price/scheme value, average VWAP during listing, or 10-day VWAP (2 weeks). Recomputation required after 90 trading days, with allottees paying any difference.
    *   **To Qualified Institutional Buyers (max 5):** Price not less than 10-day VWAP.
    *   **General Proviso:** If Articles of Association provide a higher floor price, that applies.
*   **Allotment Restrictions (Reg 324(b)):** No allotment to QIBs who are promoters or related to promoters (defined by shareholder/voting rights, veto rights, nominee director rights, excluding lenders without shares).
*   **Definition of Frequently Traded Shares (Reg 324(5)):** Traded turnover on the highest volume stock exchange (preceding 90 days) is at least 10% of total shares during the 240 trading days preceding the relevant date.
*   **Stressed Assets (Reg 164A, w.e.f. 22.06.2020):**
    *   **Pricing:** Not less than 10-day VWAP.
    *   **Allotment Criteria:** Issuer meets two of: 90-day default on loans/debt, Inter-creditor agreement (RBI 2019), or credit rating downgraded to "D."
    *   **Issuer Conditions:** Issue to non-promoter/group. Prohibited allottees include insolvents, wilful defaulters, debarred persons, fugitive economic offenders, and those convicted for certain offenses (with exceptions).
    *   **Resolution:** Public category votes in favor must exceed votes against (3x if no identifiable promoter).
    *   **Use of Proceeds:** Not for repayment of promoter/group loans.
    *   **Monitoring:** SEBI-registered credit rating agency (quarterly reports) and Audit Committee.
    *   **Lock-in:** 3 years from trading approval.
    *   **Certification:** Statutory auditor and audit committee certify compliance at notice dispatch and allotment.
*   **Optional Pricing (Reg 164B, w.e.f. 01.07.2020 to 31.12.2020):** For frequently traded shares, price not less than the higher of 12-week or 2-week average of weekly high/low VWAP. 3-year lock-in.
*   **Infrequently Traded Shares (Reg 165):** Issuer determines price using valuation parameters (book value, multiples), with a compliance certificate from an independent registered valuer.
*   **Adjustments in Pricing (Reg 166):** Prices are adjusted for corporate actions like bonus issues, rights issues, stock splits, demergers, re-classification, or other similar events. Material price movement effects may be excluded.
*   **Other Conditions for Pricing (Reg 166A, w.e.f. 14.01.2022):**
    *   **Change in Control / >5% Post-Issue Capital:** Requires an independent registered valuer's report. Floor price is the higher of Reg 164 floor, valuer's price, or AOA price. Report published on website.
    *   **Change in Control:** Requires a reasoned recommendation from a committee of independent directors (all must attend), with voting pattern disclosed.

**Lock-in and Restrictions on Transferability**

*   **Lock-in (Reg 167, amended w.e.f. 14.01.2022):**
    *   **Promoters/Promoter Group:** Specified securities/equity from warrants locked-in for 18 months. Not more than 20% of total capital locked-in for 18 months; excess for 6 months. Unlisted convertible securities/warrants for 1 year.
    *   **Others:** Specified securities/equity from warrants locked-in for 6 months. Unlisted convertible securities/warrants for 1 year.
    *   **Convertible Securities:** Lock-in reduced by prior lock-in period.
    *   **Stressed Assets:** 1 year lock-in (exception for achieving 10% public shareholding).
    *   **Re-calculated Price:** Shares remain locked-in until any re-calculated price difference is paid.
    *   **Pre-preferential Allotment Shareholding:** Locked-in for 90 trading days.
    *   **New Promoters:** Same lock-in as promoters.
*   **Pledge of Locked-in Securities (Reg 167A, w.e.f. 14.01.2022):** Promoters can pledge locked-in securities (excluding SR equity) as collateral for loans to the issuer/subsidiary from specific financial institutions, provided it's a loan condition and the lock-in continues upon invocation.
*   **Transferability (Reg 168):** Locked-in securities can be transferred among promoters/group/new promoter, but lock-in continues. Not transferable until trading approval.
*   **Payment of Consideration (Reg 169):** Full consideration at allotment (except non-cash/stressed assets). Warrants: 25% at allotment, 75% on exercise (forfeited if not exercised). Cash from allottee's bank account, certified by statutory auditor.
*   **Allotment (Reg 170):** Within 15 days of special resolution (exceptions for regulatory approvals/takeover/stressed assets). Fresh resolution if delayed. All allotments must be in dematerialised form.

**CHAPTER VI – QUALIFIED INSTITUTIONS PLACEMENT (QIP)**

*   **Definitions (Reg 171):** "Eligible securities" include equity, non-convertible debt with warrants, convertible securities (excluding warrants). "Relevant date" is board/committee decision to open issue or entitlement date for equity.
*   **Eligibility (Reg 172):** Special resolution (exceptions for minimum public shareholding), equity listed for ≥1 year (exceptions for transferee companies/minimum public shareholding), no fugitive promoters/directors. Allotment within 365 days. Subsequent QIPs require a 2-week gap.
*   **Offer for Sale by Promoters (Reg 173):** For minimum public shareholding. Promoters restricted from buying/selling issuer shares 12 weeks before/after issue (exceptions for stock exchange sales with 2-week gap).
*   **Monitoring Agency (Reg 173A, w.e.f. 14.01.2022):** Same as Reg 162A for issues >₹100 crore (excluding OFS, banks, PFIs, insurance).
*   **Lead Managers (Reg 174):** SEBI-registered merchant bankers. At least one non-associate (if associate, limited to marketing). Due diligence certificate and preliminary placement document required.
*   **Placement Document (Reg 175):** Contains material information, Schedule VII disclosures (e.g., wilful defaulters), serially numbered, circulated to select investors, hosted on stock exchange/issuer websites with disclaimer.
*   **Pricing (Reg 176):** Not less than average of 2-week weekly high/low closing prices. Up to 5% discount with shareholder approval (unless promoter OFS). Subject to adjustments for corporate actions.
*   **Tenure of Convertible Securities (Reg 177):** Max 60 months.
*   **Transferability (Reg 178):** Allotted securities cannot be sold for 1 year (except on a recognized stock exchange).
*   **Application and Allotment (Reg 179):** No withdrawal/downward revision of bids. Minimum 10% to mutual funds. No allotment to promoter/related QIB (unless lender not holding shares).
*   **Minimum Allottees (Reg 180):** At least 2 for issues ≤₹250 crore, 5 for >₹250 crore. No single allottee >50%. Group/control definitions apply.

**CHAPTER VII – INITIAL PUBLIC OFFER OF INDIAN DEPOSITORY RECEIPTS (IDRs)**

*   **Applicability (Reg 181), Reference Date (Reg 182).**
*   **Eligibility (Reg 183):** Issuer listed in home country for ≥3 years, no regulatory prohibition, compliance track record, no fugitive promoters/directors. Issue size ≥₹50 crore, one IDR denomination, underlying shares listed/pari passu. Issuer ensures in-principle listing, depository agreement, 75% finance.
*   **Funding and Use of Proceeds (Reg 184):** Stated means of finance must be made. Max 25% for general corporate purposes.
*   **Intermediaries (Reg 185):** Lead manager(s) (at least one non-associate), registrar, overseas custodian bank, domestic depository, compliance officer, collection arrangements.
*   **Offer Documents (Reg 186):** True/correct/adequate disclosures (Part A Schedule VIII). Lead manager(s) due diligence. Filing draft with SEBI, then offer document with RoC, with certificates.
*   **Public Availability (Reg 187):** Draft public for 21 days for comments, public announcement in newspapers, hosted on websites.
*   **Pricing (Reg 188):** Determined in consultation with lead manager(s) or through book-building. Price band cap 120% of floor, not less than face value. Floor price/band announced 2 working days before issue opening.
*   **Differential Pricing (Reg 189):** Retail individual investors/employees may get up to 10% discount.
*   **Issuance Conditions and Procedure (Reg 190):** Minimum application ₹20,000. Allocation: ≥50% to QIBs (proportionate), rest to non-institutional/retail (discretion). ≥30% to retail (spillover allowed). Max application not exceeding total offered.
*   **Other Provisions (Reg 191-197):** Abridged prospectus (Part B Schedule VIII), ASBA facility, availability of issue material, no incentives. Reg 197 (security deposit) omitted.
*   **Underwriting (Reg 198):** Required for non-book-built issues. Lead manager(s) and syndicate members underwrite book-built issues, responsible for minimum subscription.
*   **Public Communications (Reg 199):** Must comply with Schedule IX.
*   **Issue-related Advertisements (Reg 200):** Opening/closing ads (Schedule X). No oversubscription claims during subscription.
*   **Opening of the Issue (Reg 201):** Within 12 months of SEBI observations, at least 3 working days after RoC filing.
*   **Minimum Subscription (Reg 202):** At least 90% of offer. If not met, full refund within 4 days, with 15% p.a. interest for delay. Lead manager(s) report underwriter failures.
*   **Period of Subscription (Reg 203):** 3 to 10 working days. Extensions for price band revision (min 3 days) or unforeseen circumstances (min 1 day).
*   **Allotment Procedure (Reg 204):** No allotment exceeding offer (except rounding). Proportionate for non-retail. Retail max ₹2 lakh, minimum bid lot. Basis of allotment finalized fairly.
*   **Allotment, Refund, and Interest (Reg 205):** Simultaneous electronic allotment/refund/unblocking. 15% p.a. interest for delays.
*   **Post-Issue Advertisements (Reg 206):** Within 10 days of activity completion, detailing subscription, allotment, refunds, listing.
*   **Post-Issue Responsibilities of Lead Manager(s) (Reg 207):** Ongoing responsibility until issue completion, investor grievance redressal, reporting omissions, ensuring devolvement notice.
*   **Release of Subscription Money (Reg 208):** After listing/trading approvals. Refund if listing fails, with 15% p.a. interest for delay.
*   **Reporting of Transactions (Reg 209):** Promoter/group transactions (draft to closure) and pre-IPO placements reported to stock exchanges within 24 hours.
*   **Post-Issue Reports (Reg 210):** Final report (Part A Schedule XVII) with due diligence certificate (Form F Schedule V) within 7 days of allotment finalization or refund.
*   **Fungibility (Reg 211):** IDRs are fungible into underlying equity shares as specified by SEBI/RBI.

**CHAPTER VIII – RIGHTS ISSUE OF INDIAN DEPOSITORY RECEIPTS**

*   **Applicability (Reg 212):** Chapter VII applies, with specific exceptions.
*   **Entities Not Eligible (Reg 213):** Issuer breaching material obligations, debarred, or having fugitive promoters/directors.
*   **General Conditions (Reg 214):** Issuer applies for listing new IDRs on all listed stock exchanges.
*   **Renunciation (Reg 215):** IDR holders can renounce rights unless home jurisdiction laws prohibit.
*   **Depository (Reg 216):** Domestic depository facilitates IDR holders' entitlements.
*   **Record Date (Reg 217):** Announced per SEBI (LODR) Regulations. Withdrawal after record date restricts future rights issues for 12 months.
*   **Disclosures (Reg 218):** Home country disclosures plus an addendum (Part C Schedule VIII) for India.
*   **Appointment of Lead Managers and Compliance Officer (Reg 219):** Lead manager(s) and a company secretary as compliance officer (functioning in India by 08.03.2025).
*   **Filing of Draft Offer Document and Addendum (Reg 220):** Confidential draft (home country) and addendum (Part C Schedule VIII) filed with SEBI, with fees. Board may issue observations within 30 days. Undertaking from overseas custodian/domestic depository.
*   **Pricing (Reg 221):** Issue price and ratio decided per home country regulations, simultaneously with record date.
*   **Availability of Issue Material (Reg 222):** Abridged letter of offer (Part B Schedule IX) dispatched at least 3 days before opening. Plain paper applications allowed (cannot renounce rights).
*   **Issue-related Advertisement (Reg 223):** At least 3 days before opening in specified newspapers, detailing dispatch, duplicate forms, plain paper application process.
*   **Subscription Period and Allotment (Reg 224):** Open for period applicable under home country laws, but not less than 10 days. Allotment letters sent simultaneously.
*   **Utilisation of Funds (Reg 225):** Only after allotment completion.
*   **Fast Track Issue (Reg 226):** Exemptions from certain regulations if issuer meets conditions like 3 years of compliance, home country review, no pending show-cause notices, and 95% grievance redressal.

**CHAPTER IX – INITIAL PUBLIC OFFER BY SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES (SMEs)**

*   **Reference Date (Reg 227):** Issuer must satisfy conditions on filing draft offer document with SME exchange and filing offer document with RoC.
*   **Ineligibility Criteria (Reg 228):** Issuer, promoters, promoter group, directors, or selling shareholders debarred by SEBI. Promoters/directors of another debarred company. Issuer/promoters/directors are wilful defaulters or fraudulent borrowers. Promoters/directors are fugitive economic offenders. Outstanding convertible securities or rights to receive equity shares (as of 01.01.2020), with exceptions for ESOPs and fully paid-up convertible securities converting by RHP/prospectus filing.

This document outlines SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, specifically pages 169-172, concerning Initial Public Offers (IPOs), Convertible Debt Instruments (CDIs), Warrants, Promoters' Contribution, Lock-in periods, Intermediaries, Offer Document disclosures, Pricing, Allotment, Post-issue responsibilities, and the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP).

**I. General Provisions and Amendments:**
Section 227 covers IPOs. Restrictions on debarred persons do not apply if the debarment period is over by the draft offer document filing date with the SME Exchange. Amendments include substituting "registering" and "wilful defaulter," and changing "face value" to "paid-up" for capital references.

**II. Eligibility Requirements for an Initial Public Offer (Section 229):**
1.  **Post-Issue Capital:** Post-issue paid-up capital must be ≤ ₹10 crore. Issuers with capital > ₹10 crore and ≤ ₹25 crore may also issue specified securities.
2.  **SME Exchange Conditions:** Issuer must meet SME Exchange track record/eligibility conditions.
    *   **Partnership/LLP Track Record:** Operating profit track record considered only if financial statements conform to Companies Act, 2013 (Schedule III), include adequate disclosures, and are certified by ICAI peer-reviewed auditors.
    *   **Merger/Division Track Record:** Similar financial statement compliance required.
3.  **Conversion to Company:** Proprietorships, partnerships, or LLPs converting to a company can make an IPO only if the company has existed for at least one full financial year before filing the draft offer document, with restated financials conforming to Schedule III.
4.  **Promoter Change:** If promoters change or new promoters acquire >50% shareholding, the draft offer document can be filed only after one year from the change date.
5.  **Operating Profits:** Minimum operating profits of ₹1 crore from operations for at least two out of the three previous financial years.

**III. General Conditions for an Initial Public Offer (Section 230):**
1.  **Listing & Dematerialization:** Issuer must apply to one or more SME exchanges for listing, designate one, and agree with a depository for dematerialization.
2.  **Share Status:** All existing partly paid-up equity shares must be fully paid-up or forfeited; promoter-held specified securities must be dematerialized.
3.  **Project Finance:** Firm arrangements for 75% of project finance (excluding IPO proceeds/internal accruals) must be made. Bank/FI funding details must be disclosed.
4.  **Offer for Sale Limits:** Offer for sale by selling shareholders ≤ 20% of total issue size and ≤ 50% of their pre-issue shareholding (fully diluted).
5.  **Loan Repayment Restriction:** Issue proceeds cannot repay loans from promoter/promoter group/related parties.
6.  **General Corporate Purposes (GCP) Limit:** GCP amount ≤ 15% of amount raised or ₹10 crore, whichever is less (previously 25%).
7.  **Combined GCP & Unidentified Objects Limit:** Combined GCP and unidentified acquisition/investment objects ≤ 35% of amount raised. Unidentified acquisition/investment objects ≤ 25% of amount raised. These limits don't apply if the target is identified and disclosed.

**IV. Issue of Convertible Debt Instruments (CDIs) and Warrants (Part II):**
*   **CDIs:**
    *   **Eligibility:** Can make IPO without prior equity issue/listing. Ineligible if defaulted on public debt interest/principal for >6 months.
    *   **Additional Requirements:** Credit rating, debenture trustee, debenture redemption reserve, sufficient assets for secured CDIs (if applicable).
    *   **Redemption:** Must redeem as stipulated in offer document.
    *   **Conversion of Optionally Convertible Debt Instruments:** Requires positive consent. If convertible portion > ₹50 lakh and conversion price isn't determined, holders must have an option not to convert (unless upper price limit disclosed). If no conversion, issuer redeems within one month at ≥ face value (unless offer document states otherwise).
    *   **Financing Restrictions:** Cannot finance/loan to/acquire shares of promoter group/group companies, unless fully convertible debt instruments with conversion period < 18 months.
*   **Warrants:**
    *   **Eligibility:** Can issue in IPO subject to conditions.
    *   **Tenure:** ≤ 18 months from allotment date.
    *   **Attachment:** One or more warrants can be attached to a specified security.
    *   **Pricing & Upfront Payment:** Exercise price/formula determined upfront and disclosed. ≥ 25% of consideration (based on exercise price/cap price) received upfront.
    *   **Forfeiture:** Upfront consideration forfeited if warrant not exercised within three months from payment.

**V. Promoters’ Contribution (Part III):**
*   **Minimum Promoters’ Contribution:**
    *   **Requirement:** Promoters must hold ≥ 20% of post-issue capital.
    *   **Shortfall Contribution:** Alternative investment funds, foreign venture capital investors, scheduled commercial banks, public financial institutions, insurance companies, non-individual public shareholders (≥ 5% holding), or promoter group entities (other than promoters) may contribute up to 10% of post-issue capital to meet shortfall, without being identified as promoters.
    *   **Exemption:** Not applicable if no identifiable promoter.
    *   **Form of Contribution:** Equity shares or convertible securities. If conversion price not predetermined, promoters must contribute via public offer convertible securities and undertake to subscribe to equity shares upon conversion.
    *   **Weighted Average Price:** For convertible securities, contribution price not lower than weighted average price of equity shares from conversion.
    *   **CDI IPO without Prior Equity Issue:** Promoters contribute ≥ 20% of project cost in equity shares, subject to ≥ 20% of issue size from own funds in equity shares.
    *   **Timing:** Requirements met at least one day prior to issue opening.
    *   **Escrow Account:** Contribution amount in escrow, released with issue proceeds. If utilized, disclosure via cash flow statement.
    *   **Computation:** Based on post-issue expanded capital, assuming full conversion/exercise of options.
*   **Securities Ineligible for Minimum Promoters’ Contribution:**
    *   Acquired in preceding three years for non-cash consideration involving asset revaluation/intangible asset capitalization, or from bonus issue using revaluation reserves/unrealized profits, or bonus against already ineligible shares.
    *   Acquired by promoters/specified entities in preceding one year at a price lower than IPO price, unless difference paid to issuer, or acquired under Companies Act scheme, or IPO by government/statutory entity for infrastructure, or equity shares from conversion of fully paid-up compulsorily convertible securities held for ≥ 1 year.
    *   Allotted to promoters/AIFs in preceding one year at less than issue price against funds brought in, for issuers formed by conversion of firms (unless against capital existing for > 1 year).
    *   Pledged with any creditor.
*   **Eligibility of Certain Ineligible Securities:** Securities from the first and third points above become eligible if acquired pursuant to a Companies Act scheme.

**VI. Lock-in of Specified Securities (Regulations 238, 239):**
*   **Promoters (Regulation 238):**
    *   **Minimum Contribution:** 3 years from later of commercial production commencement or IPO allotment date.
    *   **Excess Holding:** 50% locked-in for 2 years, remaining 50% for 1 year from IPO allotment date.
*   **Persons Other Than Promoters (Regulation 239):** Entire pre-issue capital locked-in for 1 year from IPO allotment date.
    *   **Exceptions:** Employee stock options/schemes (subject to SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 lock-in), equity shares held by Venture Capital Fund/Alternative Investment Fund Category I or II/Foreign Venture Capital Investor (locked-in for ≥ 1 year from purchase date, combined holding period for convertible securities considered).
*   **Green Shoe Option:** Lock-in doesn't apply to securities lent for green shoe option during lending period; applies for remaining period once returned.
*   **Non-transferability:** Certificates inscribed "non-transferable"; depositories record lock-in for dematerialized securities.
*   **Pledge:** Locked-in promoter shares can be pledged as collateral for loans from specified entities (scheduled commercial bank, public financial institution, systemically important NBFC, housing finance company), subject to conditions (loan to issuer/subsidiary for issue objects if minimum contribution, or term of loan sanction if excess holding). Lock-in continues even after pledge invocation.
*   **Transferability:** Locked-in promoter shares (Reg 238) can be transferred to another promoter/promoter group/new promoter/controlling person. Locked-in non-promoter shares (Reg 239) can be transferred to any other person holding locked-in securities. Lock-in continues for transferee for remaining period.

**VII. Appointment of Lead Managers, Other Intermediaries, and Compliance Officer:**
*   **Lead Managers:** Issuer appoints one or more SEBI-registered merchant bankers. If multiple, rights/obligations disclosed. At least one lead manager must not be an associate of the issuer; if an associate is appointed, its role is limited to marketing and associate status disclosed.
*   **Other Intermediaries:** Appointed in consultation with lead manager(s) after capability assessment.
*   **Agreements:** Issuer enters agreements with lead manager(s) (Schedule II format) and other intermediaries.
*   **Syndicate Members/Bankers:** Appointed for book-building/other issues respectively.
*   **Registrar:** SEBI-registered registrar with depository connectivity appointed. Issuer/lead manager cannot act as registrar if handling post-issue responsibilities.
*   **Compliance Officer:** Person qualified as company secretary (w.e.f. 08.03.2025) appointed to monitor securities law compliance and investor grievance redressal.

**VIII. Disclosures in and Filing of Offer Documents:**
*   **Content:** Material, true, and adequate disclosures for informed investment decisions.
*   **Specific Disclosures:** Companies Act, 2013, Part A of Schedule VI, EPF/ESIC details (w.e.f. 08.03.2025), lead manager site visit reports, lead manager fees.
*   **Due Diligence:** Lead manager(s) must exercise due diligence on disclosures.
*   **Filing:** Issuer files offer document with Board via lead manager(s) immediately after filing with RoC. Board does not issue observations. Lead manager(s) submit due-diligence certificate (Form A, Schedule V) and additional confirmations (Form G, Schedule V) with draft offer document to SME Exchange(s).
*   **Public Availability:** Offer document displayed on websites of issuer, Board, lead manager(s), and SME exchange(s). Draft offer document public for comments for ≥ 21 days. Public announcement inviting comments in newspapers within two working days of filing draft offer document. Lead manager(s) file comments/changes with SME exchange. Copies provided to public for reasonable sum.
*   **Face Value:** Disclosed in offer documents, advertisements, application forms, with identical font size as price band/issue price.

**IX. Pricing and Price Band:**
*   **Determination:** Issuer determines price/coupon rate/conversion price in consultation with lead manager(s) or via book building (Schedule XIII).
*   **Price Band:** Cap ≤ 120% of floor price. Floor price/final price ≥ face value.
*   **Announcement:** Floor price/price band announced ≥ 2 working days before issue opening in pre-issue/price band advertisements (Part A, Schedule X) in national/regional newspapers, including financial ratios and directing to "basis of issue price" section. Details on SME exchange websites and pre-filled in application forms.
*   **Differential Pricing:** Permitted for individual investors (minimum application size) or retail individual shareholders/employees entitled to reservation, at a price not lower than by >10% of price offered to other categories (excluding anchor investors). Minimum application lot size uniform. Anchor investor price not lower than other applicants. Discount in rupee terms.

**X. Allocation in Issues:**
*   **Minimum Offer to Public:** Must comply with Securities Contracts (Regulations) Rules, 1957, rule 19(2)(b).
*   **Net Offer Category:** Not less than 35% to individual investors (minimum application size); not less than 15% to non-institutional investors; not more than 50% to QIBs (5% of this to mutual funds). Unsubscribed portions may be cross-allocated.
*   **Amendments (Effective 08.03.2025):**
    *   **Book Building:** Non-institutional investors: 1/3 for application size > 2 lots and ≤ ₹10 lakhs; 2/3 for application size > ₹10 lakhs. Cross-allocation of unsubscribed portions.
    *   **Other than Book Building:** Net offer: ≥ 50% to individual investors (minimum application size); remaining to individual applicants (minimum application size) and other investors. Cross-allocation. Higher percentage allocated to individual investors (minimum application size) if entitled on proportionate basis.

**XI. Reservation on a Competitive Basis (Regulation 254):**
*   **Permitted:** For employees and shareholders (excluding promoters/promoter group of listed subsidiaries/promoter companies).
*   **Prohibited:** For lead manager(s), registrar, syndicate member(s), their promoters, directors, employees, group/associate companies.
*   **Conditions:**
    *   Employee reservations ≤ 5% of post-issue capital, max allotment ₹2 lakhs per employee (up to ₹5 lakhs if under-subscribed).
    *   Shareholder reservations ≤ 10% of issue size.
    *   Competitive reservation applicants (except employees/retail individual shareholders) cannot apply in net offer.
    *   Unsubscribed portions in reserved categories added to other reserved categories, then to net offer. Spill-over from reserved to net offer permitted if net offer under-subscribed.
    *   Applicant in reserved category can apply for any number of securities ≤ reserved portion.

**XII. Other Issue-Related Regulations:**
*   **Abridged Prospectus (Reg 255):** Disclosures in Part E of Schedule VI; accompanies every application form.
*   **ASBA (Reg 256):** Issuers must accept bids using only ASBA facility.
*   **Availability of Issue Material (Reg 257):** Lead manager(s) ensure offer document/materials available to intermediaries/investors before issue opens.
*   **Prohibition on Payment of Incentives (Reg 258):** No direct/indirect incentives for applications, except fees/commission for services.
*   **Underwriting (Reg 260):** IPOs must be 100% underwritten. Lead manager(s) underwrite ≥ 15%. Issuer appoints underwriters/stock brokers. Lead manager(s) may agree with nominated investors. Undertaking filed one day before issue opening. Lead manager(s) responsible for fulfilling obligations. Underwriters/sub-underwriters (other than lead manager(s)/nominated investors) subscribe only to fulfill obligations. Disclosures in offer document.
*   **Deposit with Designated Stock Exchange:** 1% of issue size for public subscription deposited before subscription list opens (refundable/forfeitable).
*   **Compulsory Market Making (Reg 261):** Lead manager(s) ensure market making through SME exchange brokers for ≥ 3 years from listing/migration. Market maker inventory ≥ 5% of listed securities. Market makers buy entire shareholding if value < minimum contract size, cannot sell in lots < minimum contract size. Prohibited from buying from promoters/promoter group/their acquirers during market making. Promoters' holdings not eligible unless not locked-in and with SME exchange permission.
*   **Monitoring Agency (Reg 262):** If issue size (excluding offer for sale) > ₹50 crore, SEBI-registered credit rating agency monitors use of proceeds (not for banks/PFIs/insurance companies). Quarterly reports (Schedule XI) submitted to issuer, disseminated publicly on website and to stock exchange(s) within 45 days. If no agency required, statutory auditor's certificate for utilization submitted quarterly. If working capital > ₹5 crore, auditor's certificate for its use submitted quarterly.
*   **Public Communications, Publicity Materials, Advertisements and Research Reports (Reg 263):** Must comply with Schedule IX.
*   **Issue-related Advertisements (Reg 264):** Pre-issue/price band ads after filing prospectus with RoC, in same newspapers as public announcement, following Part A of Schedule X. Issue opening/closing ads (Parts B & C of Schedule X). No ads implying full/oversubscription during subscription period. Closure announcement only after lead manager(s) confirm ≥ 90% subscription and registrar certificate.
*   **Opening of the Issue (Reg 265):** Issue opens ≥ 3 working days after filing offer document with RoC.
*   **Period of Subscription (Reg 266):** Public issue open for minimum 3, maximum 10 working days. Bidding period extended by ≥ 3 working days if price band revised. Extended by ≥ 1 working day for force majeure/unforeseen circumstances.
*   **Application and Minimum Application Value (Reg 267):** Max application by person in net offer ≤ total offered to public. Max application by non-institutional investors ≤ total offered less QIB portion. Minimum application size is two lots and > ₹2 lakhs. Applications in multiples of lot size. Minimum sum payable on application ≥ 25% of issue price.
*   **Offer for Sale and Minimum Application Value:** Full issue price payable on application for offer for sale. "Minimum application value" refers to issue price, not amount payable on application.
*   **Allotment Procedure and Basis of Allotment (Reg 268):** Allotment not made if < 200 allottees (changed from 50 w.e.f. 08.03.2025). Allotment not to exceed specified securities offered (except for rounding off). Allotment to non-individual investors/anchor investors on proportionate basis. Value of securities allotted to any person (except employees under reservation) ≤ ₹2 lakhs. Non-institutional investor allotment ≥ minimum application size in their category. Basis of allotment finalized by stock exchange, lead manager(s), registrars (Parts A and A2 of Schedule XIV).
*   **Allotment, Refund, and Payment of Interest (Reg 269):** Allotment/refund/unblocking within Board-specified time. If not completed, issuer pays 15% p.a. interest (lead manager(s) ensure payment). Refund periods changed from 7/8 days to 4 days (w.e.f. 14.01.2022).
*   **Post-Issue Advertisements (Reg 270):** Lead manager(s) ensure advertisement within 10 days of completion of activities, detailing subscription, allotment basis, application/allottee data, refund/credit dates, listing application date. Published in English, Hindi, and regional language dailies, and on stock exchange websites.
*   **Post-Issue Responsibilities of the Lead Manager(s) (Reg 271):** Responsibility continues until issue process completion and for related matters. Monitor investor grievances, coordinate with intermediaries, report omissions to Board. Ensure devolvement notice within 10 days of issue closure for underwriters. Furnish information on defaulting underwriters (Schedule XVIII).
