*   **Release of Subscription Money (Reg 272):** Lead manager(s) confirm formalities completed to bankers for money release. If listing/trading permission fails, issuer refunds entire monies within 4 days of intimation. If not repaid, issuer and defaulting directors jointly/severally liable to repay with 15% p.a. interest from the fourth day.
*   **Post-Issue Reports:** Lead managers submit final post-issue report (Part A of Schedule XVII) and due diligence certificate (Form F of Schedule V) within 7 days of allotment basis finalization or issue failure refund. Ensure money release complies with Companies Act, 2013, Section 40(3).
*   **Reporting of Transactions:** Issuer reports all promoter/promoter group securities transactions and proposed pre-IPO placements (disclosed in draft offer document) to stock exchange(s) within 24 hours, from draft offer document/offer document filing to issue closure.
*   **Migration of Securities:**
    *   **To SME Exchange:** Listed issuer issuing specified securities under this Chapter must migrate existing listed securities to SME exchange. Listed issuer with post-issue paid-up capital < ₹25 crore may migrate if shareholders approve by special resolution (non-promoter votes in favor ≥ 2x votes against) and meets SME exchange eligibility.
    *   **To Main Board:** SME-listed issuer with post-issue paid-up capital between ₹10 crore and ₹25 crore may migrate if shareholders approve by special resolution (non-promoter votes in favor ≥ 2x votes against) and meets Main Board eligibility.
*   **Restriction on Further Capital Issues:** Generally prohibited between draft offer document filing and listing/refund. Exception for employee stock option/appreciation right schemes or if full disclosures made.
*   **Price Stabilisation through Green Shoe Option:** Permitted to stabilize post-listing prices. Requires shareholder authorization, lead manager as stabilizing agent, prior agreement. Stabilizing agent agrees with promoters/pre-issue shareholders to borrow securities for over-allotment (≤ 15% of issue size). Disclosures in offer documents. Stabilization period ≤ 30 days from trading permission. Special bank/depository accounts for over-allotment. Securities returned to lenders within 2 working days. If shortfall, issuer allots at issue price. Remaining monies transferred to Investor Protection and Education Fund. Daily reports to stock exchange, final report to Board (Schedule XV).

**XIII. Alteration of Rights (Section 280.1):**
Issuer cannot alter specified securities terms adversely affecting holders' interests without written consent from ≥ 3/4ths of that class or special resolution sanction.

**XIV. SME Exchange Migration and Further Issues (Sections 280.2, 281):**
*   If SME-listed issuer's post-issue paid-up capital exceeds ₹25 crore due to further issue, it **shall** migrate to Main Board if it meets Main Board eligibility. Requires special resolution (non-promoter votes in favor ≥ 2x votes against) and in-principle Main Board approval.
*   Alternatively, if post-issue paid-up capital exceeds ₹25 crore, issuer **may** undertake further capital issuance without migrating from SME exchange, provided it complies with SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, applicable to Main Board companies.
*   SME-listed issuers making further issues must adhere to applicable regulations.

**XV. Post-listing Exit Opportunity for Dissenting Shareholders (Section 281A):**
Promoters/controlling shareholders must provide an exit offer to dissenting shareholders (Companies Act, 2013, Schedule XX) if objects change or contract terms related to objects vary. Not applicable if no identifiable promoters/controlling shareholders.

**XVI. Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) (Chapter X, Sections 282, 283):**
*   **Applicability:** For issuers seeking listing via IPO or trading without public offer.
*   **General Regulations:** Other SEBI regulations apply mutatis mutandis, except for regulation 7(2) (GCP restrictions) and regulation 6(1) & (2) (eligibility requirements).
*   **Access:** Only institutional and non-institutional investors.
*   **SR Equity Shares:** Issuers with SR equity shares can make an IPO of *only ordinary shares* for IGP listing, subject to compliance with this chapter and SR equity share provisions (regulation 6(3)).
*   **Eligibility:** Issuer must be technology-intensive (technology, IT, IP, data analytics, bio-technology, nano-technology) providing products/services/platforms with substantial value addition. Additionally, 25% of pre-issue capital must have been held for ≥ 1 year by Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs), Innovators Growth Platform Investors, or specific regulated entities (FPIs, pooled investment funds meeting criteria).

This document outlines regulations related to the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP), Social Stock Exchange (SSE), bonus issues, and general compliance under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, and subsequent amendments.

**I. Innovators Growth Platform (IGP)**

*   **IGP Investors:**
    *   **Eligibility:** Must not be from FATF-identified deficient countries. Eligible individuals have ≥₹50 lakh annual gross income and ≥₹5 crore liquid net worth; corporate bodies/family trusts have ≥₹25 crore net worth.
    *   **Accreditation:** Through stock exchanges or depositories.
    *   **Promoter Capital:** Pre-issue capital held by promoters, even if IGP Investors, is not considered for the 25% pre-issue capital eligibility.
    *   **Terminology:** "Innovators Growth Platform Investors" replaced "Accredited Investors" (w.e.f. 05.05.2021).
*   **Eligibility for Listing on IGP:** No promoters or directors can be fugitive economic offenders. The platform was previously known as the "institutional trading platform" (w.e.f. 05.05.2021).
*   **Listing Without a Public Issue (Regulation 284):**
    *   **Process:** File draft information document with the Board (with fees) and obtain in-principle approval from stock exchanges.
    *   **Disclosures:** Must contain disclosures specified in Part A of Schedule VI.
    *   **Timeline:** Securities must be listed within 30 days of Board observations or expiry of observation period.
    *   **Exemptions:** Regulations on allotment, issue opening/closing, advertisements, underwriting, pricing, and minimum public offer are not applicable.
    *   **Minimum Public Shareholding:** Provisions are not applicable for this type of listing.
    *   **Document Approval & Liability:** Approved by the issuer's board and signed by directors, CEO, and CFO, who certify truthfulness and are liable for mis-statements.
*   **Listing Pursuant to an Initial Public Offer (IPO) (Regulation 285 onwards):**
    *   **Process:** File draft offer document with the Board (with fees).
    *   **Disclosures:** Broad objects of the issue and basis of issue price (excluding projections).
    *   **Minimum Public Shareholding & Offer Size:** Must comply with minimum public shareholding rules; minimum offer size is ₹10 crore (w.e.f. 05.04.2019).
    *   **Minimum Application Size:** ₹2 lakh and in multiples thereof (w.e.f. 05.04.2019).
    *   **Allocation:** At least 50 allottees (w.e.f. 05.04.2019). Allotment to institutional and non-institutional investors is proportionate. Up to 60% of the issue size can be allocated discretionarily to eligible investors (similar to anchor investors) prior to issue opening, at a price not lower than other applicants, with a minimum application of ₹50 lakh (w.e.f. 05.05.2021).
*   **Lock-in (Regulation 288):**
    *   **General:** Entire pre-issue capital locked-in for 6 months from allotment (public issue) or listing (without public issue).
    *   **Exemptions:** Equity shares allotted under employee schemes (subject to SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021) and shares held by Venture Capital Funds (VCF), Alternative Investment Funds (AIF Category I or II), or Foreign Venture Capital Investors (FVCI) are locked-in for at least one year from purchase date.
    *   **Specific Lock-in:** Equity shares held by non-promoters must be held for at least one year prior to listing without a public issue. Combined holding period for convertible securities is considered. Locked-in promoter shares may be pledged as collateral under specific conditions. All discretionary allotted securities are locked-in as per anchor investor rules. SR equity shares are locked-in until conversion or for the specified period, whichever is later.
*   **Exit and Delisting:**
    *   **Exit:** An issuer listed without a public issue may exit with a special resolution (90% total votes, majority non-promoter votes) and stock exchange approval.
    *   **Delisting:** Stock exchanges can delist for non-compliance. Promoters/directors of delisted entities are prohibited from listing another issuer on IGP for five years (except independent directors).
*   **Migration to Main Board (Regulation 292):**
    *   **Eligibility:** Minimum one year on IGP, at least 200 shareholders, no debarment/wilful defaulter/fugitive economic offender for company/promoters/directors.
    *   **Financial Conditions:** Net tangible assets ≥₹3 crore, average operating profit ≥₹15 crore, net worth ≥₹1 crore (all consolidated for preceding three years). If name changed, 50% revenue from new activity.
    *   **Alternative:** If financial conditions not met, 50% of capital held by Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) at application date.
    *   **Promoters’ Contribution:** Promoters must hold ≥20% of total capital. Shortfall (up to 10%) can be met by specified entities.
    *   **Lock-in:** Promoters’ contribution locked-in for three years from main board trading approval; excess holding for one year. IGP lock-in period is deducted. Not applicable if listed on IGP for three years or more.

**II. Social Stock Exchange (SSE) (Chapter X-A, inserted 2022)**

*   **Definitions:**
    *   **For Profit Social Enterprise (FPSE):** A for-profit company/body corporate that is a Social Enterprise, excluding Section 8 companies.
    *   **Not for Profit Organization (NPO):** A Social Enterprise that is a charitable trust, society, or Section 8 company.
    *   **Social Impact Assessor/Firm:** Individuals/entities registered with a self-regulatory organization, qualified by NISM certification.
    *   **Social Enterprise:** Either an NPO or an FPSE meeting eligibility criteria.
    *   **SSE:** A separate segment of a recognized stock exchange for NPOs and/or listing their securities.
*   **Applicability:** For NPOs seeking registration/fund-raising and FPSEs seeking identification as Social Enterprises.
*   **Access:** Accessible to institutional, non-institutional, and retail investors.
*   **Governing Council:** Each SSE must constitute a Governing Council for oversight.
*   **Eligibility for Social Enterprise Identification (292E):**
    *   Must establish primacy of social intent and be involved in at least one of several specified activities (e.g., eradicating hunger, promoting healthcare, education, gender equality, environmental sustainability, supporting incubators).
    *   **Criteria:** Must target underserved/less privileged populations/regions. At least 67% of preceding 3-year average revenues, expenditure, or customer base must be from eligible activities to the target population.
    *   **Ineligible:** Corporate foundations, political/religious organizations, professional/trade associations, and infrastructure/housing companies (except affordable housing).
*   **Fundraising by Social Enterprises (292G):**
    *   **NPOs:** May raise funds through Zero Coupon Zero Principal Instruments (ZCZP) to eligible investors, donations via Mutual Fund schemes, or other Board-specified means.
    *   **FPSEs:** May raise funds through equity shares (on main board, SME, or IGP, or to AIFs), debt securities, or other Board-specified means. Their securities will be listed with an identifier.
*   **Ineligibility for Raising Funds (292H):** A Social Enterprise is ineligible if it, its promoters, directors, or trustees are debarred from the securities market, are wilful defaulters, fraudulent borrowers, or fugitive economic offenders (unless past debarment period concluded).
*   **Zero Coupon Zero Principal Instruments (ZCZP):**
    *   Issued only by NPOs registered on an SSE, for a specific tenure, without coupon or principal.
    *   For specific eligible projects/activities.
    *   Procedures and fund-raising document contents are "as specified by the Board" (w.e.f. 21.12.2023).
    *   NPOs may also make private issuance of ZCZP to Social Impact Funds.
    *   Listing terminates when the project object is achieved or tenure expires.
*   **SSE Additional Norms:** SSEs must specify additional norms for issue procedures (e.g., agreements, ASBA, duration, allocation).

**III. Bonus Issues (Chapter XI)**

*   **Eligibility:** Listed issuers can issue bonus shares if their articles authorize it (or a general body resolution is passed), all prior securities are approved for listing, no default on fixed deposits/debt/employee statutory dues, partly paid shares are fully paid-up, and no promoters/directors are fugitive economic offenders.
*   **Restrictions (Regulation 294):**
    *   Equity shares must be reserved for holders of outstanding compulsorily convertible debt instruments.
    *   Must be made only from free reserves, securities premium account, or capital redemption reserve (from genuine profits/cash premium), not revaluation reserves.
    *   Cannot be issued in lieu of dividends.
    *   Bonus on SR equity shares must carry the same voting rights ratio as ordinary shares and convert along with existing SR shares.
    *   Allotment must be in dematerialized form.
*   **Completion (Regulation 295):**
    *   If only board approval is needed, implemented within 15 days.
    *   If shareholder approval is needed, implemented within two months from the board meeting (subject to approval).
    *   Cannot be withdrawn once announced.

**IV. General Regulatory Powers and Compliance**

*   **Power to Relax Strict Enforcement (Regulatory Sandbox - Regulation 295A):** The Board may exempt persons for up to 12 months to test new products/services in a "regulatory sandbox" environment.
*   **Directions by the Board (Regulation 296):** The Board can issue directions (e.g., prohibiting market access, directing divestment) in the interest of investors or the securities market, after providing an opportunity to be heard.
*   **Liability for Contravention (Regulation 297):** Contravention leads to actions by stock exchanges (fines, trading suspension, freezing holdings).
*   **Power to Remove Difficulty (Regulation 299):** The Board may issue guidance notes or circulars to address difficulties.
*   **Power to Relax Strict Enforcement (General - Regulation 300):** The Board may relax requirements (procedural, irrelevant disclosure, beyond control) for investor/market development, upon application with a ₹1 lakh fee.
*   **Repeal and Savings (Regulation 301):** The SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2009, are rescinded; actions/documents under old regulations are deemed under the new ones.

**V. Schedules (Fees, Filing, Due Diligence)**

*   **Schedule I (Lead Managers’ Inter-Se Allocation of Responsibilities):** Lead managers must disclose activity-wise responsibilities, ensure compliance, and invoke underwriting obligations.
*   **Schedule II (Agreement between Lead Manager(s) and Issuer):** Specifies clauses for issuer representations (compliance, truthfulness) and covenants (information, statutory compliance, advertisements, intermediary appointments, timely allotment/refunds, fee payment, problem reporting, no legal action without consultation, refund monies).
*   **Schedule III (Fees):** Details non-refundable fees payable to the Board for draft offer documents, offer documents, and letters of offer, based on issue size or paid-up capital, with varying rates for public issues, rights issues, and listing without a public issue. Fees are paid via direct credit/online.
*   **Schedule IV (Filing):** Draft offer documents and letters of offer must be filed by lead managers at the SEBI Head Office in Mumbai.
*   **Schedule V (Due Diligence Certificates):** Prescribes formats for various due diligence certificates from lead managers (with draft offer document, offer document, post-issue report, for SME issues, IDR issues) and debenture trustees (with draft offer document). These certificates confirm compliance with regulations, truthfulness of disclosures, intermediary registrations, underwriting capabilities, promoter lock-in, dematerialization agreements, and other specific requirements.
*   **Schedule VI:** Lists regulations pertaining to disclosures in the offer document, abridged prospectus, and letter of offer.

This document outlines comprehensive disclosure requirements for draft offer documents, draft letters of offer, offer documents, and letters of offer for public and rights issues of specified securities.

**General Disclosure Instructions:**
All information must be relevant, updated, and substantiated with disclosed sources. Technical terms require clarification, and simple English should be used. Cross-references must include paragraph headings and page numbers. Unsubstantiated forward-looking statements are prohibited, and consistency in disclosure style and financial units is mandatory. Blank spaces must be filled before filing.

**Applicability and Exceptions:**
These disclosures apply to issuers undertaking public or rights issues. Exceptions include fast track public issues (omitting Part D disclosures), further public offers (omitting Part C under specific conditions), and rights issues (only Part B disclosures under specific conditions). For SME exchange listings, "retail individual investors" are defined as those applying for the minimum application size (2025 amendment).

**Offer Document Structure and Content:**

1.  **Cover Pages:**
    *   **Physical:** At least 100 GSM, white, no patterns.
    *   **Front Outside:** Issue/issuer details, selling shareholder details (tabular, including average cost of acquisition and offer for sale), and Board-specified information (2022 update).
    *   **Front Inside (2022 update):** Document type, date, issuance type (book built/fixed price), Companies Act Section 32 clause (for public issues), issuer details (name, logo, CIN, addresses, contacts, website, email), promoter names, nature/number/price of securities, issue size (including offer for sale), aggregate amount from shelf prospectus, 'Risks in relation to the First Issue' (for first issues), 'General Risk' clause, 'Issuer’s Absolute Responsibility' clause, lead manager(s) details (including associate disclosure), registrar details, issue schedule, credit rating/IPO grading (if any), and proposed listing stock exchanges with in-principle approval.
    *   **Back Cover Pages:** Both inside and outside must be blank.

2.  **Table of Contents:** Immediately after the front inside cover page.

3.  **Definitions and Abbreviations:** Covers conventional, issue-related, issuer/industry-related terms, and abbreviations.

4.  **Offer Document Summary:** Summarizes primary business (under 100 words), promoters, issue size (fresh/offer for sale), objects of issue (tabular), pre/post-issue shareholding of promoter/promoter group/selling shareholders/top 10 shareholders (tabular, 2025 addition), restated consolidated financial statements for past 3 years and stub period (tabular: share capital, net worth, revenue, PAT, EPS, NAV, total borrowings), auditor qualifications not given effect, summary of outstanding litigations/contingent liabilities/related party transactions (with cross-references), financing arrangements by promoters/directors/relatives for security purchases in last 6 months, weighted average acquisition price for promoters/selling shareholders in last year, average cost of acquisition, pre-IPO placement size/allottees, equity issuances for non-cash consideration/split/consolidation in last year.

5.  **Key Disclosure Requirements:**
    *   **Exemption from Securities Laws:** Any SEBI exemption must be disclosed.
    *   **Risk Factors:** Clear, readable font (min 10 pt). Classified as specific (internal) or external. Materiality determined collectively. Each factor states risk and proposed addressal (no speculative outcomes or sub-judice matters). Ordered by descending materiality, with implications (financial if quantifiable). Mandatory disclosures include: unreceived statutory approvals, business seasonality, recent lower-priced issues, interim use of funds, unplaced orders for plant/machinery, lack of experience, losses in last 3 years, customer dependence, listing refusal/failure/penalties, limited trading, debt defaults, unsecured loans, deposit defaults, conflict of interest, shortfalls in previous issue objects, interests beyond remuneration, portion of proceeds to promoters/directors, land acquisition relationships, KMP/senior management dependence, unsecured investments, non-provision for investment decline, summary of litigations (tabular), project delay, issuer's discretion for fund deployment (if no monitoring agency), negative cash flow, unregistered land, restrictive covenants, investor grievances, risks of second/residual charge, and if proforma/restated CFS by non-statutory auditor (Top 10 Risk Factor).
    *   **Introduction:** Brief issue details and consolidated financial summary.
    *   **General Information:** Registered/corporate office, issuer registration, RoC, board members (names, DINs, addresses), contact details for Company Secretary, legal advisor, bankers to issuer, compliance officer, lead manager(s), registrars, and bankers/brokers to issue.

6.  **Further General Information:**
    *   **Auditors:** Names, addresses, contact details, peer review/firm registration numbers.
    *   **Lead Manager(s):** Inter-se allocation of responsibilities.
    *   **Credit Rating (for convertible debt):** All agencies, ratings obtained (including unaccepted), and ratings for issuer's listed convertible debt in prior 3 years.
    *   **IPO Grading (if obtained):** Agencies, grades, and rationale.
    *   **Debenture Trustee (for convertible debt):** Name, address, contact details.
    *   **Monitoring Agency (if appointed):** Name, address, contact details, and disclosure if regulatory appointment.
    *   **Appraising Entity (if project appraised):** Name, address, contact details.
    *   **Filing Details:** Board office and RoC address where documents are filed.
    *   **Book Building Process:** Brief explanation if applicable.
    *   **Underwriting:** Underwriters' details, amounts, board declaration of sufficient resources, extent of partial underwriting, and final arrangement in prospectus.
    *   **Changes in Auditors:** Details and reasons for changes in last 3 years.
    *   **Green Shoe Option (if applicable):** Stabilising agent, max over-allotment (number/percentage), max stabilisation period, early closing disclosure, max increase in equity/post-issue shareholding, max funds received/use, agreement details (names, shareholding, lent shares, terms), and exact number of shares allotted/transferred (borrowed vs. over-allotted).

7.  **Capital Structure and Shareholding Information:**
    *   **Capital Structure (tabular):** Authorised, issued, subscribed, paid-up capital; present issue size; paid-up capital after issue/conversion; share premium account.
    *   **Existing Share Capital:** Allotment details (date, allottee, nature, number, price, consideration).
    *   **Shares for Non-Cash/Revaluation Reserves:** Details (date, revaluation date, persons, price, reasons, benefits).
    *   **Shares under Schemes of Arrangement:** Details of allotments.
    *   **Employee Stock Option Schemes:** Quarter-wise particulars (number, price range).
    *   **Lower Priced Issues:** Details if securities issued at lower price in prior year (names, promoter group status, reasons, price).
    *   **Shareholding Pattern:** As per SEBI (LODR) Reg. 31, including shareholders holding 1% or more (at least 80% of capital), number of shares, and particulars for 2 years, 1 year, and 10 days prior to filing. Separate disclosure for IPO subscribers if IPO in prior 2 years.
    *   **Proposed Capital Structure Alterations:** Issuer's intentions/negotiations within 6 months of issue opening.
    *   **Promoters' Total Shareholding (tabular):** For each promoter (name, issue nature, allotment/transfer date, number, face value, price, paid-up date, pre/post-issue percentage, pledged shares).
    *   **Number of Members/Shareholders.**
    *   **Promoter Group and Directors' Dealings:** Aggregate shareholding of promoter group/corporate promoter directors; aggregate specified securities purchased/sold by promoter group/directors/relatives in prior 6 months; financing arrangements for others' security purchases in prior 6 months. Statement on relatives' sales/purchases based on records.
    *   **Promoters' Contribution and Lock-in Period:** Details for each promoter (allotment date, paid-up date, nature, number, face value, price, contribution percentage, lock-in end date). For IPO, all individual allotments from incorporation. For FPO, prior 5 years. Separate disclosure for shares acquired via public/rights/preferential/bonus/DR conversion/ESOS vs. secondary market. Compliance with lock-in, and promoter undertaking full conversion if contribution is in optionally convertible debt.

8.  **General Statements and Lead Manager Details:**
    *   No buy-back arrangements by issuer, directors, or lead manager(s).
    *   All offered securities fully paid-up or subject to forfeiture.
    *   Lead manager(s) and associates' shareholding in issuer.

9.  **Employee Stock Option/Purchase Schemes (ESOP/ESPS):**
    *   Details of options granted/shares issued in prior 3 years and cumulatively.
    *   For IPOs with outstanding options: granted, vested, exercised, price, shares from exercise, lapsed, variation, money realized, options in force.
    *   Employee-wise details for KMP, senior management, 5%+ recipients, and 1%+ recipients.
    *   Diluted EPS calculation.
    *   Disclosure of intrinsic vs. fair value method difference and impact on profits/EPS.
    *   Pricing formula, method, and assumptions for fair value.
    *   Impact on profits/EPS for last 3 years if SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 followed.
    *   Intentions of KMP/senior management/whole-time directors to sell ESOP/ESPS shares within 3 months of listing.
    *   For ESPS: number of shares, price, employee-wise details (KMP, senior management, 5%+ recipients, 1%+ recipients), diluted EPS, consideration.

10. **Further Public Offer Compliance:**
    *   Confirmation of compliance with relevant regulations for FPOs by listed issuers with prior preferential allotment, bonus issue, or QIP in preceding 10 years.

11. **Particulars of the Issue - Objects of the Issue:**
    *   General objects.
    *   Loan repayment: lender, terms, outstanding amount, statutory auditor's certificate for utilization.
    *   Investment in JV/subsidiary/acquisition: form of investment, or statement if undecided. For debt, interest, security, repayment, subordination, expected benefit.
    *   Loan to non-subsidiary: loan agreements, interest, security, duration, repayment, subordination, expected benefits.
    *   Long-term working capital: standalone basis, estimation basis, reasons for additional capital, projected requirements, total envisaged, existing details. Reasons if no working capital shown.
    *   Land acquisition: names of entities, cost, relationship, encumbrance status, title, registration, approvals. Consistent with "Cost of the Project."
    *   Project funding: location, plant/machinery (cost, suppliers, orders, quotations, second-hand details), technology, collaborations, infrastructure.
    *   Property purchase: vendors, amounts paid/payable, title, related transactions in prior 2 years.
    *   Plant/equipment/technology/process purchase: specifics, cost, suppliers, orders, quotations, second-hand details.

12. **Specific Instrument Disclosures:**
    *   **Secured Convertible Debt Instruments:** Asset description for security/cover, computation basis, valuation methods, periodicity, ranking of charges.
    *   **Warrants:** Objects for funds from conversions.

13. **Requirement of Funds:** Total project cost (activity/project-wise), material existing/anticipated transactions with promoters/group companies related to proceeds/cost.

14. **Funding Plan (Means of Finance):** Undertaking for 75% firm arrangements (excluding issue amount/internal accruals), details of balance finance, deployment of excess proceeds.

15. **Appraisal:** Scope, purpose, date of appraisal. Alignment of cost/finance with report, explanation for revisions. Weaknesses/threats as risk factors.

16. **Schedule of Implementation:** Tabular schedule, progress, reasons for delays.

17. **Deployment of Funds:** Sources/deployment up to 2 months prior to filing (certified by statutory auditor). Cash flow statement for promoter's contribution (certified). Means/sources for deployed funds (including bridge loans). Net issue proceeds in scheduled commercial banks. Year-wise project expenditure break-up.

18. **Expenses of the Issue:** Break-up (amount, percentage of total/issue size) for lead manager fees, brokerage, registrars, legal advisors, advertising, regulators, printing, others.

19. **Basis for Issue Price:**
    *   Consolidated basis, adjusted for bonus/split: EPS (basic/diluted, pre-issue, last 3 years), P/E ratio (pre-issue, comparison with industry), Average Return on Net Worth (last 3 years), NAV per share (last balance sheet, after issue, comparison with issue price). Illustrative format provided.
    *   Formula/basis for ratios. Lead manager(s) due diligence.
    *   Comparison with industry average/peer group (size, industry, consistency, regulatory filings).
    *   Dilution due to bonus shares, justification of issue price.
    *   Statements for book-built (price determined with lead manager) and fixed-price issues (price justified with lead manager).
    *   Accounting ratios account for compulsory conversions/options.
    *   For fully convertible debt with interest < bank rate, disclose investor's effective price (considering notional interest loss).
    *   **Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):** Defined consistently in "Definitions," approved by Audit Committee, certified by statutory auditor/CA/Cost Accountant (with Peer Review Board certificate), included in material documents. Provided for period co-terminus with restated financials, with explanations for historical use and changes due to acquisitions/dispositions.
    *   **KPIs in 'Basis for Issue Price':** All KPIs disclosed to investors in prior 3 years must be included, with Audit Committee confirmation of verified/audited details. Issuer/lead merchant banker may disclose other material KPIs. Cross-references to other sections. Comparison with Indian/global listed peers (comparable size, industry, business model), with notes for differences.
    *   **Ongoing KPI Disclosure:** Issuer must disclose KPIs from 'Basis for Issue Price' periodically (at least annually or lesser period) for 1 year post-listing or until issue proceeds utilization, explaining any changes. Certified by expert body member.
    *   **Issue Price, Floor Price, or Price Band:** Disclose primary/new issue price (equity/convertible, excluding ESOP/ESOS/bonus) if 5%+ of fully diluted paid-up capital (pre-issue, excluding unvested ESOPs) in single/rolling 30-day transaction during 18 months prior to DRHP/RHP filing. Secondary sale/acquisition price (equity/convertible) involving promoter/promoter group/selling shareholders/director nomination rights (excluding gifts) if 5%+ of fully diluted paid-up capital in single/rolling 30-day transaction during 18 months prior to DRHP/RHP filing. If no such transactions, last 5 primary/secondary transactions (involving specific parties) not older than 3 years, irrespective of size. All prices adjusted for corporate actions.
    *   **Weighted Average Cost of Acquisition (WACA):** Floor/cap price expressed as "[●] times" WACA (tabular). Detailed explanation for offer price/cap price being "[●] times" WACA, comparing issuer's KPIs/financial ratios for last 3 years/stub period. Explanation for offer price/cap price being "[●] times" WACA due to external factors. WACA table and Independent Directors' Committee recommendation (justifying price band based on quantitative factors/KPIs vs. WACA) in 'Risks to Investors' section of Price Band Advertisement.

21. **About the Issuer:**
    *   **Industry Overview:** Complete industry report for any extract disclosed (2023 amendment).
    *   **Business Overview:** Primary business, plant/machinery/technology/process, collaborations, infrastructure, products/services (nature, end users, marketing), business strategy (no financial forecasts), installed capacities/utilization (prior 3 years), intellectual property rights, material properties.
    *   **Key Industry-Regulations (if applicable).**
    *   **History and Corporate Structure:** Incorporation date, business commencement, conversions, name/registered office changes (with reasons), major historical events (partnerships, project overruns, capacity, product launches, market entry/exit, awards, defaults/restructuring), material acquisitions/divestments, mergers, amalgamations, asset revaluations in last 10 years.

22. **Main Objects and Amendments:** Main objects from Memorandum of Association, dates/details of amendments in last 10 years.

23. **Group Entities:** Holding companies, subsidiaries, JVs (name, business, capital structure, issuer's shareholding, accumulated profits/losses of subsidiaries not accounted for).

    *   Details of guarantees by promoter offering shares in OFS (reasons, amount, obligations, period, financial implications, security, consideration).
    *   Key terms, dates, parties, nature of other material agreements not in ordinary course of business.
    *   Agreements required under SEBI (LODR) Reg. 31, Clause 5A (2025 insertion).
    *   All such agreements in material contracts list.

Current/past directorships in listed companies with suspended/delisted shares (prior 5 years). Family relationships between directors/KMP/senior management (2023 insertion). Arrangements/understandings for selection. Service contracts with termination benefits. Borrowing powers.
    *   **Compensation of Managing Directors and/or Whole-time Directors:** Contracts appointing/fixing remuneration (prior 2 years). Compensation paid/benefits in kind by issuer/subsidiary/associate (last financial year), including contingent/deferred. Bonus/profit-sharing plan description. All such contracts in material contracts list.
    *   **Shareholding of Directors:** Including qualification shares.
    *   **Interest of Directors:** Nature/extent of interest in issuer/promotion/property acquired/proposed. Details if interest through firm/company. Sums paid.

    *   **Key Managerial Personnel (KMP) and Senior Management (2023 insertion):** Name, joining date, qualification, term, service contracts, previous employment, functions, experience. Family relationships. Arrangements/understandings for selection. Compensation paid/benefits in kind (last financial year), including contingent/deferred. Bonus/profit-sharing plan. Permanent employee status. Shareholding. Changes (other than normal retirement) in last 3 years.

    *   Reasons for high attrition of KMP/senior management compared to industry.

    *   **Company Promoters:** Brief history, changes in activities, present activities. History of companies/promoters (natural persons controlling 15%+ voting rights or on board). Change in control in prior 3 years. Declaration of PANs, Bank Account Numbers, Company Registration Numbers, RoC addresses submission to stock exchanges.

29. **Financial Statements (Indian Accounting Standards - Ind AS):**
    *   Financial information divided into restated and other financial information.
    *   **Restated Financial Information:** Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) for 3 years and stub period (if latest full year CFS older than 6 months from filing, stub period not earlier than 6 months from filing). Audited/certified by statutory auditor/CA (with Peer Review Board certificate). Restated for consistency (presentation, disclosures, accounting policies), reflecting errors, non-provisions, regrouping. Changes in accounting policies/error corrections disclosed per Ind AS 8. Quantifiable audit modifications adjusted; unquantifiable disclosed in notes. Reconciliation of audited vs. restated CFS equity/profit (loss).
    *   **Auditor Requirements:** Examination report on restated/audited financials per ICAI Guidance Note. Auditor must have valid Peer Review Board certificate at signing date. If new auditor for stub period and predecessor lacked certificate for last annual, last annual re-audited (excluding CARO, IFC, regulatory matters). Earlier certificate valid if renewal initiated and not refused.
    *   **Presentation/Disclosure:** If no subsidiary/associate/JV, separate financial statements for that year. List of related parties and all related party transactions (consolidated entities) per Ind AS 24/Companies Act 2013. Funding arrangements/inter-se guarantees among consolidated entities (excluding equity share capital), terms, conditions, transfer restrictions. For non-Ind AS companies, SEBI Circular No SEBI/HO/CFD/DIL/CIR/P/2016/47 applies.

    *   **Foreign Entities/Materiality:** Certified English translation of non-English CFS on website. Non-INR CFS translated to INR per Ind AS 21. Foreign consolidated entities' CFS audited unless not material and local law doesn't mandate. 'Material' if 10%+ of turnover, net-worth, or PBT in annual CFS. Total unaudited info in CFS not to exceed 20% of turnover, net-worth, or PBT. Foreign entities' CFS audited per local regulations or Indian standards. Foreign subsidiaries' CFS acceptable in non-Ind AS GAAP if local law requires.
    *   **Other Financial Information:** EPS (basic/diluted), Return on net worth, NAV per share, EBITDA computed per ICAI Guidance Note.

30. **Acquisitions/Divestments:**
    *   If issue proceeds for material acquisitions (20%+ of turnover, net worth, or PBT in latest annual CFS), audited balance sheets, P&L, cash flow for latest 3 financial years/stub period included.
    *   Voluntary provision for non-material acquisitions or proforma financials (certified by statutory auditor/CA with Peer Review Board certificate).
    *   If general purpose financials unavailable for acquired/divested businesses, combined/carved-out financials prepared per ICAI guidance/standards/guidelines and audited by seller's auditor.
    *   Proforma financial statements (certified by statutory auditor/CA with Peer Review Board certificate) for material subsidiaries/businesses (20%+) acquired/divested after latest disclosed financials but before filing. Prepared for at least last completed financial year/stub period. Voluntary for non-material or prior acquisitions/divestments.
    *   Single combined set of Proforma financial statements for multiple acquisitions/divestments.
    *   If acquired/divested businesses not separate entities, combined/carved-out financials per ICAI guidance.
    *   Disclosures for non-material acquisitions/divestments (fact, consideration, financing) certified by issuer's statutory auditor/CA (with Peer Review Board certificate).
    *   Voluntary inclusion of certified financial statements of acquired/divested business/subsidiary.

31. **Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A):**
    *   Based on restated Ind AS CFS.
    *   Directors' statement on significant developments since last financial year/stub period, addressing adverse impacts on trading/profitability, asset value, or ability to pay liabilities within 12 months.
    *   Factors affecting results.
    *   Discussion on results: summary of past financial results (adjusted), major income/expenditure, income/sales by major product/activity, break-up/nature of other income (if >10% of total), dependence on customers/suppliers (including foreign), impact of exchange rate fluctuations, analysis of deviation from accounting standards for sales/revenues, nature of miscellaneous income/expenditure.
    *   Comparison of last 3 years/stub period on major P&L heads, with analysis of reasons for changes (unusual events, economic changes, trends, future cost/revenue changes, sales/revenue increases, turnover by segment, new products, seasonality, dependence, competitive conditions).
    *   MD&A based on restated financial information for last 3 years and stub period.

32. **Capitalisation Statement:**
    *   Total borrowings, total equity, borrowing/equity ratios before/after issue.
    *   Based on restated CFS for latest financial year/stub period.
    *   Explanatory note for share capital changes since financial information disclosure date.
    *   Terms (Current/Non-current borrowings, Equity share capital, Other equity) as per Companies Act, 2013 Schedule III.

33. **Requirements for Indian GAAP in Restated Financial Information:**
    *   Financial information divided into restated and other financial information.
    *   **Restated Financial Information:** CFS for 3 years/stub period (if latest full year CFS older than 6 months from filing, stub period not earlier than 6 months from filing). Audited/certified by statutory auditor/CA (with Peer Review Board certificate). Prepared per Companies Act, 2013. Restated for consistency (presentation, disclosures, accounting policies), reflecting errors, non-provisions, regrouping. Changes in estimates not restated. Disclosures for error correction, accounting policy changes, estimate changes per AS 5. Quantifiable/estimable audit modifications adjusted; non-quantifiable disclosed in notes. Columnar reconciliation of audited vs. restated CFS equity/profit (loss).
    *   **Auditor Requirements:** Examination report on restated/audited financials per ICAI Guidance Notes. Auditor must have valid Peer Review Board certificate at signing date. If new auditor for stub period and predecessor lacked certificate for last annual, last annual re-audited (excluding CARO, IFC, regulatory matters). Earlier certificate valid if renewal initiated and not refused.
    *   If no subsidiary/associate/JV, separate financial statements for that year.

This document outlines extensive financial disclosure and reporting requirements for restated financial information, offer documents (including for Further Public Offers, Rights Issues, and Indian Depository Receipts), and other financial reporting under SEBI regulations.

**I. Financial Information Disclosures:**

*   **Restated Financial Information:** Requires disclosure of related parties and their transactions (AS 18/Companies Act, 2013), funding arrangements (including inter-se guarantees, terms, restrictions), and disclosures as per AS 13 and AS 14 (Indian GAAP/ICAI Guidance Notes).
*   **Separate Audited Financial Statements:** Issuer and material subsidiaries must make three years of separate audited financial statements available on the issuer's website. Non-English statements require certified English translations. Foreign currency statements must be translated to INR (Ind AS 21). Foreign consolidated entities' statements must be audited unless immaterial (contributing <10% to turnover, net-worth, or PBT) and local law doesn't mandate it; total unaudited CFS cannot exceed 20%. Audits may follow local regulations, or Indian standards if local law doesn't mandate.
*   **Other Financial Information:** Earnings per share (Basic and Diluted), Return on net worth, Net Asset Value per share, and EBITDA must be computed as per ICAI Guidance Notes.
*   **Restated Audited Financials (General):** Issuers must provide restated audited financials (standalone and consolidated) for the latest stub period and three preceding financial years, including total income, net profit/loss, equity capital, reserves/surplus, net worth, Basic/Diluted EPS, Return on net worth, and Net Asset Value per share.

**II. Acquisitions and Divestments:**

*   **Material Acquisitions (≥20% of turnover, net worth, or PBT):** If issue proceeds are used, audited balance sheets, P&L, and cash flow statements for the latest three financial years and stub period of the acquired business/entity must be included.
*   **Material Acquisitions/Divestments (≥20%) after latest disclosed financials:** Proforma financial statements are mandatory for at least the last completed financial year and stub period, prepared as per ICAI guidance and certified by a statutory auditor or ICAI Peer Review Board certified CA. Voluntary proforma statements are allowed for non-material or earlier transactions.
*   **Unavailable General Purpose Financials:** Combined/carved-out financial statements must be prepared as per ICAI guidance and audited by the seller's auditor (for acquisitions using proceeds) or certified by the issuer's auditor/ICAI Peer Review Board certified CA (for proforma statements).
*   **Non-material Acquisitions/Divestments:** Disclosures on the fact, consideration, and financing mode must be certified by the issuer's statutory auditor or an ICAI Peer Review Board certified CA.

**III. Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A):**

*   Must be based on restated Indian GAAP CFS, covering financial position and results of operations.
*   Includes a directors' statement on significant adverse developments affecting trading, profitability, asset value, or ability to pay liabilities within 12 months.
*   Discussion on factors affecting operations, summary of past financial results (three years + stub period), major income/expenditure items, income/sales by product/activity, other income break-up (if >10%), dependence on customers/suppliers (including foreign and exchange rate impact), deviations from sales recording, and nature of miscellaneous income/expenditure.
*   Comparison of major P&L heads for the last three years and stub period, analyzing changes due to unusual events, accounting policy changes, economic changes, known trends/uncertainties, future cost-revenue relationships, sales drivers, segment turnover, new product status, seasonality, supplier/customer dependence, and competitive conditions.

**IV. Capitalisation Statement:**

*   Required, showing total borrowings (short-term, long-term), total equity (share capital, reserves, surplus, money against share warrants), total capital, and the long-term borrowings/total equity ratio, both pre-issue and as adjusted for the proposed issue.
*   Based on restated Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) for the latest financial year or stub period. Any change in share capital since the financial information disclosure date must be explained.

**V. Further Public Offers (FPOs):**

*   **Fast-Track FPOs:** May disclose specific financial information if conditions like existing listing, online financial reports, no management change, and no certain relaxation-based listing are met. This includes consolidated financial statements, a limited review report (not older than six months), and material changes/commitments.
*   **Additional FPO Requirements:** Week-end prices (last four weeks), current market price, high/low prices with dates (last three years, monthly for six months), accounting ratios (EPS, RoNW, NAV, EBITDA), FPO-specific Capitalisation Statement, MD&A, directors' statement on adverse developments, factors affecting operations, and detailed discussion on results of operations.

**VI. Legal and Other Information:**

*   **Outstanding Litigations:** Disclosure of criminal proceedings, regulatory actions, disciplinary actions against promoters (last five years), consolidated tax claims, and other pending litigations based on materiality policy or if value/impact exceeds 2% of turnover, 2% of net worth, or 5% of average absolute profit/loss after tax. Criminal proceedings and regulatory actions involving KMP and senior management must also be disclosed.
*   **Outstanding Dues to Creditors:** Consolidated number and aggregate amount, dues to MSMEs, and complete details of overdues to material creditors on the company's website.
*   **Wilful Defaulters or Fraudulent Borrowers:** If the issuer, promoter, or director is declared, specific disclosures are required for each person (name, declaring bank, year, outstanding amount, steps for removal, other relevant info). This must be prominently disclosed on the cover page and in a separate chapter/section. (Amendments effective Jan 14, 2022, expanded scope and removed "in the last ten years" clause).
*   **Government Approvals:** Investment approvals, letter of intent, industrial license, non-responsibility declarations, and all material government/other approvals for business operations.
*   **Group Companies:** Names and registered office addresses of all group companies. Top five group companies (by market cap for listed, turnover for unlisted) must host specific audited financial information (reserves, sales, PAT, EPS, diluted EPS, NAV) for the preceding three years on their websites, with the offer document referring to these. Pending litigation with material impact on the issuer and common pursuits among group entities must also be disclosed.
*   **Other Regulatory and Statutory Disclosures:** Authority for issue, prohibition statement (issuer/promoters/directors not debarred by SEBI), SBO compliance, director association with securities market, eligibility, Part B compliance, mandatory disclaimer clauses (SEBI does not approve, lead manager certification, issuer responsibility), jurisdiction disclaimer, other regulatory disclaimers, designated stock exchanges, consents (directors, auditors, lead managers, etc.), expert opinion, previous public/rights issues (last five years), commission/brokerage (last five years), particulars of issuer/listed group companies/subsidiaries/associates (last three years), performance vis-à-vis objects, and price information of past issues handled by lead manager(s).

**VII. Stock Market Data for Listed Equity Shares:**

*   High, low, and average market prices for the preceding three years.
*   Monthly high and low prices for six months preceding draft offer document filing, updated until offer document filing.
*   Number of shares traded on high/low price days, total trading days, and average volume for the preceding six months.
*   Data shown separately for periods with capital structure changes.
*   Market price immediately after board resolution approving the issue.
*   Monthly trading volume for six months preceding offer document filing.
*   Information must be provided separately for each stock exchange if listed on multiple.

**VIII. Investor Grievance Redressal:**

*   Arrangements/mechanisms (including SCORES).
*   Number of complaints received/disposed of (last three years).
*   Number of complaints pending on draft offer document filing date (for issuer and five largest listed group companies).
*   Normal time taken to dispose of grievances.

**IX. Offering Information - Terms and Procedure:**

*   **Terms:** Pari passu statement (with existing shares, excluding SR shares), dividend for offer for sale, face value/issue price/price band, instrument rights, market lot, nomination facility, subscription period, minimum subscription (90% of fresh issue portion, with full refund and 15% p.a. interest for delays), composite issue rules, odd lot arrangements, transfer restrictions, new financial instrument terms, and mandatory dematerialized allotment.
*   **Procedure:** Fixed price/book building details, mandatory dematerialized securities (depository account details required, no physical allotment), single bid limits, HUF/Mutual Fund/NRI application procedures, ASBA process details, escrow mechanism, payment terms, electronic bids, bid revision rules (QIBs/non-institutional cannot lower/withdraw, retail can), price discovery, underwriting, offer document filing, pre-issue advertisement, CAN & allotment, designated date, general instructions, PAN requirement, technical rejection instances, contact for compliance officer, application disposal, Companies Act, 2013 provisions for fictitious applications (punishment under section 447), anchor investor refunds, allotment basis finalization, allotment schedule/demat credit, allotment method, allotment/refund documents ("at par" facility for non-ASBA), and refund modes (electronic transfer for specified centers, registered post for others, ASBA unblocking).

**X. Refunds and Interest for Delays:**

*   **Refund Modes:** Electronic transfer (NACH, Direct Credit, RTGS, NEFT) for Board-specified centers; registered post or ASBA unblocking for others.
*   **Interest for Delays (15% p.a.):** If allotment letters/refund orders/electronic instructions are not dispatched/given to clearing system within eight days (fixed price issue), six days (book-built issue), or fifteen days (rights issue) from issue closure. Allotment in rights issue must occur within fifteen days of closure.

**XI. Issuer Undertakings:**

*   Expeditious complaint handling, timely listing/trading formalities, advance listing application for convertible equities, funds availability for refunds/unblocking, electronic refund communication, full promoter contribution before issue opening, no further issues until current securities are listed/refunded (unless disclosed), and adequate ASBA arrangements.
*   **For Convertible Debt Instruments:** Half-yearly utilization details to debenture trustees, trustee disclosure in annual report, yearly compliance certificates, confirmation of security maintenance, and cooperation with credit rating agencies.

**XII. Issue Withdrawal:**

*   Issuer can withdraw after bidding by public notice within two days of closure and informing stock exchanges. A fresh draft offer document must be filed if withdrawn.

**XIII. Utilisation of Issue Proceeds:**

*   All public issue monies (excluding offer for sale or issues by scheduled commercial banks/public financial institutions) must be transferred to a separate bank account.
*   Utilized and unutilized monies must be disclosed under separate heads in the balance sheet, detailing purpose and investment form, until fully utilized. Promoters' contribution and reservations also require similar disclosure.

**XIV. Other General Disclosures:**

*   Restrictions on foreign ownership.
*   Description of Equity Shares and Articles of Association (rights, forfeiture, restrictions).
*   Material contracts and documents available for inspection (including online).
*   IPO grading reports.
*   Draft offer document/letter of offer must be approved by the Board and signed by all directors (including MD/Manager) and CFO/head of finance, certifying truth and correctness.
*   Declaration of compliance with Companies Act, 2013, SEBI Act, 1992, and related guidelines.

**XV. Disclosures in a Letter of Offer (Rights Issue Specifics):**

*   **Cover Page:** Type of letter, date, issuer details, nature/number/price of securities, issue size, promoter(s), wilful defaulter disclosure, "General Risk" and "Issuer's Absolute Responsibility" clauses, registrar details, issue schedule, stock exchanges, and Designated Stock Exchange.
*   **Format:** Clear, readable font (min. size ten), table of contents after front inside cover.
*   **Content:** Business summary, promoter/promoter group participation intentions (subscribe, over and above, renounce to specific investors), issuer's intention for under-subscribed portion (to specific investors), wilful defaulter/fraudulent borrower details, outstanding litigations (tabular summary, materiality thresholds), risk factors, compliance with listing regulations (last three years), investor complaints (95% redressal), actions against issuer/promoters/directors, trading suspension details, general information (contacts, credit rating, underwriting details, filing confirmation).
*   **Capital Structure:** Tabular form (authorised, issued, subscribed, paid-up capital, outstanding convertible securities, promoter/promoter group holdings, ex-rights price, shareholding pattern, >1% shareholders, non-cash consideration).
*   **Objects of the Issue:** Specific objects (loan repayment, investment/acquisition, loan to entity, long-term working capital, project funding, asset purchase, warrants/partly paid shares).
*   **Requirement of Funds:** Total project cost, phased project costs, material existing/anticipated transactions with related parties, purchase of business/interest (>50% with accountants' report and voluntary proforma financials).
*   **Acquisition of Subsidiary:** Accountants' report on profits/losses and assets/liabilities, voluntary proforma financials.
*   **Funding Plan:** Undertaking for 75% firm arrangements, details of balance, tied-up funds, excess proceeds deployment.
*   **Project Details:** Appraisal, implementation schedule, fund deployment (certified by CA), year-wise expenditure, unutilized proceeds in scheduled commercial banks.
*   **Issue Expenses:** Itemized expenses as amounts and percentages.
*   **Tax Benefits:** Special tax benefits for issuer, shareholders, material subsidiaries.
*   **Issuer's Financial Information:** Audited consolidated financial statements (last FY with comparative prior year), latest limited review financials (not older than six months), specific metrics (total income, net profit/loss, equity capital, net worth, EPS, return on net worth), and rationale for issue price.
*   **Management:** Details of manager, MD, directors (name, DOB, age, DIN, address, occupation, term expiration).
*   **Approvals:** Material pending government/regulatory approvals for issue objects.
*   **Statutory Compliance:** Authority for issue, statement of no prohibition by Board, director's association with securities market.
*   **Disclaimers:** Jurisdiction, stock exchanges, RBI, IRDAI.
*   **Application Process:** Terms of payment, procedure, time schedule for allotment/demat credit, instructions for mutual funds/NRIs/ASBA, plain paper applications, fractional entitlement.
*   **Legal Compliance:** Companies Act, 2013 provisions on fictitious/multiple applications.
*   **Timelines and Refunds:** Credit of securities/unblocking of ASBA funds within fifteen days (with interest for delays), refunds within fifteen days (with interest for delays).
*   **Basis of Allotment:** Priority for full entitlement, then additional to eligible shareholders, then to renouncees, then to specific investors.
*   **Issuer Undertakings:** As per general section.
*   **Proceeds Utilisation:** As per general section.
*   **Other Disclosures:** Foreign ownership restrictions, dematerialized allotment, material contracts.

**XVI. Exemptions and Specific Document Requirements:**

*   **FPO/Fast Track Public Issues:** May omit certain capital structure and management disclosures under specific conditions (e.g., online financial results, investor grievance mechanism, lead manager certification, no material changes).
*   **Abridged Prospectus:** Must contain material information in a Board-specified format (Annexure I), submitted to Board, printed in A4 booklet form (max five sheets), with specific font size and application form placement. Generic information is in a separate General Information Document (GID).
*   **SME Issues:** Must include market maker details.
*   **Placement Document (for QIBs):** Includes disclaimer, glossary, advisors, issue summary, risk factors, market prices (3 years, 6 months, monthly), use of proceeds, capitalization statement, dividends (3 years), selected financial info, audited financial statements (3 years, consolidated/unconsolidated, with all components, auditor report, accounting policies, notes, related party transactions, liquidity/capital resources), latest reviewed financials, voluntary proforma financials, MD&A, industry/business description, organizational structure, board/senior management, latest shareholding pattern, and taxation aspects.

**XVII. Indian Depository Receipts (IDR) Offer Document (Schedule VIII):**

*   **General Instructions:** Draft prospectus can be public or confidential (then public updated draft for 21 days). Prospectus and financials (issuer, subsidiaries, associates) must be in simple English. Must contain material, true, adequate information. Filed by lead manager(s) with Board and Registrar of Companies, New Delhi, certified by two authorized signatories (whole-time director, CFO/Chief Accounts Officer). Domestic depository agreement furnished. Lead manager(s) sign due diligence certificate and make statement. Disclaimer for statements outside prospectus.
*   **The Issue:** Summary of offer terms.
*   **Forward-looking Statements:** Paragraph on.
*   **General Information:** Definitions, contacts, punishment for fictitious applications, refund of excess subscription, 15% p.a. interest for delayed allotment/refund, timely issue declaration, issue dates (3-10 working days subscription), lead manager declaration on underwriter resources, separate domestic bank account for IDR monies, prospectus/form availability, payment details, investor grievances (Indian court jurisdiction).
*   **Risk Factors:** Related to business, country, IDR/underlying shares; classified as project-specific/internal or external; determined by materiality; include issuer's envisaged risk and proposals to address it.
*   **Recent Developments:** Important events from last two financial years.
*   **Exchange-wise Market Price Information:** High, low, average daily trading volume for shares (last three calendar years by quarter, last calendar year by month, month preceding prospectus date), opening/closing price and volume on last day of month preceding prospectus date.
*   **Dividends:** Policy, rate/amount (last five FYs), regulatory framework, depository arrangements, changes/time gap, dividend yield, taxation.
*   **Exchange Rates:** Brief history, high/low/average (last five years, last twelve months).
*   **Foreign Investment and Exchange Controls:** Relevant laws/regulations of home country.
*   **Objects of the Issue/Use of Proceeds:** Purpose, project cost break-up, financing, deployment.
*   **Interim Use of Funds:** Funds in bank with 'A' or above credit rating by international agency.
*   **Capitalisation Statement:** Short-term debt, long-term debt, shareholders’ funds, long-term debt/equity, pre-issue.
*   **Capital Structure:** Authorised, issued, subscribed, paid-up capital, present issue size, share premium, notes.
*   **Shareholder and Share Class Information:** Major shareholders, different classes of shares.
*   **Financial Information (IDR Specific):**
    *   Format can align with home country. Issuer specifies Indian Accounting Standards, IFRS, or US GAAP. Currency restricted to Sterling Pound, Euro, Yen, or US Dollar.
    *   **Audited Statements:** Consolidated/unconsolidated for three preceding FYs, prepared as per chosen GAAP. Components include Auditors' Report, Balance Sheets, Income Statements, Schedules, Statements of Changes in Stockholders’ Equity, Cash Flow Statements, Accounting Policies, Notes, Subsidiary Statements (for unconsolidated), Related Party Transactions, Liquidity/Capital Resources.
    *   If IFRS/US GAAP, audited by professional accountant/CPA in home country adhering to ISA.
    *   Statutory auditor's report on audited financials (3 years) required if mandated by home country law, detailing profits/losses, assets, liabilities, cash flow. Gap between issue opening and report date <120 days. Report must present financials in INR (at closing exchange rate) in tabular format.
    *   **Interim Financial Statements:** Required if gap between latest audited statements and issue opening >180 days, covering period ending <180 days prior to issue opening. Material changes sufficient if gap ≤180 days. Foreign banks may provide limited review report for interim period.
    *   **Reconciliation:** If US GAAP, reconciliation with Indian Accounting Standards required. If IFRS, summary of significant differences with Indian Accounting Standards required.
    *   **No Statutory Audit:** If home country law doesn't require audit, report prepared as per Indian Accounting Standards, certified by Indian CA, for three preceding FYs, detailing profits/losses, assets, liabilities, cash flow. Gap <120 days. Report must present financials in INR (at closing exchange rate) in tabular form. Interim financials required under similar conditions.
    *   **Investment in Other Bodies Corporate:** Names, addresses, financial reports if IDR proceeds used for investment.
*   **Subsequent Developments and Management Discussion:** Directors' statement on material adverse circumstances (trading, profitability, asset value, ability to pay liabilities within 12 months). MD&A comparing recent FY with previous three, covering business overview, operational factors, changes in income/expenditure, trends, future cost/revenue changes, sales drivers, segment turnover, new product status, seasonality, supplier/customer dependence, and competitive conditions.
*   **Industry and Business Overview:** Market, competition, production, capacity, exports, demand/supply forecasts.
*   **Issuing Company Details:** Main object, history, present business, project location/details/schedule, products/services, R&D, patents, property/plants/equipment, financial/other defaults, underwriting, experts, sources for additional information, enforcement of civil liabilities against foreign persons.
*   **Subsidiaries and Associates:** For last three years (based on audited statements or certified by Board/management/local CPA if no audit), information on incorporation date, activities, equity capital, reserves (excluding revaluation), sales, PAT, EPS, NAV.
*   **Management:** Background of promoters (or 5%+ equity holders), board of directors, key managerial personnel, senior management (details, remuneration, relation to promoters, equity holding, duration, organizational structure, board practices, employee information).
*   **Securities Market of Country of Incorporation:** Brief history, stock exchange/listing regulations, securities market regulator (including MoU with Board/IOSCO), disclosure requirements, stock exchanges, Takeover/Buyback Code, economic reforms, restrictions on foreign ownership, financial sector overview, nature of securities trading market, impact of foreign location on Indian securities law enforcement, and comparative analysis of corporate governance provisions.
*   **IDR and IDR Holder Rights:** Description of IDR, dividends/distributions/rights, voting rights (if any and how exercised), record dates/disclosure, reports/communications, conversion procedure, and governing law.
*   **Transfer Provisions:** For IDRs and underlying shares after conversion.
*   **Depository Information:** Domestic depository, overseas custodian bank, and depository agreement.
*   **Approvals:** Status of government/regulatory approvals in home country and India.
*   **Taxation Framework:** In India and country of incorporation/listing.

This document outlines extensive disclosure requirements for Indian Depository Receipts (IDRs) across various stages: the main prospectus, abridged prospectus, and addendum for rights issues, along with regulations for public communications, book-building, and allotment.

**I. Disclosure Requirements for Indian Depository Receipts (IDRs):**

*   **Main Prospectus (Sections 28-32):**
    *   **Litigations & Defaults:** Material litigations, liabilities, and defaults of the issuing company, promoters, controlling shareholders, directors, subsidiaries, and associates must be disclosed. Materiality considers individual/collective, qualitative/quantitative, and present/future impacts.
    *   **Issue Price Basis:** Justification requires pre-issue EPS (last 3 years, adjusted), pre-issue P/E, average return on net worth (last 3 years), minimum return on increased net worth to maintain pre-issue EPS, NAV per share (last balance sheet and post-issue vs. issue price). These ratios must be compared with industry averages/peers (source indicated). Face value of IDR is required. Projected earnings cannot be used. Ratios must account for compulsory conversions and outstanding options.
    *   **Company Charter:** Main provisions of Articles of Association/Main Charter.
    *   **Inspection Documents:** Place for inspection of documents (Rule 7, Companies (Issue of IDRs) Rules, 2004), prospectus, financial statements, and auditor's report during business hours.
    *   **Other Information:** Mandatory legal vetting, consents from lead manager(s), overseas custodian bank, domestic depository, and other intermediaries, and fees/expenses payable to them.

*   **Abridged Prospectus (Part B):**
    *   **Format:** A4 size, max 5 sheets (printed both sides), Times New Roman size 11 (or equivalent), 1.0 line spacing. Application form positioned to avoid mutilation. Submitted to the Board.
    *   **Key Disclosures (1-17):**
        *   **General:** Name, address, contact details (issuer, domestic depository, overseas custodian bank with India office, lead manager(s), underwriter, advisors, intermediaries, India-based compliance officer). Stock exchanges for listing, issue dates, payment details, investor grievances, and issuer undertaking to Indian court jurisdiction.
        *   **Capital Structure:** Pre-issue shares and percentage holding for Promoter & Promoter Group and Public.
        *   **Terms:** Issue size, proposed listing exchanges, designated exchange, procedure, timeline.
        *   **Instructions:** How to apply, nationality/residency declarations (Indian resident, Indian resident for NRI non-repatriation, Indian non-resident for non-repatriation), PAN (mandatory, applications without PAN rejected), bank details for refunds (including ECS), physical securities trading limits, special tax benefits (section/substance), and restrictions on IDR investments/fungibility.
        *   **Particulars:** Objects, project cost, financing, appraising/monitoring agencies.
        *   **IDR Description & Rights:** Brief description, dividends, distributions, voting rights, record dates, reports, conversion, governing law.
        *   **Business Model:** Max 500 words.
        *   **Market Data:** Exchange-wise stock market data (High, Low, Average Daily Trading Volume) for last 3 calendar years (quarterly), last calendar year (monthly), and month preceding prospectus date (daily, opening/closing price, volume).
        *   **Risk Factors:** Min 5, max 10, limited to 500 words.
        *   **Litigations & Defaults:** Total number/amount, brief details of top 5 material outstanding litigations.
        *   **Material Developments:** After latest balance sheet date and their impact.
        *   **Board of Directors:** Name, designation, experience (20-40 words per director).
        *   **Financial Performance:** Last 3 years (audited, tabular): Balance Sheet (Equity Capital, Reserves, Borrowings), P&L (Sales, Gross/Net profit, dividend paid). Changes in accounting policies and their effect. Extracted auditor's report data (net profit before/after extraordinary items, extraordinary items).
        *   **Investor Grievances & Redressal System.**
        *   **Taxation Law, Tax Treaties, and Impact for IDR Holders.**
        *   **Domestic Depository, Overseas Custodian Bank, and Depository Agreement details.**
        *   **Signatories.**

*   **Addendum for Rights Issue (Part C):**
    *   **General:** For listed issuers, home country regulations may prevail if they meet requirements.
    *   **Cover Page:** Front (issuer name/logo, addresses, IDR details, disclaimer, risk advisory, issuer responsibility, lead manager(s), registrar, issue schedule, listing approvals). Back (white).
    *   **Instructions:** Record date, payment terms, allotment/credit timeline, how to apply, plain paper applications (no renunciation), punishment for fictitious applications, refund modes, 15% p.a. interest for delayed dispatch of allotment letters/refunds.
    *   **General Information:** Contact details for domestic depository, overseas custodian bank (with India office), merchant banker, underwriter, syndicate, bankers, auditors, legal advisors, experts, counsel, and India-based Company Secretary/compliance officer. Inter-se allocation of responsibilities among lead managers.
    *   **Company & Issue Specifics:** Underwriting details (including financial capacity declaration), issue method/timetable, transfer of proceeds to a separate domestic bank account, document availability, payment mode, issuer history, corporate structure, business, major events, and compliance status.
    *   **Management:** Comprehensive details for executive/whole-time directors (name, DOB, age, qualifications, experience, address, occupation, term, other directorships), family relationships, arrangements with major shareholders/customers/suppliers, and service contracts/termination benefits.
    *   **Financial Information:** Convenience translations into INR (at closing exchange rates) of latest annual audited consolidated P&L, assets, liabilities, cash flow, and latest periodical results. Use of one standard financial unit. Link to detailed Annual Report.
    *   **Risk Factors:** Associated with business, country, and IDR/underlying shares. Classified as project-specific/internal or external/beyond company control. Materiality considers collective, qualitative, and future impacts.
    *   **Capital Structure:** Authorized, issued, subscribed (including convertibles), paid-up (segregating IDRs), outstanding options, latest shareholding/IDR holding patterns, shareholders holding >3%, IDR lock-in/pledge/encumbrance by promoters, and promoter/group IDR acquisitions in the last 6 months.
    *   **Particulars:** Objects, project cost, financing, deployment of proceeds, promoter/director interest, interim use of funds (in 'A' rated bank), and special tax benefits for IDR holders.
    *   **Market Price & Exchange Rate:** Week-end prices (last 4 weeks), highest/lowest equity share prices with dates, stock market quotations (high/low for last 3 years, monthly high/low for last 6 months) for shares and IDRs. Exchange rate history (issuer's home country to India), high/low/average rates for last 12 months.
    *   **Litigations, Defaults, Material Developments:** Material litigation, liabilities, and defaults (including arrears/potential liabilities) concerning issuer, promoters, controlling shareholders, directors, subsidiaries, and associates (materiality factors apply). Material developments after latest balance sheet date and their impact (as per home country regulations).
    *   **Regulatory & Statutory:** Authority for issue, resolutions passed. Statement of no prohibition from capital markets by SEBI or home country regulator. Disclosure if issuer/promoters/directors/controlling persons are wilful defaulters. Mandatory disclaimer clauses (bold capital letters) regarding SEBI's non-approval, issuer/lead manager responsibility, jurisdiction, and disclaimers from stock exchanges and RBI. Broad details of fees to intermediaries. Investor grievance redressal arrangements and typical disposal times.
    *   **Undertakings & Declarations:** Issuer undertakes expeditious complaint handling, listing formalities within 7 working days, funds for refunds, electronic refund communications, adequate application collection/processing (including ASBA). IDRs credited/refunds made within 15 days (with interest for delays). Board statement on proceeds utilization. Disclosure of foreign ownership restrictions. Addendum approval by Board, signed by all directors, CEO, CFO. Declaration of compliance with corporate laws and Companies (Issue of Indian Depository Receipts) Rules, 2004, and truth/correctness of disclosures.

*   **Abridged Letter of Offer (Part D):** For rights issues of IDRs by listed issuers, it must include disclosures as per home country regulations and Part B of this Schedule. Order of items should correspond to the full offer document. Additional disclosures include application forms, rights entitlement ratio, fractional entitlements, renunciation, application for additional IDRs, and promoters' intention to subscribe. General instructions specify information from Part A, minimum font size (Times New Roman size 11, 1.0 line spacing), and proper positioning of the application form.

**II. Public Communications and Publicity Materials (SCHEDULE IX & X):**

*   **General Principles:** All public communications (advertisements, interviews, reports, press releases) must be truthful, fair, non-manipulative, non-deceptive, clear, concise, and understandable. They must reproduce full information from the draft/offer document.
*   **Content Restrictions:** No issue slogans/brand names (except existing commercial names), expletives, non-factual/unsubstantiated titles, technical/complex language, excessive details, or statements promising rapid revenue/profit increases. Advertisements must not display models, celebrities, fictional characters, landmarks, or caricatures. TV advertisements must not appear as crawlers, and risk factors should not be scrolled.
*   **Financial Data:** If presented, must include particulars for the past three years (revenue/sales, net profit, share capital, reserves/other equity, EPS, dividends, book values).
*   **Required Disclosures:** Advertisements/research reports with highlights must prominently advise referring to the draft/offer document for risk factors and details (min point seven size).
*   **Timing-based Guidelines:**
    *   **Before DRHP filing:** Consistent with past practices, or prominently disclose intent to make a public issue and file a DRHP.
    *   **After DRHP filing until allotment:** Prominently disclose proposed issue, DRHP/final offer document filing, and its availability on websites of the Board, lead manager(s), and stock exchanges (excluding product/service ads).
*   **Post-filing Material Developments:** Issuer must make prompt, true, and fair disclosure via public notices in all newspapers where pre-issue advertisements were released.
*   **Information Integrity:** No material/information not contained in the offer document shall be released.
*   **Approval:** All issue advertisements and public communications require approval from the lead manager(s) responsible for marketing, with copies provided to all lead managers.
*   **Advertisement Specifics (Schedule X):**
    *   Risk factors must have equal importance (min point seven print size). Billboard ads are restricted. No direct/indirect incentives to investors. Product ads must not reference issuer performance during the public issue period. No extraneous information to specific investors/analysts. Lead manager(s) must submit a compliance certificate for news reports in specified media.
    *   **Pre-issue and Price Band Advertisement (Part A):** Public announcement, not an offer.
