**Board's Powers (Chapter V-A, VI):**
*   **Power to Relax (Regulation 31A):** The Board may exempt persons for up to twelve months for innovation testing in a "regulatory sandbox."
*   **Power to Issue Directions (Regulation 32):** The Board can issue directions or orders (e.g., divestment, transfer to Investor Protection and Education Fund, debarment from capital market, directing open offers or interest payments) in the interest of investors and the securities market, adhering to natural justice.
*   **Power to Remove Difficulties (Regulation 33):** The Board may issue clarifications or guidelines.

**Repeal and Savings (Regulation 35):**
*   The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 1997, are repealed.
*   Savings provisions ensure that actions taken under the 1997 regulations are deemed valid under the 2011 regulations, and ongoing open offers initiated under the 1997 regulations must be completed under those repealed regulations.

**Amendments to other regulations (Regulation 34 and Schedule):**
*   The document also details amendments to the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2009, clarifying their applicability to certain SAST provisions, timelines for preferential allotments, and disclosure requirements for ex-rights prices.

This document is an Extraordinary publication in THE GAZETTE OF INDIA, Part III - Section 4, published on September 11, 2018, by the SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA (SEBI) from Mumbai. It contains NOTIFICATION No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2018/31 regarding the SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA (ISSUE OF CAPITAL AND DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS) REGULATIONS, 2018. These regulations, made under section 30 of the SEBI Act, 1992, came into force on the sixtieth day from their publication.

**Chapter I: Preliminary Aspects and Definitions**
The regulations outline preliminary aspects, including their short title and commencement, and define numerous key terms. Examples of defined terms include "Anchor investor," "Application supported by blocked amount (ASBA)," "Book building," "Fugitive economic offender," "Green shoe option," "Initial Public Offer (IPO)," "Innovators Growth Platform," "Qualified Institutional Buyer (QIB)," "Retail Individual Investor (RII)," "Senior Management" (inserted w.e.f. 31.01.2023), "SR Equity Shares" (inserted w.e.f. 29.07.2019), and "Wilful Defaulter or a Fraudulent Borrower" (substituted w.e.f. 14.1.2022). Undefined terms derive meaning from the SEBI Act, Companies Act, 2013, Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, or Depositories Act, 1996.

These regulations apply to IPOs by unlisted issuers, rights issues by listed issuers (clause "where the aggregate value of the issue is fifty crore rupees or more;" omitted w.e.f. 08.04.2025), further public offers (FPOs), preferential issues, qualified institutions placements (QIPs) by listed issuers, IPOs and rights issues of Indian depository receipts (IDRs), IPOs by small and medium enterprises (SMEs), listings on the Innovators Growth Platform (substituted w.e.f. 05.04.2019), and bonus issues by listed issuers. They generally do not apply to certain issues under clauses (b), (d), and (e) of sub-regulation (1) of regulation 9 of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.

**I. Initial Public Offers (IPOs)**
An issuer must satisfy specified conditions at the date of filing the draft offer document with the Board and the offer document with the Registrar of Companies.

*   **Ineligibility (Regulation 5):** An issuer is ineligible if the issuer, its promoters, promoter group, directors, or selling shareholders are debarred by SEBI (unless debarment is over), or if any of its promoters or directors is a promoter/director of another debarred company (unless debarment is over). Ineligibility also applies if the issuer or any of its promoters/directors is a "wilful defaulter or a fraudulent borrower" (substituted w.e.f. 14.01.2022) or a fugitive economic offender. Outstanding convertible securities or other rights entitling a person to receive equity shares are generally restricted, with exceptions.
*   **Eligibility (Regulation 6):** An issuer is eligible if, on a restated and consolidated basis, it has:
    *   Net Tangible Assets of at least ₹3 crore in each of the preceding three full years, with not more than 50% in monetary assets (unless the IPO is entirely an offer for sale or excess monetary assets are committed to business).
    *   Average Operating Profit of at least ₹15 crore during the preceding three years, with operating profit in each of those three years.
    *   Net Worth of at least ₹1 crore in each of the preceding three full years.
    *   If the name changed within the last year, at least 50% of the revenue for the preceding full year must be from the activity indicated by the new name.
    If these conditions are not met, an issuer may still be eligible if the issue is book-built and at least 75% of the net offer is allotted to QIBs, with a refund if this fails.
*   **Special Conditions for Issuers with SR Equity Shares (Regulation 6(3)):** An issuer with SR equity shares can do an IPO of ordinary shares for Main Board listing if it is technology-intensive, the SR shareholder's net worth (determined by a Registered Valuer) is not more than ₹1,000 crore (substituted w.e.f. 26.10.2021), SR shares were issued only to executive promoters/founders, and the issue was authorized by a special resolution detailing size and voting ratio. SR equity shares must specify differential dividends, sunset provisions, and matters where they have ordinary voting rights. They must be issued before DRHP filing and held for at least three months before RHP filing (updated from six months). Voting rights must be 2:1 to 10:1 (whole numbers) compared to ordinary shares, with the same face value, and only one class of SR equity shares.
*   **General Conditions (Regulation 7):** An issuer must apply for in-principle listing approval, enter a depository agreement, ensure promoter-held securities are dematerialized, have all partly paid-up shares fully paid or forfeited, and make firm arrangements for 75% of project finance (excluding public issue amount). The combined amount for general corporate purposes and objects without identified acquisition/investment targets cannot exceed 35% of the amount raised, with the latter specifically not exceeding 25% (unless specific disclosures are made for identified targets).
*   **Offer for Sale (Regulation 8):** Only fully paid-up equity shares held by sellers for at least one year prior to DRHP filing can be offered, with exceptions for government companies, shares from court-approved schemes, and bonus issues from free reserves. For issues under Regulation 6(2), shareholders holding over 20% of pre-issue shareholding can offer a maximum of 50% of their holding, while those holding less than 20% can offer a maximum of 10%.
*   **Convertible Debt Instruments (Regulations 9-12):** An issuer can make an IPO of convertible debt instruments without a prior equity IPO if not in default on public debt for over six months, requiring a credit rating, debenture trustee, and debenture redemption reserve. Secured instruments need sufficient unencumbered assets. Optionally convertible debt instruments require positive consent for conversion, or redemption if not converted. Convertible debt instruments cannot finance, provide loans to, or acquire shares of promoter group or group companies, unless fully convertible with a conversion period less than eighteen months.
*   **Issue of Warrants (Regulation 13):** Warrants can be issued with a tenure not exceeding eighteen months, requiring upfront payment of at least 25% of the exercise price, with forfeiture for non-exercise.
*   **Minimum Promoters’ Contribution (Regulation 14):** Promoters must hold at least 20% of the post-issue capital. Shortfalls can be met by specific entities (e.g., AIFs, FVCIs, banks, PFIs, insurance companies) up to 10% of post-issue capital. This contribution can be in equity shares or convertible securities, with specific pricing and timing requirements. The amount for promoters' contribution must be kept in an escrow account.
*   **Securities Ineligible for Minimum Promoters’ Contribution (Regulation 15):** Generally, securities acquired for non-cash consideration involving revaluation, bonus issues from revaluation reserves, or those acquired by promoters/specified entities in the preceding one year at a price lower than the IPO price are ineligible (with exceptions). Securities from partnership/LLP conversions (unless capital existed for over one year) and pledged securities are also ineligible.
*   **Lock-in of Specified Securities (Regulations 16-22):** Promoters' minimum contribution is locked-in for eighteen months (or three years if majority issue proceeds are for capital expenditure). Promoters' excess holding is locked-in for six months (or one year for capital expenditure). SR Equity Shares are locked-in until conversion or the specified period, whichever is later. Pre-issue capital (non-promoters) is locked-in for six months, with exemptions. Locked-in securities are non-transferable but can be pledged as collateral for specific loans, with the lock-in continuing for the transferee upon invocation. They can be transferred to other promoters/promoter group members or other persons holding locked-in securities, but the lock-in continues.
*   **Appointment of Intermediaries and Compliance Officer (Regulation 23):** The issuer must appoint one or more SEBI-registered merchant bankers as lead manager(s) (at least one non-associate), other SEBI-registered intermediaries, a SEBI-registered registrar to the issue, and a qualified company secretary as compliance officer.
*   **Disclosures in and Filing of Offer Documents (Regulations 24-26):** Draft and final offer documents must contain true, adequate, and not more than six-month-old material disclosures. Lead manager(s) must exercise due diligence. Three copies of the draft offer document are filed with SEBI through lead manager(s), along with fees and due diligence certificates. SEBI may issue observations within thirty days. The draft offer document must be made public for comments for at least twenty-one days on websites and through public announcements in newspapers.
*   **Pricing (Regulations 27-30):** The face value, price band, or issue price must be disclosed prominently. The issuer determines the price in consultation with lead manager(s) or via book building. For book-built issues, the cap on the price band must be 105-120% of the floor price, and the floor/final price not less than face value. The floor price or price band must be announced at least two working days before issue opening. Differential pricing allows up to a 10% discount for retail individual investors, retail individual shareholders, or employees (excluding anchor investors).
*   **Issuance Conditions and Procedure (Regulations 31-39):** The minimum offer to the public is subject to the Securities Contracts (Regulations) Rules, 1957.
    *   **Book Building (Regulation 6(1)):** Not less than 35% of the net offer to retail individual investors, not less than 15% to non-institutional investors, and not more than 50% to QIBs (with 5% for mutual funds). Up to 60% of the QIB portion can go to anchor investors. Non-institutional investor portion is split into one-third for applications between ₹2-10 lakh and two-thirds for over ₹10 lakh (effective 01.04.2022/01.07.2022 for large issues).
    *   **Book Building (Regulation 6(2)):** Not more than 10% to retail individual investors, not more than 15% to non-institutional investors, and not less than 75% to QIBs (with 5% for mutual funds).
    *   **Non-Book Building:** Minimum 50% to retail individual investors.
    Reservations are permitted for employees (up to 5% of post-issue capital, individual allotment up to ₹2 lakh, or ₹5 lakh for under-subscription) and shareholders (up to 10% of issue size). Abridged prospectuses must accompany application forms. Bids must use the ASBA facility. Grading from credit rating agencies is optional.
*   **Underwriting:** For non-book built issues, underwriting agreements must be in place before filing the prospectus. For book-built issues, lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s) underwrite the issue, but at least 75% of the net offer compulsorily allotted to QIBs for eligibility cannot be underwritten. Underwriting obligations must cover at least the minimum subscription. Regulation 38, concerning security deposits, was omitted w.e.f. May 18, 2024.
*   **Monitoring Agency (Regulation 41):** Required if issue size (excluding offer for sale) exceeds ₹100 crore (not for banks, public financial institutions, or insurance companies). A SEBI-registered credit rating agency monitors the use of proceeds, submitting quarterly reports until 100% of proceeds are utilized. The issuer's board and management must comment on findings, and the report must be publicly disseminated on the issuer's website and submitted to stock exchange(s) within 45 days from the end of each quarter.
*   **Public Communications, Advertisements, and Research Reports (Regulation 42, 43):** Must comply with Schedule IX. A pre-issue and price band advertisement is required after RHP/prospectus filing, in specified newspapers, following Schedule X. No advertisements implying full/oversubscription or indicating investor response are permitted during the subscription period.
*   **Issue Opening (Regulation 44):** A public issue may open within twelve months from the Board's observations and at least three working days after filing the RHP/prospectus with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
*   **Minimum Subscription (Regulation 45):** Must be at least 90% of the offer (excluding offer for sale). If not met, all application monies must be refunded forthwith, no later than four days from issue closure.
*   **Subscription Period (Regulation 46):** At least three working days and not more than ten working days. If the price band is revised, the bidding period must be extended for a minimum of three working days. Extensions for force majeure are possible for a minimum of one working day.
*   **Application and Minimum Application Value (Regulation 47):** A person cannot apply for more than the total securities offered to the public in the net offer category. Non-institutional investors' maximum application is capped. The minimum application value must be between ₹10,000 and ₹15,000, with applications in multiples. The minimum sum payable on application is 25% of the issue price (full price for offer for sale).
*   **Manner of Calls (Regulation 48):** Outstanding subscription money must be called within twelve months of allotment. Failure to pay results in forfeiture of shares/money, unless a monitoring agency is appointed.
*   **Allotment Procedure (Regulation 49):** Allotment cannot be made if prospective allottees are less than one thousand, and cannot exceed offered securities (except for 1% rounding off). Allotment to non-retail, non-institutional, and anchor investors is proportionate. Value of specified securities allotted under specific reservations is capped (₹2 lakh for retail, ₹5 lakh for eligible employees). Retail investors receive at least the minimum bid lot, then proportionately. Non-institutional investors (w.e.f. 1.4.2022/1.7.2022) receive at least the minimum application size, then proportionately. The basis of allotment is finalized fairly by authorized employees of the designated stock exchange, lead manager(s), and registrars.
*   **Allotment, Refund, and Interest (Regulation 50):** Issuer and lead manager(s) must ensure allotment/refund/unblocking within the Board-specified period. If not completed, the issuer must pay 15% per annum interest.
*   **Post-Issue Advertisements (Regulation 51):** Lead manager(s) must release an advertisement within ten days of completion of activities, detailing subscription, allotment basis, application statistics, refunds, credit of securities, and listing application date. This must be published in specified national and regional newspapers and on stock exchange websites.
*   **Post-Issue Responsibilities of Lead Manager(s) (Regulation 52):** Lead manager(s) remain responsible until the issue process is complete, investor grievances are redressed, applicants receive securities/credit/refund, and listing/trading permission is obtained. They coordinate with intermediaries and report omissions/commissions to the Board.
*   **Release of Subscription Money (Regulation 53):** Lead manager(s) confirm to bankers for money release or refund. If listing/trading permission is not obtained, the issuer must refund all monies within four days (w.e.f. 14.1.2022) of rejection intimation. Failure to repay within this period incurs 15% per annum interest from the fifth day (w.e.f. 14.1.2022), with the issuer and defaulting directors jointly and severally liable.
*   **Reporting of Transactions (Regulation 54):** The issuer must ensure all security transactions by promoters and the promoter group between the filing of the draft offer document/offer document and issue closure are reported to stock exchange(s) within twenty-four hours. (This regulation was substituted w.e.f. 08.03.2025, with prior text provided).
*   **Post-Issue Reports (Regulation 55):** Lead manager(s) must submit a final post-issue report and a due diligence certificate within seven days of allotment basis finalization or refund if the issue fails.
*   **Restrictions on Further Issue (Regulation 56):** An issuer cannot make further issues between draft offer document filing and listing/refund, except for employee stock option schemes or stock appreciation right schemes (w.e.f. 08.03.2025) with full disclosures.
*   **Price Stabilisation (Regulation 57):** Issuers may use a green shoe option (max 15% over-allotment) for price stabilization for up to thirty days post-listing. Requires shareholder authorization, a lead manager as stabilising agent, and agreements for borrowing securities from promoters/pre-issue shareholders. Specific disclosures, special accounts, and reporting to SEBI are mandated.
*   **Alteration of Rights (Regulation 58):** Terms of specified securities cannot be altered adversely without 3/4 written consent or a special resolution of holders.
*   **Exit Opportunity (Regulation 59):** Promoters/controlling shareholders must provide an exit offer to dissenting shareholders (as per Companies Act, 2013) for changes in objects or contract terms related to objects in the offer document, unless there are no identifiable promoters/controlling shareholders.
*   **Chapter IIA: IPO through Pre-filing (w.e.f. 21.11.2022):** Provides an alternative IPO process. The issuer files a confidential draft offer document, makes a public announcement, receives Board observations (30 days), files an "updated draft red herring prospectus-I" (public for 21 days), and then an "updated draft red herring prospectus-II." Limited marketing to QIBs is permitted. Outstanding convertible securities/rights must be converted before Board observations (with exceptions). A public issue can open within eighteen months from Board observations if an updated DRHP-I is filed within sixteen months.

**II. Rights Issue**

*   **Eligibility (Regulation 60, 61, 62):** Conditions must be met at the time of filing the draft letter of offer (DLOO) with stock exchange(s) and the letter of offer (LOO) with the Board/stock exchange(s) (w.e.f. 08.04.2025). Ineligible if the issuer, promoters, promoter group, or directors are debarred by SEBI, or if equity shares are suspended from trading as a disciplinary measure (w.e.f. 08.04.2025). Must have in-principle listing approval, all partly paid-up shares fully paid or forfeited, and firm finance for 75% of project capital expenditures. General corporate purposes cannot exceed 25% of the amount raised. Combined general corporate purposes and unidentified acquisition/investment targets cannot exceed 35% (unidentified target max 25%) (w.e.f. 14.01.2022). If the issuer/promoter/director is a wilful defaulter/fraudulent borrower, promoters/promoter group cannot renounce rights (except within the group or to specific disclosed investors). SR shareholders cannot renounce rights, and SR shares remain locked-in until conversion.
*   **Convertible Debt Instruments (Regulation 63, 64, 65, 66):** Require a credit rating, appointment of a debenture trustee, and creation of a debenture redemption reserve. Secured instruments require sufficient, unencumbered assets. Roll-over of non-convertible portions (if >₹10 crore) requires 75% holder approval and redemption for non-consenting holders. Conversion of Optionally Convertible Debt Instruments (OCDIs) requires positive consent; holders must have an option not to convert if the conversion price wasn't determined at issue. Cannot be issued to finance/loan/acquire shares of promoter group/group companies, unless fully convertible and conversion period is less than eighteen months.
*   **Warrants (Regulation 67):** Tenure cannot exceed eighteen months. Exercise price/formula must be determined upfront and disclosed, with at least 25% of consideration received upfront. Consideration is forfeited if the option is not exercised within three months.
*   **Record Date (Regulation 68):** Issuer announces a record date. Withdrawal of a rights issue after announcing the record date makes the issuer ineligible for listing any specified securities for twelve months.
*   **Intermediaries (Regulation 69):** Issuer must appoint Board-registered intermediaries (e.g., bankers, registrars) and ensure agreements do not limit liabilities. Issuer cannot appoint itself as registrar.
*   **Disclosures and Filing (Regulation 70, 71, 72):** DLOO and LOO must contain material, true, and adequate disclosures (Part B of Schedule VI), with information not more than six months old. Disclose if the issuer/promoter/director is a "wilful defaulter or a fraudulent borrower." The issuer files DLOO with stock exchange(s) and LOO with stock exchanges/designated stock exchange and the Board (w.e.f. 08.04.2025). DLOO and LOO must be hosted on websites and match filed versions.
*   **Pricing (Regulation 73):** Issuer decides the issue price before the record date, in consultation with the designated stock exchange. The issue price cannot be less than the face value.
*   **Reservations (Regulation 74):** Equity shares must be reserved for holders of outstanding compulsorily convertible debt instruments, proportionate to their convertible part, issued on the same terms as the rights issue.
*   **ASBA (Regulation 76):** Applicants must apply through the ASBA facility.
*   **Availability and Despatch (Regulation 77):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) ensures LOO and issue materials are available with various entities. LOO and application forms must be despatched to existing shareholders at least three days before issue opening.
*   **Credit of Rights Entitlements (Regulation 77A):** Rights entitlements must be credited to demat accounts before issue opening, and allotment must be in dematerialized form.
*   **Allotment to Specific Investors (Regulation 77B, w.e.f. 08.04.2025):** Applications by specific investors must be made on the first day of issue opening before 11 A.M., with status disclosed by 11:30 A.M. No withdrawal is permitted for these applications.
*   **Plain Paper Applications (Regulation 78):** Shareholders not receiving forms can apply on plain paper, provided all required details are specified. Dual applications (form and plain paper) may be rejected.
*   **Underwriting (Regulation 81):** If desired, the issuer appoints SEBI-registered merchant bankers/stock brokers. Underwriting is limited to the entitlement of non-promoter shareholders. (Lead manager(s) minimum underwriting obligations omitted w.e.f. 08.04.2025).
*   **Monitoring Agency (Regulation 82):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) must arrange for a SEBI-registered credit rating agency to monitor the use of issue proceeds, submitting quarterly reports until 100% of proceeds *actually raised* (w.e.f. 28.09.2020) are utilized.
*   **Advertisement Requirements (Regulation 84):** An advertisement must be published at least two days (w.e.f. 2019) before issue opening in specified newspapers, disclosing despatch dates, centres for duplicate forms, plain paper application details, and specific investor details (w.e.f. 2025). No ads implying full/oversubscription during the subscription period. Issue closure announcement requires 90% subscription and registrar certificate.
*   **Issue Opening (Regulation 85):** A rights issue may be opened within such period as specified by the Board (substituted w.e.f. 2025).
*   **Minimum Subscription (Regulation 86):** At least 90% of the offer. Not applicable (w.e.f. 2020) if the issue's object is not financing capital expenditure and promoters/promoter group subscribe fully without renouncing (except within group or to specific investors (w.e.f. 2025)). If not met, refund within four days (w.e.f. 2022).
*   **Subscription Period (Regulation 87):** Open for a period specified by the Board (substituted w.e.f. 2025). No withdrawal after issue closing date (w.e.f. 2019).
*   **Payment Options (Regulation 88):** Part payment (at least 25% of issue price) with balance in calls, or full payment.
*   **Allotment Procedure (Regulation 90):** Allotment is made first to eligible shareholders and renouncees, then to shareholders applying for additional shares, then to renouncees applying for additional shares, and finally to specific investors (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) if an under-subscribed portion remains. The basis is finalized by designated stock exchange employees and registrars (lead manager(s) omitted w.e.f. 08.04.2025).
*   **Allotment, Refund, and Interest (Regulation 91):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) ensures allotment/refund/unblocking electronically within the Board-specified period. If not completed, the issuer pays 15% per annum interest.
*   **Post-Issue Advertisements (Regulation 92):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) releases an advertisement within ten days of completion, detailing subscription, allotment basis, refunds, credit of securities, and listing application date, published in specified newspapers and on stock exchange websites.
*   **Post-Issue Responsibilities (Regulation 93):** The designated stock exchange (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) monitors investor grievance redressal. The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) is responsible for post-issue activities until applicants receive demat credit/refund and listing/trading permission is obtained.
*   **Release of Subscription Money (Regulation 94):** The issuer (w.e.f. 08.04.2025) confirms to bankers for money release or refund. If listing/trading permission fails, the issuer must refund all monies within four days (w.e.f. 2022) of rejection intimation, or pay 15% interest from the fifth day (w.e.f. 2022).
*   **Reporting of Transactions (Regulation 95):** The issuer must report all security transactions by promoters and the promoter group between the filing of the draft letter of offer/letter of offer and issue closure to stock exchange(s) within twenty-four hours (prior to 2025 substitution).
*   **Post-Issue Reports:** The issuer (substituted from "lead manager(s)" w.e.f. 08.04.2025) must submit an initial post-issue report (Part B of Schedule XVII) within three working days of issue closure, and a final post-issue report (Part C of Schedule XVII) within fifteen days of allotment finalization or refund if the issue fails.
*   **Restriction on Further Capital Issues:** An issuer is prohibited from making any further issue of specified securities between the date of filing the draft letter of offer with the stock exchange(s) (substituted from "Board" w.e.f. 08.04.2025) and the listing of offered securities or refund of application monies. Exceptions apply for employee stock option/appreciation right schemes (inserted w.e.f. 08.04.2025) or if full disclosures are made.
*   **Alteration of Rights (Regulation 98):** An issuer cannot alter the terms of specified securities if it adversely affects holders' interests, unless with written consent from holders of not less than three-fourths of that class of securities, or with a special resolution.
*   **Fast Track Rights Issue (Part IX):** The entire Part IX, including Regulation 99 (Eligibility conditions) and Regulation 100 (Issue conditions) for fast track rights issues, was omitted by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, effective 08.04.2025.

**III. Further Public Offer (FPO) - Chapter IV**

*   **Reference Date (Reg 101):** Conditions must be met as of the date of filing the draft offer document with the Board and filing the offer document with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
*   **Ineligibility (Reg 102):** An issuer is ineligible if the issuer, its promoters, promoter group, directors, or selling shareholders are debarred by the Board (unless debarment period concluded), or if any promoter/director is a promoter/director of another debarred company, or if the issuer/promoter/director is a wilful defaulter/fraudulent borrower, or a fugitive economic offender.
*   **Eligibility (Reg 103):** An issuer is eligible if it has not changed its name in the last one year immediately preceding the filing date, OR if it has, at least 50% of its revenue for the preceding full year must be from the new name's activity. If this isn't met, an FPO is still possible via book-building, with an undertaking to allot at least 75% of the net offer to Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs), refunding if this fails.
*   **General Conditions (Reg 104):** Application for in-principle listing approval, agreement with a depository for dematerialization, all existing partly paid-up equity shares are fully paid-up or forfeited, and firm finance arrangements (verifiable) for 75% of stated means of finance for the specific project (capital expenditures only), excluding public issue proceeds or existing internal accruals. Fund Utilization Limits: Amount for general corporate purposes and objects without an identified acquisition/investment target shall not exceed 35% of the amount raised. Within this, the amount for objects without an identified acquisition/investment target shall not exceed 25% of the amount raised. These limits do not apply if the acquisition/investment target is identified and disclosed.
*   **Offer for Sale (Reg 105):** Only fully paid-up equity shares held by selling shareholder(s) for at least one year prior to filing the draft offer document may be offered. Combined holding period for convertible securities and resultant equity shares counts. Exemptions to one-year holding include offer for sale by government companies/SPVs in infrastructure, equity shares from court/tribunal/Central Government approved schemes, and bonus shares from free reserves/share premium (not revaluation/unrealized profits) on securities held for at least one year.
*   **FPO of Convertible Debt Instruments (Reg 106 & 107):** Eligibility: Issuer's equity shares must be listed, and no default in interest/principal payment for public debt instruments for over six months. Requirements: Credit rating, debenture trustee, debenture redemption reserve. If secured: sufficient, unencumbered assets; consent for second/pari passu charge; security cover calculated after reducing prior charges. Redemption as per offer document.
*   **Roll Over of Non-Convertible Portion (Reg 108):** Non-convertible portion of partly convertible debt instruments (> ₹10 crore) may be rolled over if 75% of holders (by value) approve via postal ballot, and an auditor's certificate on cash flow/liquidity is sent. A credit rating is required within one month before redemption due date.
*   **Conversion of Optionally Convertible Debt Instruments (Reg 109):** Cannot convert without positive consent. If convertible portion > ₹10 crore and conversion price not determined, holders must be given an option not to convert (unless upper limit/formula disclosed). If option not exercised, issuer must redeem within one month at not less than face value (unless offer document states otherwise).
*   **Issue of Convertible Debt Instruments for Financing (Reg 110):** Prohibited for financing/loaning to/acquiring shares of promoter group/group companies, unless fully convertible debt with conversion period < eighteen months.
*   **Issue of Warrants (Reg 111):** Warrants in FPO must have tenure <= eighteen months. Exercise price/formula set upfront, >= 25% consideration upfront. Consideration forfeited if option not exercised within three months.
*   **Minimum Promoters’ Contribution (Reg 112, 113, 114):** Not applicable if no identifiable promoter, OR if equity shares frequently traded for >= 3 years, >= 95% investor complaints redressed, and compliant with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 for >= 3 years (board composition non-compliance acceptable if compliant at filing and disclosed). Otherwise, 20% of proposed issue size or 20% of post-issue capital (excluding rights component for composite issues). Contribution satisfied at least one day before issue opening, held in escrow. SR Equity Shares are eligible. Ineligible securities include those acquired for non-cash consideration involving revaluation, bonus issues from revaluation reserves, or pledged (unless for issuer/subsidiary borrowings).
*   **Lock-in Periods for Promoters' Securities (Reg 115-120):** Minimum Promoters' Contribution: 18 months from FPO allotment (reduced from 3 years). Exception: 3 years if majority of issue proceeds (excluding OFS) are for capital expenditure (includes civil work, fixed assets, land, building, plant/machinery, and repayment of existing loans for such capital expenditure w.e.f. 08.03.2025). Promoters' Holding in Excess of Minimum Contribution: 6 months (reduced from 1 year). Exception: 1 year if majority proceeds for capital expenditure. SR Equity Shares: Locked-in until conversion. Lock-in does not apply to securities lent for green shoe option. Locked-in securities can be pledged as collateral for specific loans, with the lock-in continuing for the transferee upon invocation. Transferable to another promoter/group member/new promoter/controlling person, but lock-in continues.
*   **Appointment of Lead Managers, Other Intermediaries, and Compliance Officer (Reg 121):** Issuer appoints one or more SEBI-registered merchant bankers as lead manager(s) (at least one non-associate), other SEBI-registered intermediaries, a SEBI-registered registrar, and a qualified company secretary as compliance officer.
*   **Disclosures in and Filing of Offer Documents (Reg 122-125):** Draft and final offer documents must contain material, true, and adequate disclosures. Lead manager(s) must exercise due diligence. Issuer files three copies of the draft offer document with the Board through lead manager(s) (with fees and certificates), and with stock exchanges. The Board may specify changes or issue observations within thirty days. Draft offer document must be made public for comments for at least twenty-one days.
*   **Pricing (Reg 126-128):** Disclosures about face value and price band/issue price must be in identical font size. Issuer determines price in consultation with lead manager(s) or via book-building. Cap on price band <= 120% of floor price and >= 105% of floor price. Floor price/final price cannot be less than face value. Floor price/price band announced at least two working days before bid opening. Differential Pricing: Allowed, up to a 10% discount for retail individual investors, retail individual shareholders, or employees (excluding anchor investors).
*   **Issuance Conditions and Procedure (Reg 129-136):** Allocation in Net Offer: Book Building (Reg 103(1)): Not less than 35% to RII, not less than 15% to NII, not more than 50% to QIB (5% of QIB to MFs). Book Building (Reg 103(2)): Not more than 10% to RII, not more than 15% to NII, not less than 75% to QIB (5% of QIB to MFs). Up to 60% of QIB portion can go to anchor investors. NII Sub-categories (w.e.f. 2022): 1/3 of NII for applications > ₹2 lakh to ₹10 lakh; 2/3 for applications > ₹10 lakh. Reservations are permitted for employees (<= 5% of post-issue capital) and shareholders (<= 10% of issue size). Abridged prospectus and ASBA are mandatory. Underwriting: For non-book building FPOs, if desired, agreement before filing prospectus. For book-built public issues, issue must be underwritten by lead manager(s) and syndicate member(s) (except for >= 75% net offer to QIBs).
*   **Monitoring Agency (Reg 137):** If issue size (excluding OFS) exceeds ₹100 crore, issuer must appoint a SEBI-registered credit rating agency to monitor use of proceeds (not for banks, PFIs, insurance companies). Agency submits quarterly reports to issuer, which are then publicly disseminated within forty-five days.
*   **Public Communications and Advertisements (Reg 138, 139):** All public communication must comply with Schedule IX. Pre-issue and price band advertisements must be made after filing RHP/prospectus with RoC, in specified newspapers. No advertisements implying full or oversubscription during the subscription period.
*   **Opening of the Issue (Reg 140):** A public issue may open within twelve months from Board observations. Must open at least three working days after filing RHP/prospectus with RoC.
*   **Minimum Subscription (Reg 141):** Must be at least ninety percent of the offer (excluding OFS). If not met, all application monies refunded forthwith, no later than four days from issue closure.
*   **Period of Subscription (Reg 142):** FPO must be open for at least three working days and not more than ten working days. Price band revision requires extending bidding by a minimum of three working days.
*   **Application and Minimum Application Value (Reg 143):** Maximum application cannot exceed total offered to public in net offer. Minimum application size (number of securities) corresponding to a value between ₹10,000 and ₹15,000. Minimum sum payable on application per specified security is at least twenty-five percent of the issue price (full price for OFS).
*   **Allotment and Post-Issue (Reg 144-151):** Outstanding amount called within twelve months of allotment. Allotment not made if less than one thousand prospective allottees. Allotment (except RII, NII, anchor) on a proportionate basis. RII receive at least minimum bid lot, then proportionately. NII receive at least minimum application size, then proportionately. Allotment/refund/unblock within Board-specified period, with 15% p.a. interest for delays. Lead manager(s) release post-issue advertisements and remain responsible until issue completion. If listing/trading permission denied, issuer must refund all monies within four days (substituted from "seven days" w.e.f. 14.01.2022) of intimation, or pay 15% p.a. interest. Issuer ensures all transactions by promoters/promoter group (between filing draft/offer doc and issue closure) are reported to stock exchange(s) within twenty-four hours. Lead manager(s) submit final post-issue report and due diligence certificate within seven days.
*   **Price Stabilisation through Green Shoe Option (Reg 153):** Issuer may implement a green shoe option to stabilize post-listing price (max 15% over-allotment) for up to thirty days. Requires shareholder authorization, a stabilising agent, and agreements to borrow securities.
*   **Eligibility Conditions for Fast Track Further Public Offer (Reg 155):** Certain sub-regulations of Reg 123 do not apply if the issuer meets conditions including: equity shares listed for >= 3 years, entire promoter group shareholding dematerialised, average market capitalization of public shareholding >= ₹1000 crore, high trading turnover, compliance with listing regulations for >= 3 years, >= 95% investor complaints redressed, no pending show-cause notices (excluding penalty proceedings) from the Board, disclosure of compliance with SEBI settlement orders, no trading suspension as disciplinary measure in last 3 years, no conflict of interest with lead manager(s), and restated financials for audit qualifications or appropriate disclosure.
*   **Post-listing Exit Opportunity for Dissenting Shareholders (Reg 157):** In FPOs (including fast track), promoters or controlling shareholders must provide an exit offer to dissenting shareholders if there's a change in objects or variation in contract terms related to objects in the offer document, as per Companies Act, 2013. Not applicable if no identifiable promoters or controlling shareholders.

**IV. Preferential Issue (Chapter V)**

*   **General Exemptions (Reg 158):** Chapter V provisions generally do not apply to preferential issues made pursuant to conversion of loans/options (Companies Act, 2013), court/tribunal/Central Government approved schemes (though pricing provisions may apply), Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP), rehabilitation schemes (BIFR), resolution plans (IBC Section 31) (except lock-in), equity shares allotted to certain financial institutions (except pricing/lock-in), or debt conversion as part of RBI debt restructuring (subject to specific conditions).
*   **Issuers Ineligible (Reg 159):** Cannot make a preferential issue to any person who sold issuer's equity shares in the last 90 trading days (previously six months) preceding the relevant date (unless Board relaxation). Promoters/promoter group are ineligible if they sold/transferred shares in the last 90 trading days (unless inter-se transfer or pledge invocation by specific entities). Promoters/promoter group who previously subscribed to warrants but failed to exercise them are ineligible for one year. Ineligible if any promoter/director is a fugitive economic offender. Ineligible if the issuer has any outstanding dues to the Board, stock exchanges, or depositories (inserted w.e.f. 14.01.2022), unless these dues are subject to a pending appeal or proceeding.
*   **Conditions (Reg 160):** A listed issuer must ensure allotted equity shares are fully paid, a special resolution is passed, proposed allottees hold dematerialised shares and have PANs (unless exempt) before applying for in-principle approval, and the issuer complies with continuous listing conditions. The in-principle approval application must be made on the same day the general meeting notice is sent.
*   **Relevant Date (Reg 161):** For equity shares, it's 30 days prior to the shareholder meeting (except for stressed assets under RBI/NCLT, where it's the approval date). For convertible securities, it's either the equity share date or 30 days prior to entitlement to apply for equity shares.
*   **Tenure of Convertible Securities (Reg 162):** Cannot exceed 18 months from allotment. Equity shares upon conversion must be allotted within 15 days of exercise.
*   **Monitoring Agency (Reg 162A):** For issues exceeding ₹100 crore (excluding banks, public financial institutions, insurance companies), a SEBI-registered credit rating agency monitors proceeds. Quarterly reports are submitted to the issuer, uploaded on its website, and submitted to stock exchanges within 45 days from quarter-end, with board/management comments.
*   **Disclosures to Shareholders (Reg 163):** Disclosures in the explanatory statement for the special resolution include: objects of issue, maximum securities, promoter/director/KMP/senior management intent to subscribe, shareholding pattern (before/after), issue timeframe, identity of ultimate beneficial owners, percentage of post-issue capital for allottees, change in control, and undertakings for price re-computation and lock-in if not paid. Disclosures for wilful defaulters/fraudulent borrowers (Schedule VI) are also required. Amendments (2022 & 2023) included "senior management," replaced "statutory auditors" with "practicing company secretary" for compliance certificates, stipulated non-cash consideration as a share swap based on an independent registered valuer's report, and required the special resolution to specify the relevant date for pricing equity shares from convertible securities.
*   **Pricing of Preferential Issues (Reg 164-166A):**
    *   **Frequently Traded Shares (Reg 164):** For shares listed ≥ 90 trading days, price not less than the higher of 90-day VWAP or 10-day VWAP preceding the relevant date. For shares listed < 90 trading days, price not less than the higher of IPO price/scheme value, average VWAP during listing, or 10-day VWAP. Recomputation required after 90 trading days. For Qualified Institutional Buyers (max 5), price not less than 10-day VWAP.
    *   **Stressed Assets (Reg 164A, w.e.f. 22.06.2020):** Price not less than 10-day VWAP. Allotment criteria include 90-day default on loans/debt, Inter-creditor agreement, or credit rating downgraded to "D." Issue to non-promoter/group, with prohibited allottees. Requires public category votes in favor to exceed votes against. Proceeds not for repayment of promoter/group loans. Monitoring by SEBI-registered credit rating agency and Audit Committee. 3-year lock-in.
    *   **Optional Pricing (Reg 164B, w.e.f. 01.07.2020 to 31.12.2020):** For frequently traded shares, price not less than the higher of 12-week or 2-week average of weekly high/low VWAP, with a 3-year lock-in.
    *   **Infrequently Traded Shares (Reg 165):** Issuer determines price using valuation parameters, with a compliance certificate from an independent registered valuer.
    *   **Adjustments in Pricing (Reg 166):** Prices are adjusted for corporate actions like bonus issues, rights issues, stock splits, etc.
    *   **Other Conditions for Pricing (Reg 166A, w.e.f. 14.01.2022):** For change in control or >5% post-issue capital, an independent registered valuer's report is required, and the floor price is the higher of Reg 164 floor, valuer's price, or AOA price. Change in control also requires a reasoned recommendation from a committee of independent directors.
*   **Lock-in and Restrictions on Transferability (Reg 167, 167A, 168):** Promoters/Promoter Group: Specified securities/equity from warrants locked-in for 18 months. Not more than 20% of total capital locked-in for 18 months; excess for 6 months. Unlisted convertible securities/warrants for 1 year. Others: Specified securities/equity from warrants locked-in for 6 months. Unlisted convertible securities/warrants for 1 year. Lock-in reduced by prior lock-in period. Stressed Assets: 1 year lock-in (exception for achieving 10% public shareholding). Pre-preferential Allotment Shareholding: Locked-in for 90 trading days. Promoters can pledge locked-in securities (excluding SR equity) as collateral for loans to the issuer/subsidiary from specific financial institutions. Locked-in securities can be transferred among promoters/group/new promoter, but lock-in continues.
*   **Payment of Consideration (Reg 169):** Full consideration at allotment (except non-cash/stressed assets). Warrants: 25% at allotment, 75% on exercise (forfeited if not exercised). Cash from allottee's bank account, certified by statutory auditor.
*   **Allotment (Reg 170):** Within 15 days of special resolution (exceptions for regulatory approvals/takeover/stressed assets). Fresh resolution if delayed. All allotments must be in dematerialised form.

**V. Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP) - Chapter VI**

*   **Definitions (Reg 171):** "Eligible securities" include equity, non-convertible debt with warrants, convertible securities (excluding warrants). "Relevant date" is board/committee decision to open issue or entitlement date for equity.
*   **Eligibility (Reg 172):** Special resolution (exceptions for minimum public shareholding), equity listed for ≥1 year (exceptions for transferee companies/minimum public shareholding), no fugitive promoters/directors. Allotment within 365 days. Subsequent QIPs require a 2-week gap.
*   **Offer for Sale by Promoters (Reg 173):** For minimum public shareholding. Promoters restricted from buying/selling issuer shares 12 weeks before/after issue (exceptions).
*   **Monitoring Agency (Reg 173A, w.e.f. 14.01.2022):** Same as Reg 162A for issues >₹100 crore (excluding OFS, banks, PFIs, insurance).
*   **Lead Managers (Reg 174):** SEBI-registered merchant bankers. At least one non-associate (if associate, limited to marketing). Due diligence certificate and preliminary placement document required.
*   **Placement Document (Reg 175):** Contains material information, Schedule VII disclosures (e.g., wilful defaulters), serially numbered, circulated to select investors, hosted on stock exchange/issuer websites with disclaimer.
*   **Pricing (Reg 176):** Not less than average of 2-week weekly high/low closing prices. Up to 5% discount with shareholder approval (unless promoter OFS). Subject to adjustments for corporate actions.
*   **Tenure of Convertible Securities (Reg 177):** Max 60 months.
*   **Transferability (Reg 178):** Allotted securities cannot be sold for 1 year (except on a recognized stock exchange).
*   **Application and Allotment (Reg 179):** No withdrawal/downward revision of bids. Minimum 10% to mutual funds. No allotment to promoter/related QIB (unless lender not holding shares).
*   **Minimum Allottees (Reg 180):** At least 2 for issues ≤₹250 crore, 5 for >₹250 crore. No single allottee >50%. Group/control definitions apply.

**VI. Initial Public Offer of Indian Depository Receipts (IDRs) - Chapter VII**

*   **Applicability (Reg 181), Reference Date (Reg 182).**
*   **Eligibility (Reg 183):** Issuer listed in home country for ≥3 years, no regulatory prohibition, compliance track record, no fugitive promoters/directors. Issue size ≥₹50 crore, one IDR denomination, underlying shares listed/pari passu. Issuer ensures in-principle listing, depository agreement, 75% finance.
*   **Funding and Use of Proceeds (Reg 184):** Stated means of finance must be made. Max 25% for general corporate purposes.
*   **Intermediaries (Reg 185):** Lead manager(s) (at least one non-associate), registrar, overseas custodian bank, domestic depository, compliance officer, collection arrangements.
*   **Offer Documents (Reg 186):** True/correct/adequate disclosures (Part A Schedule VIII). Lead manager(s) due diligence. Filing draft with SEBI, then offer document with RoC, with certificates.
*   **Public Availability (Reg 187):** Draft public for 21 days for comments, public announcement in newspapers, hosted on websites.
*   **Pricing (Reg 188):** Determined in consultation with lead manager(s) or through book-building. Price band cap 120% of floor, not less than face value. Floor price/band announced 2 working days before issue opening.
*   **Differential Pricing (Reg 189):** Retail individual investors/employees may get up to 10% discount.
*   **Issuance Conditions and Procedure (Reg 190):** Minimum application ₹20,000. Allocation: ≥50% to QIBs (proportionate), rest to non-institutional/retail (discretion). ≥30% to retail (spillover allowed). Max application not exceeding total offered.
*   **Other Provisions (Reg 191-197):** Abridged prospectus (Part B Schedule VIII), ASBA facility, availability of issue material, no incentives. Reg 197 (security deposit) omitted.
*   **Underwriting (Reg 198):** Required for non-book-built issues. Lead manager(s) and syndicate members underwrite book-built issues, responsible for minimum subscription.
*   **Public Communications (Reg 199):** Must comply with Schedule IX.
*   **Issue-related Advertisements (Reg 200):** Opening/closing ads (Schedule X). No oversubscription claims during subscription.
*   **Opening of the Issue (Reg 201):** Within 12 months of SEBI observations, at least 3 working days after RoC filing.
*   **Minimum Subscription (Reg 202):** At least 90% of offer. If not met, full refund within 4 days, with 15% p.a. interest for delay. Lead manager(s) report underwriter failures.
*   **Subscription Period (Reg 203):** 3 to 10 working days. Extensions for price band revision (min 3 days) or unforeseen circumstances (min 1 day).
*   **Allotment Procedure (Reg 204):** No allotment exceeding offer (except rounding). Proportionate for non-retail. Retail max ₹2 lakh, minimum bid lot. Basis of allotment finalized fairly.
*   **Allotment, Refund, and Interest (Reg 205):** Simultaneous electronic allotment/refund/unblocking. 15% p.a. interest for delays.
*   **Post-Issue Advertisements (Reg 206):** Within 10 days of activity completion, detailing subscription, allotment, refunds, listing.
*   **Post-Issue Responsibilities of Lead Manager(s) (Reg 207):** Ongoing responsibility until issue completion, investor grievance redressal, reporting omissions, ensuring devolvement notice.
*   **Release of Subscription Money (Reg 208):** After listing/trading approvals. Refund if listing fails, with 15% p.a. interest for delay.
*   **Reporting of Transactions (Reg 209):** Promoter/group transactions (draft to closure) and pre-IPO placements reported to stock exchanges within 24 hours.
*   **Post-Issue Reports (Reg 210):** Final report (Part A Schedule XVII) with due diligence certificate (Form F Schedule V) within 7 days of allotment finalization or refund.
*   **Fungibility (Reg 211):** IDRs are fungible into underlying equity shares as specified by SEBI/RBI.

**VII. Rights Issue of Indian Depository Receipts (IDRs) - Chapter VIII**

*   **Applicability (Reg 212):** Chapter VII applies, with specific exceptions.
*   **Entities Not Eligible (Reg 213):** Issuer breaching material obligations, debarred, or having fugitive promoters/directors.
*   **General Conditions (Reg 214):** Issuer applies for listing new IDRs on all listed stock exchanges.
*   **Renunciation (Reg 215):** IDR holders can renounce rights unless home jurisdiction laws prohibit.
*   **Depository (Reg 216):** Domestic depository facilitates IDR holders' entitlements.
*   **Record Date (Reg 217):** Announced per SEBI (LODR) Regulations. Withdrawal after record date restricts future rights issues for 12 months.
*   **Disclosures (Reg 218):** Home country disclosures plus an addendum (Part C Schedule VIII) for India.
*   **Appointment of Lead Managers and Compliance Officer (Reg 219):** Lead manager(s) and a company secretary as compliance officer (functioning in India by 08.03.2025).
*   **Filing of Draft Offer Document and Addendum (Reg 220):** Confidential draft (home country) and addendum (Part C Schedule VIII) filed with SEBI, with fees. Board may issue observations within 30 days. Undertaking from overseas custodian/domestic depository.
*   **Pricing (Reg 221):** Issue price and ratio decided per home country regulations, simultaneously with record date.
*   **Availability of Issue Material (Reg 222):** Abridged letter of offer (Part B Schedule IX) despatched at least 3 days before opening. Plain paper applications allowed (cannot renounce rights).
*   **Issue-related Advertisement (Reg 223):** At least 3 days before opening in specified newspapers.
*   **Subscription Period and Allotment (Reg 224):** Open for period applicable under home country laws, but not less than 10 days. Allotment letters sent simultaneously.
*   **Utilisation of Funds (Reg 225):** Only after allotment completion.
*   **Fast Track Issue (Reg 226):** Exemptions from certain regulations if issuer meets conditions like 3 years of compliance, home country review, no pending show-cause notices, and 95% grievance redressal.

**VIII. Initial Public Offer by Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) - Chapter IX**

*   **Reference Date (Reg 227):** Issuer must satisfy conditions on filing draft offer document with SME exchange and filing offer document with RoC.
*   **Ineligibility Criteria (Reg 228):** Issuer, promoters, promoter group, directors, or selling shareholders debarred by SEBI. Promoters/directors of another debarred company. Issuer/promoters/directors are wilful defaulters or fraudulent borrowers. Promoters/directors are fugitive economic offenders. Outstanding convertible securities or rights to receive equity shares (as of 01.01.2020), with exceptions for ESOPs and fully paid-up convertible securities converting by RHP/prospectus filing.
*   **Eligibility Requirements (Section 229):** Post-issue paid-up capital must be ≤ ₹10 crore. Issuers with capital > ₹10 crore and ≤ ₹25 crore may also issue specified securities. Issuer must meet SME Exchange track record/eligibility conditions. Partnership/LLP track record considered only if financial statements conform to Companies Act, 2013 (Schedule III), include adequate disclosures, and are certified by ICAI peer-reviewed auditors. Proprietorships, partnerships, or LLPs converting to a company can make an IPO only if the company has existed for at least one full financial year before filing the draft offer document. If promoters change or new promoters acquire >50% shareholding, the draft offer document can be filed only after one year from the change date. Minimum operating profits of ₹1 crore from operations for at least two out of the three previous financial years.
*   **General Conditions (Section 230):** Issuer must apply to one or more SME exchanges for listing, designate one, and agree with a depository for dematerialization. All existing partly paid-up equity shares must be fully paid-up or forfeited; promoter-held specified securities must be dematerialized. Firm arrangements for 75% of project finance (excluding IPO proceeds/internal accruals) must be made. Offer for sale by selling shareholders ≤ 20% of total issue size and ≤ 50% of their pre-issue shareholding (fully diluted). Issue proceeds cannot repay loans from promoter/promoter group/related parties. General Corporate Purposes (GCP) amount ≤ 15% of amount raised or ₹10 crore, whichever is less (previously 25%). Combined GCP and unidentified acquisition/investment objects ≤ 35% of amount raised. Unidentified acquisition/investment objects ≤ 25% of amount raised.
*   **Issue of Convertible Debt Instruments (CDIs) and Warrants (Part II):** CDIs can make IPO without prior equity issue/listing, but are ineligible if defaulted on public debt interest/principal for >6 months. Require credit rating, debenture trustee, debenture redemption reserve, and sufficient assets for secured CDIs. Warrants can be issued with tenure ≤ 18 months, requiring ≥ 25% upfront payment, with forfeiture for non-exercise.
*   **Promoters’ Contribution (Part III):** Promoters must hold ≥ 20% of post-issue capital. Shortfalls can be met by specific entities (e.g., AIFs, FVCIs, banks, PFIs) up to 10% of post-issue capital. Not applicable if no identifiable promoter. Contribution can be in equity shares or convertible securities. The amount for promoters' contribution must be kept in an escrow account. Securities acquired for non-cash consideration involving revaluation, bonus issues from revaluation reserves, or those acquired by promoters/specified entities in the preceding one year at a price lower than the IPO price are ineligible (with exceptions). Pledged securities are also ineligible.
*   **Lock-in of Specified Securities (Regulations 238, 239):** Promoters' minimum contribution is locked-in for 3 years from the later of commercial production commencement or IPO allotment date. Promoters' excess holding is 50% locked-in for 2 years, remaining 50% for 1 year from IPO allotment date. Pre-issue capital (non-promoters) is locked-in for 1 year from IPO allotment date, with exceptions for employee stock options/schemes and shares held by VCF/AIF/FVCI. Locked-in securities are non-transferable but can be pledged as collateral for specific loans, with the lock-in continuing. They can be transferred within the promoter group or to other persons holding locked-in securities, but the lock-in continues.
*   **Appointment of Lead Managers, Other Intermediaries, and Compliance Officer:** Issuer appoints one or more SEBI-registered merchant bankers as lead manager(s) (at least one non-associate), other SEBI-registered intermediaries, a SEBI-registered registrar, and a qualified company secretary (w.e.f. 08.03.2025) as compliance officer.
*   **Disclosures in and Filing of Offer Documents:** Material, true, and adequate disclosures are required. Lead manager(s) must exercise due diligence. Issuer files offer document with Board via lead manager(s) immediately after filing with RoC. Board does not issue observations. Draft offer document public for comments for ≥ 21 days.
*   **Pricing and Price Band:** Issuer determines price/coupon rate/conversion price in consultation with lead manager(s) or via book building. Cap on price band ≤ 120% of floor price. Floor price/final price ≥ face value. Floor price/price band announced ≥ 2 working days before issue opening. Differential pricing is permitted for individual investors or retail individual shareholders/employees (up to 10% discount).
*   **Allocation in Issues:** Minimum offer to public must comply with Securities Contracts (Regulations) Rules, 1957. Net offer category: Not less than 35% to individual investors (minimum application size); not less than 15% to non-institutional investors; not more than 50% to QIBs (5% of this to mutual funds). Amendments (effective 08.03.2025) split non-institutional investors into two sub-categories.
*   **Reservation on a Competitive Basis (Regulation 254):** Permitted for employees (≤ 5% of post-issue capital, max allotment ₹2 lakhs per employee, up to ₹5 lakhs if under-subscribed) and shareholders (≤ 10% of issue size). Prohibited for lead manager(s), registrar, syndicate member(s), their promoters, directors, employees, group/associate companies.
*   **Other Issue-Related Regulations:** Abridged prospectus (Reg 255), ASBA (Reg 256), 100% underwriting required (Reg 260), compulsory market making for ≥ 3 years (Reg 261), monitoring agency if issue size > ₹50 crore (Reg 262), public communications (Reg 263), issue advertisements (Reg 264), issue opening ≥ 3 working days after RoC filing (Reg 265), subscription period 3-10 working days (Reg 266), minimum application size two lots and > ₹2 lakhs (Reg 267).
*   **Allotment Procedure and Basis of Allotment (Reg 268):** Allotment not made if < 200 allottees (changed from 50 w.e.f. 08.03.2025). Allotment to non-individual investors/anchor investors on proportionate basis. Value of securities allotted to any person (except employees under reservation) ≤ ₹2 lakhs.
*   **Allotment, Refund, and Payment of Interest (Reg 269):** Allotment/refund/unblocking within Board-specified time. If not completed, issuer pays 15% p.a. interest. Refund periods changed from 7/8 days to 4 days (w.e.f. 14.01.2022).
*   **Post-Issue Advertisements (Reg 270):** Lead manager(s) ensure advertisement within 10 days of completion of activities.
*   **Post-Issue Responsibilities of the Lead Manager(s) (Reg 271):** Responsibility continues until issue process completion.
*   **Release of Subscription Money (Reg 272):** Lead manager(s) confirm formalities completed to bankers. If listing/trading permission fails, issuer refunds entire monies within 4 days of intimation, or pays 15% p.a. interest.
*   **Post-Issue Reports:** Lead managers submit final post-issue report and due diligence certificate within 7 days.
*   **Reporting of Transactions:** Issuer reports all promoter/promoter group securities transactions and proposed pre-IPO placements to stock exchange(s) within 24 hours.
*   **Migration of Securities:** SME-listed issuers may migrate existing listed securities to SME exchange or to Main Board under specific conditions (e.g., special resolution, meeting eligibility criteria).
*   **Restriction on Further Capital Issues:** Generally prohibited between draft offer document filing and listing/refund, with exceptions.
*   **Price Stabilisation through Green Shoe Option:** Permitted to stabilize post-listing prices, similar to IPOs.
*   **Alteration of Rights (Section 280.1):** Issuer cannot alter specified securities terms adversely affecting holders' interests without written consent from ≥ 3/4ths of that class or special resolution sanction.
*   **SME Exchange Migration and Further Issues (Sections 280.2, 281):** If SME-listed issuer's post-issue paid-up capital exceeds ₹25 crore due to further issue, it *shall* migrate to Main Board if it meets Main Board eligibility. Alternatively, it *may* undertake further capital issuance without migrating from SME exchange, provided it complies with SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, applicable to Main Board companies.
*   **Post-listing Exit Opportunity for Dissenting Shareholders (Section 281A):** Promoters/controlling shareholders must provide an exit offer to dissenting shareholders if objects change or contract terms related to objects vary.

**IX. Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) - Chapter X**

*   **Applicability (Sections 282, 283):** For issuers seeking listing via IPO or trading without public offer. Other SEBI regulations apply mutatis mutandis, except for regulation 7(2) (GCP restrictions) and regulation 6(1) & (2) (eligibility requirements). Access is only for institutional and non-institutional investors. Issuers with SR equity shares can make an IPO of *only ordinary shares* for IGP listing, subject to compliance with this chapter and SR equity share provisions (regulation 6(3)).
*   **Eligibility:** Issuer must be technology-intensive (technology, IT, IP, data analytics, bio-technology, or nano-technology) providing products/services/platforms with substantial value addition. Additionally, 25% of pre-issue capital must have been held for ≥ 1 year by Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs), Innovators Growth Platform Investors, or specific regulated entities.
*   **IGP Investors:** Must not be from FATF-identified deficient countries. Eligible individuals have ≥₹50 lakh annual gross income and ≥₹5 crore liquid net worth; corporate bodies/family trusts have ≥₹25 crore net worth. Accreditation is through stock exchanges or depositories. Pre-issue capital held by promoters, even if IGP Investors, is not considered for the 25% pre-issue capital eligibility. "Innovators Growth Platform Investors" replaced "Accredited Investors" (w.e.f. 05.05.2021).
*   **Listing Without a Public Issue (Regulation 284):** Issuer files a confidential draft information document with the Board and obtains in-principle approval from stock exchanges. Securities must be listed within 30 days of Board observations. Regulations on allotment, issue opening/closing, advertisements, underwriting, pricing, and minimum public offer are not applicable. Minimum public shareholding provisions are not applicable.
*   **Listing Pursuant to an Initial Public Offer (IPO) (Regulation 285 onwards):** Issuer files draft offer document with the Board. Must comply with minimum public shareholding rules; minimum offer size is ₹10 crore (w.e.f. 05.04.2019). Minimum application size is ₹2 lakh and in multiples thereof (w.e.f. 05.04.2019). At least 50 allottees (w.e.f. 05.04.2019). Up to 60% of the issue size can be allocated discretionarily to eligible investors (similar to anchor investors) prior to issue opening, at a price not lower than other applicants, with a minimum application of ₹50 lakh (w.e.f. 05.05.2021).
*   **Lock-in (Regulation 288):** Entire pre-issue capital locked-in for 6 months from allotment (public issue) or listing (without public issue). Exceptions for employee schemes and shares held by VCF/AIF/FVCI (locked-in for at least one year from purchase date). Equity shares held by non-promoters must be held for at least one year prior to listing without a public issue. Locked-in promoter shares may be pledged as collateral under specific conditions. All discretionary allotted securities are locked-in as per anchor investor rules. SR equity shares are locked-in until conversion or for the specified period, whichever is later.
*   **Exit and Delisting:** An issuer listed without a public issue may exit with a special resolution (90% total votes, majority non-promoter votes) and stock exchange approval. Stock exchanges can delist for non-compliance. Promoters/directors of delisted entities are prohibited from listing another issuer on IGP for five years.
*   **Migration to Main Board (Regulation 292):** Eligibility requires minimum one year on IGP, at least 200 shareholders, and no debarment/wilful defaulter/fugitive economic offender for company/promoters/directors. Financial conditions (Net Tangible Assets ≥₹3 crore, average operating profit ≥₹15 crore, net worth ≥₹1 crore, all consolidated for preceding three years) or 50% of capital held by QIBs. Promoters must hold ≥20% of total capital (shortfall up to 10% can be met by specified entities). Promoters’ contribution locked-in for three years from main board trading approval; excess holding for one year. IGP lock-in period is deducted.

**X. Social Stock Exchange (SSE) - Chapter X-A (inserted 2022)**

*   **Definitions:** For Profit Social Enterprise (FPSE), Not for Profit Organization (NPO), Social Impact Assessor/Firm, Social Enterprise, SSE.
*   **Applicability:** For NPOs seeking registration/fund-raising and FPSEs seeking identification as Social Enterprises.
*   **Access:** Accessible to institutional, non-institutional, and retail investors. Each SSE must constitute a Governing Council.
*   **Eligibility for Social Enterprise Identification (292E):** Must establish primacy of social intent and be involved in at least one of several specified activities (e.g., eradicating hunger, promoting healthcare, education, gender equality, environmental sustainability). Must target underserved/less privileged populations/regions. At least 67% of preceding 3-year average revenues, expenditure, or customer base must be from eligible activities to the target population. Ineligible: Corporate foundations, political/religious organizations, professional/trade associations, and infrastructure/housing companies (except affordable housing).
*   **Fundraising by Social Enterprises (292G):** NPOs may raise funds through Zero Coupon Zero Principal Instruments (ZCZP) to eligible investors, donations via Mutual Fund schemes, or other Board-specified means. FPSEs may raise funds through equity shares (on main board, SME, or IGP, or to AIFs), debt securities, or other Board-specified means. Their securities will be listed with an identifier.
*   **Ineligibility for Raising Funds (292H):** A Social Enterprise is ineligible if it, its promoters, directors, or trustees are debarred from the securities market, are wilful defaulters, fraudulent borrowers, or fugitive economic offenders (unless past debarment period concluded).
*   **Zero Coupon Zero Principal Instruments (ZCZP):** Issued only by NPOs registered on an SSE, for a specific tenure, without coupon or principal, for specific eligible projects/activities. Procedures and fund-raising document contents are "as specified by the Board" (w.e.f. 21.12.2023). NPOs may also make private issuance of ZCZP to Social Impact Funds. Listing terminates when the project object is achieved or tenure expires. SSEs must specify additional norms for issue procedures.

**XI. Bonus Issues (Chapter XI)**

*   **Eligibility:** Listed issuers can issue bonus shares if their articles authorize it (or a general body resolution is passed), all prior securities are approved for listing, no default on fixed deposits/debt/employee statutory dues, partly paid shares are fully paid-up, and no promoters/directors are fugitive economic offenders.
*   **Restrictions (Regulation 294):** Equity shares must be reserved for holders of outstanding compulsorily convertible debt instruments. Must be made only from free reserves, securities premium account, or capital redemption reserve (from genuine profits/cash premium), not revaluation reserves. Cannot be issued in lieu of dividends. Bonus on SR equity shares must carry the same voting rights ratio as ordinary shares and convert along with existing SR shares. Allotment must be in dematerialized form.
*   **Completion (Regulation 295):** If only board approval is needed, implemented within 15 days. If shareholder approval is needed, implemented within two months from the board meeting (subject to approval). Cannot be withdrawn once announced.

**XII. General Regulatory Powers and Compliance**

*   **Power to Relax Strict Enforcement (Regulatory Sandbox - Regulation 295A):** The Board may exempt persons for up to 12 months to test new products/services in a "regulatory sandbox" environment.
*   **Directions by the Board (Regulation 296):** The Board can issue directions (e.g., prohibiting market access, directing divestment) in the interest of investors or the securities market, after providing an opportunity to be heard.
*   **Liability for Contravention (Regulation 297):** Contravention leads to actions by stock exchanges (fines, trading suspension, freezing holdings).
*   **Power to Remove Difficulty (Regulation 299):** The Board may issue guidance notes or circulars to address difficulties.
*   **Power to Relax Strict Enforcement (General - Regulation 300):** The Board may relax requirements (procedural, irrelevant disclosure, beyond control) for investor/market development, upon application with a ₹1 lakh fee.
*   **Repeal and Savings (Regulation 301):** The SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2009, are rescinded; actions/documents under old regulations are deemed under the new ones.

**XIII. Schedules (Fees, Filing, Due Diligence, Disclosures, etc.)**
The document details various schedules:
*   **Schedule I:** Lead Managers’ Inter-Se Allocation of Responsibilities.
*   **Schedule II:** Agreement between Lead Manager(s) and Issuer.
*   **Schedule III:** Fees payable to the Board for various filings.
*   **Schedule IV:** Filing locations for draft offer documents and letters of offer.
*   **Schedule V:** Formats for Due Diligence Certificates from lead managers and debenture trustees.
*   **Schedule VI:** Comprehensive disclosure requirements for draft offer documents, offer documents, and letters of offer, including general instructions, cover page content, summary, risk factors, capital structure, objects of the issue, financial statements (Ind AS and Indian GAAP), Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), legal and other information, stock market data, investor grievance redressal, offering terms and procedures, issuer undertakings, and issue withdrawal. It also specifies disclosures for FPOs, fast track public issues, rights issues, and abridged prospectuses.
*   **Schedule VII:** Requirements for Placement Documents for QIPs.
*   **Schedule VIII:** Disclosure requirements for IDR Offer Documents, Abridged Prospectuses for IDRs, and Addendums for Rights Issues of IDRs.
*   **Schedule IX:** General principles and content restrictions for Public Communications and Publicity Materials.
*   **Schedule X:** Specific requirements for Issue-related Advertisements, including pre-issue, price band, opening, and closing advertisements, and mandatory sections like "Risks to Investors" and "Basis for Offer Price."
*   **Schedule XI:** Format of the Monitoring Agency Report for utilization of issue proceeds.
*   **Schedule XII:** Mandatory Collection Centres for applications.
*   **Schedule XIII:** Detailed procedures for the Book Building Process, including roles of intermediaries, underwriting, pricing, anchor investor rules, bidding process, and alternative methods for FPOs.
*   **Schedule XIV:** Illustrations of Allotment Procedures for Retail Individual Investors (RIIs) and Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs), including scenarios for oversubscription and lottery.
*   **Schedule XV:** Format of Report for Green Shoe Option.
*   **Schedule XVI & XVI-A:** Nature of Changes in the Offer Document Requiring Filing of Updated Offer Document, specifying thresholds for fresh filings or updated filings with/without fees.
*   **Schedule XVII:** Formats of Post-Issue Reports for public and rights issues.
*   **Schedule XVIII:** Format of Underwriting Devolvement Statement.
*   **Schedule XIX:** Requirements for Listing of Securities on Stock Exchanges.
*   **Schedule XX:** Conditions/Manner of Providing Exit Opportunity to Dissenting Shareholders, detailing eligibility, pricing, and process for such offers.

**XIV. SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (LODR)**
These regulations, notified on September 2, 2015, apply to listed entities with various designated securities.
*   **Definitions (Chapter I):** Key terms include "specified securities," "subsidiary," "control," "Independent Director," "Material Subsidiary," and "Senior Management."
*   **Applicability (Regulation 3):** Applies to listed entities with specified securities, non-convertible debt/preference shares, perpetual debt instruments, IDRs, securitised debt instruments, mutual fund units, or other Board-specified securities.
*   **Principles Governing Disclosures and Obligations (Regulation 4(1)):** Mandates preparation and disclosure of information according to applicable standards, ensuring no misrepresentation, providing adequate and timely information, ensuring disseminations are accurate and accessible, and abiding by all applicable laws.
*   **Corporate Governance Provisions for Specified Securities (Regulation 4(2)):** Protects shareholder rights, ensures timely information, equitable treatment, recognizes stakeholder rights, mandates disclosure and transparency, and outlines responsibilities of the Board of Directors.
*   **Common Obligations of Listed Entities (Chapter III):** Includes appointment of a Compliance Officer and Share Transfer Agent, cooperation with intermediaries, preservation of documents, filing of information, adherence to scheme of arrangement rules, electronic payment preference, grievance redressal mechanism (including SCORES), and payment of fees.
*   **Obligations for Entities with Listed Specified Securities (Chapter IV):** Certain corporate governance provisions do not apply to entities with paid-up equity capital not exceeding ₹10 crore AND net worth not exceeding ₹25 crore, or to entities listed on an SME Exchange.
    *   **Board of Directors (Regulation 17):** Must have an optimum combination of executive and non-executive directors, including at least one woman director, with non-executive directors comprising not less than 50%. Independent directors must constitute at least one-third or half, depending on the chairperson's status. Meetings must occur at least four times a year.
    *   **Committees (Regulations 18-21):** Audit Committee (qualified, independent, 2/3 independent), Nomination and Remuneration Committee (non-executive, 50% independent), Stakeholders Relationship Committee (non-executive chair), and Risk Management Committee (majority board members, for top 100 listed entities).
    *   **Vigil Mechanism (Regulation 22):** Must be formulated for directors and employees to report concerns.
    *   **Related Party Transactions (Regulation 23):** Policy on materiality (material if >10% of annual consolidated turnover). All RPTs require prior audit committee approval, and material RPTs require shareholder approval (related parties abstain).
    *   **Corporate Governance Requirements for Subsidiaries (Regulation 24):** At least one independent director of the listed entity must be on the board of an unlisted material Indian subsidiary.
    *   **Obligations with respect to Independent Directors (Regulation 25):** Limits on directorships and requirement for annual meetings without non-independent directors/management.
